source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. V (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio capituli primi: Fratribus qui sunt per Ægyptum Judæis, etc.
1.title_en: Explanation of the first chapter: To the brethren, the Jews that are throughout Egypt, etc.

paras.t: Fratribus qui sunt per Ægyptum Judæis: qui fratres nostri sunt, scilicet nati ex semine Jacob, sicut et nos, et ejusdem nobiscum sunt legis ac fidei; salutem dicunt fratres qui sunt in Jerosolymis Judæi, et qui in regione Judææ, et pacem bonam, id est spiritualem, internam, imo et temporalem, ordinatam ad pacem spiritualem. Habitabant autem plurimi Judæorum in Ægypto, præsertim ab eo tempore quo Ptolemæus cognomento Soter, qui post Alexandrum Magnum primus in Ægypto regnavit, plurimos Judæorum a Jerosolyma et Judæa secum captivos in Ægyptum deduxit. Cujus successor Ptolemæus Philadelphus, cupiens sibi transferri libros veteris Testamenti, plurima millia Judæorum liberavit a servitute, et remisit Judæorum pontifici: a quo petiit sibi viros doctissimos mitti ad transferendum libros legis Mosaicæ de Hebræo in Græcum. Nihilo minus adhuc multi Judæorum in Ægypto manserunt, et multiplicati sunt ibi valde: quibus missa fuit ista epistola.
paras.en: [[1:1|To the brethren, the Jews that are throughout Egypt|Fratribus qui sunt per Ægyptum Judæis]]: who are our brethren, that is, born of the seed of Jacob, as we also are, and of one law and one faith with us; [[1:1|the brethren, the Jews that are in Jerusalem, and in the land of Judea, send health|salutem dicunt fratres qui sunt in Jerosolymis Judæi, et qui in regione Judææ]] [[1:1|and good peace|et pacem bonam]], that is, spiritual and inward peace, and indeed temporal peace too, ordered to spiritual peace. Now very many of the Jews lived in Egypt, especially from the time when Ptolemy surnamed Soter, who was the first to reign in Egypt after Alexander the Great, carried off very many of the Jews from Jerusalem and Judea with him into Egypt as captives. His successor Ptolemy Philadelphus, wishing to have the books of the Old Testament translated for him, set many thousands of the Jews free from bondage and sent them back to the high priest of the Jews, from whom he asked that most learned men be sent to him to translate the books of the law of Moses from Hebrew into Greek. Nevertheless many of the Jews still remained in Egypt and multiplied there greatly; and to them this letter was sent.

paras.t: Benefaciat vobis Deus, benedicendo vobis in spiritualibus ac temporalibus bonis; et meminerit testamenti sui, id est, promissiones veteris Testamenti in vobis implere dignetur. Sicque per effectum ostendat se memorem pacti seu promissionis, quod iniit et percussit cum patribus nostris in monte Sinai legem dando, imo et ante cum Patriarchis, Abraham, Isaac et Jacob, quibus tam pro ipsorum personis, quam pro posteris eorumdem multa promisit: ut in Genesi per diversa recitatur capitula. Hinc subditur, quod ad Abraham, Isaac et Jacob locutus est, qui sunt de numero servorum suorum fidelium: et sic aliquid hic suppletur. Potest tamen absque supplemento exponi: Meminerit testamenti sui, id est pacti sui, servorum suorum fidelium, id est concernentis servos suos fideles, et eis facti. De hoc pacto legitur in Genesi: Dixit Dominus ad Abraham: Faciam te in gentem magnam, et magnificabo nomen tuum, erisque benedictus; et semini tuo dabo terram hanc. Et alio Genesis loco ait ad Isaac: Tibi et semini tuo dabo universas regiones has, complens juramentum quod spopondi Abraham patri tuo: benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ. Præterea in Genesi locutus est ad Jacob: Terram hanc tibi dabo et semini tuo. Eritque semen tuum sicut pulvis terræ; et benedicentur in te et in semine tuo cunctæ tribus terræ.
paras.en: [[1:2|May God be gracious to you|Benefaciat vobis Deus]], blessing you in goods spiritual and temporal; [[1:2|and remember his covenant|et meminerit testamenti sui]], that is, may he deign to fulfil in you the promises of the Old Testament [*testamentum* means both “covenant” and “testament”]. And so may he show in effect that he is mindful of the pact or promise which he entered into and struck with our fathers on Mount Sinai in giving the law, and indeed before that with the Patriarchs, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, to whom he promised many things, both for their own persons and for their posterity, as is related in various chapters of Genesis. Hence it is added, [[1:2|that he made with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob|quod ad Abraham, Isaac et Jacob locutus est]] [literally, “which he spoke to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob”], who are of the number of [[1:2|his faithful servants|servorum suorum fidelium]]; and so something is supplied here. It can, however, be explained without supplying anything: [[1:2|remember his covenant|Meminerit testamenti sui]], that is, his pact, of [[1:2|his faithful servants|servorum suorum fidelium]], that is, the pact concerning his faithful servants and made with them. Of this pact we read in Genesis: The Lord said to Abraham: [[Gen 12:2|I will make of thee a great nation|Faciam te in gentem magnam]], [[Gen 12:2|and magnify thy name, and thou shalt be blessed|et magnificabo nomen tuum, erisque benedictus]]; and: [[Gen 12:7|To thy seed will I give this land|semini tuo dabo terram hanc]]. And in another place of Genesis he says to Isaac: [[Gen 26:3|to thee and to thy seed I will give all these countries, to fulfil the oath which I swore to Abraham thy father|Tibi et semini tuo dabo universas regiones has, complens juramentum quod spopondi Abraham patri tuo]]: [[Gen 26:4|in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed|benedicentur in semine tuo omnes gentes terræ]]. Again, in Genesis he spoke to Jacob: [[Gen 28:13|The land, wherein thou sleepest, I will give to thee and to thy seed|Terram hanc tibi dabo et semini tuo]] [Denis reads “this land” for “the land wherein thou sleepest”]. [[Gen 28:14|And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth|Eritque semen tuum sicut pulvis terræ]]; and [[Gen 28:14|IN THEE and thy seed, all the tribes of the earth SHALL BE BLESSED|et benedicentur in te et in semine tuo cunctæ tribus terræ]].

paras.t: Et det vobis cor omnibus, id est, cordis illuminationem et devotionem det omnibus vobis, ut colatis eum, per observantiam legis divinæ. Et præsertim colitur Deus cultu interno per fidem, spem, et caritatem; deinde per latriam, cujus actus sunt devotio, oratio, laudatio, sacrificium, juramentum, et votum. Et faciatis ejus voluntatem, id est ea quæ Deo sunt placita, et in primis ejus præcepta, corde magno, id est cum ingenti cordis affectu. Potius enim respicit Deus ex quanto, quam quantum, hoc est, ex quali et quanto affectu cordis quid fiat, quam opus seu datum exterius. Et animo volenti, id est spontaneo, non coacto; atque ex caritate, non ex servili timore: quemadmodum in libro Josue legitur, Servite Domino corde perfecto atque verissimo. Unde et primo Paralipomenon volumine David hortatur: Fili mi, servi Deo corde perfecto et animo voluntario.
paras.en: [[1:3|And give you all a heart|Et det vobis cor omnibus]], that is, may he give all of you enlightenment and devotion of heart, [[1:3|to worship him|ut colatis eum]] by keeping the divine law. And God is worshipped above all by inward worship, through faith, hope and charity; then through latria [the worship owed to God alone], whose acts are devotion, prayer, praise, sacrifice, oath and vow. [[1:3|And to do his will|Et faciatis ejus voluntatem]], that is, the things that are pleasing to God, and first of all his commandments, [[1:3|with a great heart|corde magno]], that is, with great affection of heart. For God looks rather at *from how much* than at *how much* [that is, at the love from which a thing is given rather than at the size of the gift]: that is, at the quality and the degree of the heart’s affection with which a thing is done, more than at the outward work or gift. [[1:3|And a willing mind|Et animo volenti]], that is, spontaneous, not forced; and out of charity, not out of servile fear: as we read in the book of Josue, [[Jos 24:14|serve him with a perfect and most sincere heart|Servite Domino corde perfecto atque verissimo]] [Denis has “serve the Lord”]. Hence David too exhorts in the first volume of Paralipomenon: [[1 Par 28:9|my son|Fili mi]], [[1 Par 28:9|serve him with a perfect heart, and a willing mind|servi Deo corde perfecto et animo voluntario]].

paras.t: Adaperiat cor vestrum, intellectum illustrando, voluntatemque excitando ac inflammando, in lege sua intelligenda ac adimplenda: prout orat Psalmista, Da mihi intellectum, et scrutabor legem tuam, et custodiam illam in toto corde meo; et in præceptis suis, ut ea sincere intelligatis ac impleatis; et faciat pacem pectoris ac temporis: juxta illud Proverbiorum, Quum placuerint Domino viæ hominis, inimicos ejus convertet ad pacem.
paras.en: [[1:4|May he open your heart|Adaperiat cor vestrum]], enlightening the understanding and stirring up and kindling the will, [[1:4|in his law|in lege sua]], to understand and fulfil it: as the Psalmist prays, [[Ps 118:34|Give me understanding, and I will search thy law; and I will keep it with my whole heart|Da mihi intellectum, et scrutabor legem tuam, et custodiam illam in toto corde meo]]; [[1:4|and in his commandments|et in præceptis suis]], that you may sincerely understand and fulfil them; [[1:4|and send you peace|et faciat pacem]], peace of heart and of the times: according to that saying of Proverbs, [[Prov 16:7|When the ways of man shall please the Lord, he will convert even his enemies to peace|Quum placuerint Domino viæ hominis, inimicos ejus convertet ad pacem]].

paras.t: Exaudiat orationes vestras, quibus petitis vere salubria, et peti a Deo decentia, et reconcilietur vobis, misericorditer ignoscendo, nec vos deserat in tempore malo, id est in adversis, imo nec in vitiis et peccatis, sed in eis pie præveniat vos, et ad pœnitendum ac emendandum inducat. Denique tempus dicitur bonum aut malum, propter ea quæ contingunt aut fiunt in tempore, a quibus denominationem sortitur.
paras.en: [[1:5|May he hear your prayers|Exaudiat orationes vestras]], in which you ask for things truly wholesome and fitting to be asked of God, [[1:5|and be reconciled unto you|et reconcilietur vobis]], mercifully forgiving, [[1:5|and never forsake you in the evil time|nec vos deserat in tempore malo]], that is, in adversity; nay, nor in vices and sins either, but in them may he graciously prevent you [that is, go before you with his grace], and lead you to repent and amend. Lastly, a time is called good or evil because of the things that happen or are done in it, from which it takes its name.

paras.t: Et nunc hic, scilicet in Jerusalem et in templo, sumus orantes pro vobis: in quo patet caritas nostra ad vos; quod et tangimus, ut vos quoque oretis pro nobis.
paras.en: [[1:6|And now here|Et nunc hic]], that is, in Jerusalem and in the temple, [[1:6|we are praying for you|sumus orantes pro vobis]]: in which our charity towards you is plain; and we touch on this so that you too may pray for us.

paras.t: Regnante Demetrio, anno centesimo sexagesimo nono. Supra in primo libro facta est mentio de duobus regibus nominis hujus. Primus Demetrius fuit filius Seleuci filii Antiochi Magni: qui Demetrius jussit occidi Antiochum regem, filium Antiochi Nobilis seu Illustris; qui etiam Demetrius intravit terram patrum suorum, et cœpit regnare anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo regni Græcorum, ut dictum est in primo libro. Hunc autem primum Demetrium vicit et interfecit Alexander rex, filius præfati Antiochi. Deinde, anno centesimo sexagesimo quinto, venit Demetrius, prænominati Demetrii filius, et regnare exorsus est, ut patuit in eodem libro; et regnavit usque ad annum centesimum septuagesimum secundum, in quo captus fuit et incarceratus a rege Medorum atque Persarum, sicut præhabitum est in primo libro. Quæritur ergo, de quo Demetrio intelligatur hæc littera, ac data hujus epistolæ: et videtur ex dictis, quod de secundo Demetrio, qui cœpit regnare anno centesimo sexagesimo quinto, occiso Demetrio patre suo; sed obviare videtur, quoniam glossa Rabani dicit hunc Demetrium filium fuisse Seleuci. Propter quod quidam hoc loco negat hanc glossam: quæ tamen posset salvari, dicendo, quod Demetrius iste vocetur filius Seleuci, quia fuit filius filii ejus, sicut in libris Regum etiam Asa et Josaphat ac Ezechias dicuntur filii David regis. Insuper dici posset, quod quota annorum istorum aliter sumitur hic, et aliter primo libro. Nam et in isto primo capitulo paulo post legitur, Anno centesimo octogesimo octavo, populus qui est in Jerosolymis, senatusque et Judas: quod de Juda Machabæo exponitur, qui tamen occisus fuit anno centesimo quinquagesimo secundo regni Græcorum, ut fertur in primo libro.
paras.en: [[1:7|When Demetrius reigned, in the year one hundred and sixty-nine|Regnante Demetrio, anno centesimo sexagesimo nono]]. Above, in the first book, mention was made of two kings of this name[[1 Mach 7:1||]][[1 Mach 10:67||]]. The first Demetrius was the son of Seleucus, the son of Antiochus the Great; this Demetrius ordered king Antiochus, son of Antiochus the Noble or Illustrious, to be slain[[1 Mach 7:4||]]; this Demetrius also entered the land of his fathers and began to reign in the hundred and fifty-first year of the kingdom of the Greeks, as was said in the first book[[1 Mach 7:1||]]. This first Demetrius was conquered and slain by king Alexander, son of the aforesaid Antiochus[[1 Mach 10:50||]]. Then, in the hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius, son of the Demetrius just named, came and began to reign, as appeared in the same book[[1 Mach 10:67||]]; and he reigned until the hundred and seventy-second year, in which he was taken and imprisoned by the king of the Medes and Persians, as was told earlier in the first book[[1 Mach 14:1||]][[1 Mach 14:3||]]. It is asked, then, of which Demetrius this text is to be understood, and so the date of this letter; and from what has been said it seems to be the second Demetrius, who began to reign in the hundred and sixty-fifth year, when his father Demetrius had been slain. But against this there seems to stand the gloss of Rabanus, which says that this Demetrius was the son of Seleucus. For this reason a certain writer rejects this gloss here; yet it could be saved by saying that this Demetrius is called the son of Seleucus because he was the son of his son, just as in the books of Kings Asa and Josaphat and Ezechias too are called sons of king David[[3 Kings 15:11||]][[3 Kings 15:24||]][[3 Kings 22:51||]][[4 Kings 18:3||]] [the margin’s last reference reads IV Reg. xvi, 3; it is taken as xviii, 3, where Ezechias does as David his father]. It could further be said that the count of these years is taken one way here and another way in the first book. For in this very first chapter we read a little further on, [[1:10|In the year one hundred and eighty-eight, the people that is at Jerusalem|Anno centesimo octogesimo octavo, populus qui est in Jerosolymis]], [[1:10|and the senate, and Judas|senatusque et Judas]]: which is explained of Judas Machabeus, who nevertheless was slain in the hundred and fifty-second year of the kingdom of the Greeks, as is related in the first book[[1 Mach 9:3||]][[1 Mach 9:18||]].

paras.t: Nos Judæi, in Jerusalem commorantes, scripsimus vobis Judæis in Ægypto manentibus, in tribulatione, id est constituti in afflictione, et impetu, id est impetuosa et subita persecutione, qui impetus supervenit nobis in istis annis, a regibus et eorum principibus infidelibus, nos dire vastantibus, ex quo, id est postquam, recessit Jason a sancta terra, et a regno, id est a terra patribus nostris promissa et data, ad divinum cultum electa, et a regione Judææ. Portam succenderunt, id est, portas Jerusalem combusserunt ministri regis Antiochi Epiphanis, et effuderunt sanguinem innocentem, plurimos in Jerusalem occidendo fideles. Quod qualiter factum sit in primo libro recitatur diffuse. De isto Jasone, et qualiter adspiravit ad sacerdotii principatum, infra habetur. Fuitque princeps eorum qui (ut primo libro scriptum est) abierunt ad regem Antiochum, qui dedit eis potestatem ut facerent justitiam gentium.
paras.en: [[1:7|we Jews|Nos Judæi]], dwelling in Jerusalem, [[1:7|wrote to you|scripsimus vobis]] Jews abiding in Egypt, [[1:7|in the trouble|in tribulatione]], that is, set in affliction, [[1:7|and violence|et impetu]], that is, a violent and sudden persecution, [[1:7|that came upon us in those years|qui impetus supervenit nobis in istis annis]] from unbelieving kings and their princes, who cruelly laid us waste, [[1:7|after|ex quo]], that is, from the time that, [[1:7|Jason withdrew himself from the holy land|recessit Jason a sancta terra]], [[1:7|and from the kingdom|et a regno]], that is, from the land promised and given to our fathers and chosen for the worship of God, and from the region of Judea. [[1:8|They burnt the gate|Portam succenderunt]], that is, the ministers of king Antiochus Epiphanes burned the gates of Jerusalem, [[1:8|and shed innocent blood|et effuderunt sanguinem innocentem]], slaying very many of the faithful in Jerusalem. How this was done is told at length in the first book[[1 Mach 1:33||]][[1 Mach 1:39||]] [the margin, partly unread, gives I Mach. i, ?3 et seq.; the city is burnt at 1 Mach 1:33 and innocent blood shed at 1:39]. Of this Jason, and how he aspired to the chief priesthood, we read below[[2 Mach 4:7||]]. And he was the leader of those who (as is written in the first book[[1 Mach 1:13||]]) [[1 Mach 1:14|went to the king|abierunt ad regem]] Antiochus, who [[1 Mach 1:14|gave them license to do after the ordinances of the heathens|dedit eis potestatem ut facerent justitiam gentium]].

paras.t: Et oravimus ad Dominum pro auxilio contra hostes, et exauditi sumus ab eo, quia ejus auxilio prævaluimus adversariis nostris, et recuperavimus templum: in quo recuperato et obtulimus sacrificium, gratias referendo, et similaginem, id est similam seu panes factos ex simila, quæ est tritici farina mundissima, de qua panes propositionis fiebant; et proposuimus panes, id est, duodecim panes propositionis posuimus in templo, super mensam ad hoc deputatam, sicut in Exodo præcipitur; et accendimus lucernas, id est septem lampades quæ erant super candelabrum aureum. Præterea, qualiter factum sit totum istud, primo libro plene narratur.
paras.en: [[1:8|then we prayed to the Lord|Et oravimus ad Dominum]] for help against our enemies, [[1:8|and were heard|et exauditi sumus]] by him, since by his help we prevailed over our adversaries and recovered the temple; and when it had been recovered, [[1:8|we offered sacrifices|obtulimus sacrificium]], giving thanks, [[1:8|and fine flour|et similaginem]], that is, *simila*, or loaves made of *simila*, which is the purest flour of wheat, of which the loaves of proposition were made; [[1:8|and set forth the loaves|et proposuimus panes]], that is, we placed the twelve loaves of proposition in the temple, on the table appointed for this, as is commanded in Exodus[[Ex 25:30||]]; [[1:8|and lighted the lamps|et accendimus lucernas]], that is, the seven lamps that were on the golden candlestick[[Ex 25:37||]]. Moreover, how all this was done is told in full in the first book[[1 Mach 4:36||]] [the margin, partly unread, gives I Mach. iv, 3? et seq.; the cleansing of the temple is told from 1 Mach 4:36].

paras.t: Et nunc frequentate, id est, omni anno solennizate, dies Scenopegiæ mensis Casleu, id est Decembris, vel Novembris, secundum quosdam, ut in expositione quarti capituli primi libri plenius dictum est. Per dies autem Scenopegiæ, quidam in expositione hujus capituli et alibi, intelligit festum Purificationis Dedicationisve templi, quod Judas et fratres ejus instituerunt. Quæ expositio videtur omnino inepta, quia per festum Scenopegiæ in Scripturis veteris Testamenti designatur festum Tabernaculorum, sicut et Thomas in prima secundæ, Guillelmus quoque Parisiensis in libro de Fide et legibus, et Alexander de Hales super tertium Sententiarum, testantur. Unde Magister in historiis: Quintadecima, inquit, die mensis septimi erat Scenopegia, quod sonat, fixio tabernaculorum, a σκῆνος, quod est umbra, et πῆξις, quod fixio. Primo autem mensi Judæorum correspondet apud nos Martius vel Aprilis. Sicque septimo mensi illorum apud nos correspondet November aut December. Itaque, Judæi Jerosolymitæ hortabantur Judæos Ægyptios, ut etiam festum Scenopegiæ servarent, nec illud omitterent occasione celebrationis novi festi ab ipsis instituti, scilicet Dedicationis templi, ad cujus celebrationem ipsos exhortabantur. Sicque auctor Scholasticæ historiæ, et alii antiqui expositores interpretantur hunc passum.
paras.en: [[1:9|And now celebrate ye|Et nunc frequentate]], that is, solemnize every year, [[1:9|the days of Scenopegia in the month of Casleu|dies Scenopegiæ mensis Casleu]], that is, of December, or of November according to some, as was said more fully in the exposition of the fourth chapter of the first book[[1 Mach 4:59||]]. Now by the days of Scenopegia a certain writer, in his exposition of this chapter and elsewhere, understands the feast of the Purification or Dedication of the temple, which Judas and his brethren instituted. This exposition seems altogether unfitting, since by the feast of Scenopegia the Scriptures of the Old Testament mean the feast of Tabernacles, as Thomas also testifies in the Prima Secundæ, and William of Paris too in his book On Faith and Laws, and Alexander of Hales on the third book of the Sentences. Hence the Master in the Histories [Peter Comestor, author of the Scholastic History]: On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, he says, was the Scenopegia, which means “the fixing of tabernacles”, from σκῆνος, which is “shade”, and πῆξις, which is “fixing”. Now the first month of the Jews corresponds with us to March or April; and so the seventh month of theirs corresponds with us to November or December [a footnote of the edition corrects this to “September or October”]. So the Jews of Jerusalem exhorted the Jews of Egypt to keep the feast of Scenopegia as well, and not to leave it out on account of the celebration of the new feast they had instituted, namely the Dedication of the temple, to whose celebration they were exhorting them. And so the author of the Scholastic History and other ancient expositors interpret this passage.

paras.t: Anno centesimo octogesimo octavo. Hic, secundum quorumdam expositionem, incipit epistola missa Judæis in Ægypto morantibus, a Juda Machabæo et suis, distincta a præinducta epistola quam dicunt missam tempore Simonis post mortem Judæ et Jonathæ, Judæis pacem habentibus. Cui dicto obviare videtur quod in præhabita epistola legitur, Nos Judæi scripsimus vobis in tribulatione et impetu, ut dictum atque expositum est. Quidam tamen exponit sic, In tribulatione, id est de tribulatione: quæ expositio videtur extorta, nec textui consona, nec Glossæ, nec Rabano, nec Scholasticæ auctori historiæ. Verumtamen apparet quod ista sit alia ac specialis epistola, tam ex data ejus, quam ex personis scribentibus, et ex forma dictaminis, ut intuentibus innotescit. Qui vero vult dicere quod sit una epistola, poterit respondere: quod personæ scribentes ponuntur hic magis in speciali, quæ supra ponuntur solum in generali; similiter personæ quibus hæc scripta sunt: et quod data sit eadem in re, sed diversificatur secundum quod numeratio annorum diversimode inchoatur.
paras.en: [[1:10|In the year one hundred and eighty-eight|Anno centesimo octogesimo octavo]]. Here, according to the explanation of some, begins a letter sent to the Jews living in Egypt by Judas Machabeus and his men, distinct from the letter set down before, which they say was sent in the time of Simon, after the death of Judas and Jonathan, when the Jews had peace. Against this saying there seems to stand what we read in the preceding letter, [[1:7|we Jews wrote to you in the trouble and violence|Nos Judæi scripsimus vobis in tribulatione et impetu]], as has been said and explained. Yet a certain writer explains it thus: *In tribulatione*, that is, *about* the trouble [taking *in* as “concerning”, so that the letter would only speak of troubles past]; an explanation that seems forced, and in keeping neither with the text, nor with the Gloss, nor with Rabanus, nor with the author of the Scholastic History. Nevertheless it appears that this is another and particular letter, both from its date and from the persons writing and from the form of its wording, as is plain to those who look at it. But whoever wishes to say that it is one letter will be able to answer that the persons writing are named here more in particular, who above are named only in general, and likewise the persons to whom these things are written; and that the date is in fact the same, but differs according as the count of years is begun in different ways.

paras.t: Quidquid autem de hoc dicatur, merito quæritur, qualiter ista epistola missa a Juda ac suis, asseratur data anno centesimo octogesimo octavo, quum Judas occisus sit anno centesimo quinquagesimo secundo, sicut jam fuit probatum. Ad quod Lyra respondet: In epistola Judæ, numeratio annorum non fit a principio regni Græcorum, sed ante, ut hic innuit Glossa; sed ubi incipiat, non dicit. Additque Lyra: Potest rationabiliter dici, quod incipit a duodecimo anno regni Assueri, in quo populus Israel mirabiliter liberatus fuit a persecutione Aman, ut habetur in Esther libro. Nam liberatio illa fuit multum mirabilis, et similis liberationi Judæorum sub Antiocho factæ. In probatione autem hujus dicti, Lyra præsupponit unum, quod et alibi sæpius scripsit, quod scilicet Darius, de cujus licentia templum fuit consummatum sub Zorobabel et Aggeo, fuit filius Assueri regis et Esther reginæ, ac postea victus ab Alexandro Magno.
paras.en: Whatever be said of this, it is rightly asked how this letter, sent by Judas and his men, is said to be dated [[1:10|In the year one hundred and eighty-eight|anno centesimo octogesimo octavo]], when Judas was slain in the hundred and fifty-second year, as has already been shown. To this Lyra answers: In the letter of Judas the count of years is not made from the beginning of the kingdom of the Greeks but from before it, as the Gloss hints here; but where it begins, it does not say. And Lyra adds: It can reasonably be said that it begins from the twelfth year of the reign of Assuerus, in which the people of Israel was wonderfully delivered from the persecution of Aman, as is found in the book of Esther[[Esth 3:1||]]. For that deliverance was exceedingly wonderful, and like the deliverance of the Jews brought about under Antiochus. Now in proving this saying Lyra presupposes one thing, which he has also written often elsewhere: namely that Darius, by whose leave the temple was finished under Zorobabel and Aggeus, was the son of king Assuerus and queen Esther, and was afterwards conquered by Alexander the Great.

paras.t: Quod dictum stare non potest: quia non solum contrariatur Josepho, Bedæ, Rabano, aliisque antiquis doctoribus; sed et B. Hieronymo super Aggæum et Danielem, ubi affirmat, Darium de cujus licentia consummatum est templum, fuisse filium Hystaspis: cui Dario successit in regno filius suus Xerxes, post quem regnavit Artabanus; cui successit in regno Artaxerxes, qui et Longimanus vocatus est, post quem Xerxes, atque post eum Sogdianus; cui successit Darius cognomento Nothus, post quem regnavit Artaxerxes, qui cognominatus est Mnemon, et ab Hebræis dicitur Assuerus; Assuero successit Artaxerxes qui dictus est Ochus, cui successit in regno filius ejus Arsamus, post quem filius ejus Darius, qui ab Alexandro est victus. Hæc secundum Scholasticam historiam sunt narrata. Ex quibus patet, quod inter Darium sub quo templum est consummatum, et Darium ab Alexandro prostratum, valde multi regnaverunt. Josephus tamen non ponit tam multos. Sed quod Darius ille qui templum jussit compleri, non fuerit ille quem Alexander dejecit, tam Hieronymus quam Josephus aliique communiter tenent. Nec verum est quod Hebræi omnes dicunt, Darium, de cujus jussu consummatum est templum, fuisse filium Assueri, ut patet ex introductis: quæ omnia super Esdram plenius sunt probata. Ideo computatio prætacta falso innititur fundamento. Sed quia epistola ista sub Juda Machabæo scripta est Judæis in Ægyptum abductis, posset forsan computatio prætacta inchoari a Ptolemæo Sotere rege Ægypti, qui juxta jam dicta, Judæos secum duxit captivos in regnum suum.
paras.en: This saying cannot stand: for it goes against not only Josephus, Bede, Rabanus and other ancient doctors, but also St. Jerome on Aggeus and Daniel, where he affirms that the Darius by whose leave the temple was finished was the son of Hystaspes. To this Darius succeeded in the kingdom his son Xerxes, after whom Artabanus reigned; to him succeeded in the kingdom Artaxerxes, who was also called Longimanus, after whom came Xerxes, and after him Sogdianus; to him succeeded Darius surnamed Nothus, after whom reigned Artaxerxes, who was surnamed Mnemon and is called Assuerus by the Hebrews; Assuerus was succeeded by Artaxerxes, who was called Ochus, and to him succeeded in the kingdom his son Arsamus, after whom his son Darius, who was conquered by Alexander. These things are related according to the Scholastic History. From them it is clear that between the Darius under whom the temple was finished and the Darius overthrown by Alexander very many kings reigned. Josephus, however, does not put so many. But that the Darius who ordered the temple to be completed was not the one whom Alexander cast down, Jerome as well as Josephus and the others commonly hold. Nor is what all the Hebrews say true, that the Darius by whose command the temple was finished was the son of Assuerus, as is clear from what has been brought forward: all of which has been proved more fully in the commentary on Esdras[[1 Esd 4:24||]][[1 Mach 1:1||]] [the margin here is partly unread; it seems to give I Esdr. iv, 24, on the Darius of the temple, and I Mach. i, 1, on the Darius overthrown by Alexander]. Therefore the reckoning mentioned rests on a false foundation. But since this letter was written under Judas Machabeus to the Jews carried off into Egypt, the reckoning mentioned could perhaps begin from Ptolemy Soter, king of Egypt, who, as was said already, took the Jews with him as captives into his kingdom.

paras.t: Itaque, Judas et senatus Judæorum scripserunt Aristobulo magistro Ptolemæi. Aristobulus iste fuit natione Judæus, habitatione Ægyptius, peripateticus quoque philosophus; et Ptolemæo Philometori scripsit commenta super Moysis libros, atque in multis instruxit regem: propter quod ejus magister vocatur, prout hæc in Josepho et in Scholastica historia plenius describuntur. Qui Aristobulus est de genere christorum sacerdotum. Fuit namque de semine Aaron et posterorum ejus christorum, id est unctorum, quoniam sacerdotes in sua consecratione ungebantur, prout in Exodo atque Levitico refertur. Et his qui in Ægypto sunt Judæis fratribus, salutem animæ nunc in spe et merito, postea in re et præmio, et sanitatem corporalem ad salutem animæ ordinatam.
paras.en: So Judas and the senate of the Jews wrote [[1:10|to Aristobolus, the preceptor|Aristobulo magistro]] of Ptolemee. This Aristobulus was a Jew by nation and an Egyptian by dwelling, and also a Peripatetic philosopher; and he wrote for Ptolemee Philometor commentaries on the books of Moses, and instructed the king in many things: for which reason he is called his preceptor, as these things are more fully described in Josephus and in the Scholastic History [that is, the Historia scholastica of Peter Comestor]. This Aristobulus [[1:10|is of the stock of the anointed priests|est de genere christorum sacerdotum]]. For he was of the seed of Aaron and of his posterity, the *christs*, that is, the anointed, since the priests were anointed at their consecration, as is related in Exodus[[Ex 29:7||]][[Ex 29:21||]] and Leviticus[[Lev 8:12||]][[Lev 8:30||]]. [[1:10|And to the Jews that are in Egypt|Et his qui in Ægypto sunt Judæis]], their brethren, [[1:10|health|salutem]] of soul, now in hope and merit, hereafter in reality and reward, [[1:10|and welfare|et sanitatem]] of body, ordered to the health of the soul.

paras.t: De magnis periculis, id est arduis impugnationibus, liberati a Deo, cujus auxilio et virtute prævaluimus hostibus, magnifice, scilicet totis præcordiis, gratias agimus ipsi Deo. Qui enim beneficia non advertit, nec gratias agit, damnabiliter est ingratus. Utpote qui adversus talem, id est tam ferocem et potentem, regem, scilicet Antiochum Illustrem, dimicavimus, victoriamque sortiti sumus.
paras.en: [[1:11|Having been delivered by God|liberati a Deo]] [[1:11|out of great dangers|De magnis periculis]], that is, out of hard assaults (by God, with whose help and strength we have prevailed over our enemies), [[1:11|we give him great thanks|gratias agimus ipsi]], to God: *greatly* [Latin *magnifice*], that is, with our whole heart (for he who does not heed benefits, and gives no thanks, is damnably ungrateful), [[1:11|forasmuch as we have been in war with such|Utpote qui adversus talem]], that is, so fierce and mighty, [[1:11|a king|regem]], namely Antiochus the Illustrious [that is, Antiochus Epiphanes], and won the victory.

paras.t: Ipse enim, ebullire, id est copiose ac impetuose venire, fecit de Perside, id est regione Persarum, eos qui pugnaverunt contra nos, id est duces et principes suos cum auxiliariis suis, qui nos impugnaverunt, ut patuit primo libro.
paras.en: [[1:12|For he made numbers of men swarm|Ipse enim, ebullire]] [literally, “made them boil out”], that is, come in great numbers and with violence, [[1:12|out of Persia|fecit de Perside]], that is, the country of the Persians, [[1:12|that have fought against us|eos qui pugnaverunt contra nos]], that is, his generals and princes with their auxiliaries, who attacked us, as was shown in the first book[[1 Mach 3:31||]] [the margin gives I Mach. iii, 31 et seq., and a further reference that cannot be read].

paras.t: Nam quum in Perside esset dux ipse. Hoc exponitur non de Antiocho Nobili, sed patre ipsius, qui fuit dux et caput filii sui. Et cum ipso immensus, id est valde magnus, exercitus, cecidit, id est, occisus est, in templo Naneæ, id est Dianæ vel Fortunæ, secundum quosdam, consilio deceptus sacerdotum Naneæ.
paras.en: [[1:13|For when the leader himself was in Persia|Nam quum in Perside esset dux ipse]]. This is explained not of Antiochus the Noble [that is, Epiphanes], but of his father, who was the leader, and the head of his son. And [[1:13|with him a very great|cum ipso immensus]], that is, exceedingly large, [[1:13|army|exercitus]], [[1:13|he fell|cecidit]], that is, was slain, [[1:13|in the temple of Nanea|in templo Naneæ]], that is, of Diana, or of Fortune according to some, [[1:13|being deceived by the counsel of the priests of Nanea|consilio deceptus sacerdotum Naneæ]].

paras.t: Etenim cum ea habitaturus, venit ad locum Antiochus, id est, mox quum Antiochus Magnus a Romanis de bello fugatus venisset ad templum Naneæ, quasi quieturus cum ipsa, hoc est reverentiam ei facturus ad tempus, et ut acciperet pecunias multas, in templo illo repositas, quas sacerdotes promiserunt ei dolose, ut comprehensum in templo occiderent: acciperet, inquam, dotis nomine, id est sub ratione doni gratis exhibiti.
paras.en: For, [[1:14|as though he would marry her|cum ea habitaturus]] [literally, “as one about to dwell with her”], Antiochus [[1:14|came to the place|venit ad locum]]: that is, as soon as Antiochus the Great, put to flight in war by the Romans, had come to the temple of Nanea, as though to rest with her, that is, to do her reverence for a time, [[1:14|and that he might receive great sums of money|et ut acciperet pecunias multas]] laid up in that temple, which the priests had treacherously promised him, so that they might seize him in the temple and kill him: that he might receive them, I say, [[1:14|under the title of a dowry|dotis nomine]], that is, under the name of a gift freely offered.

paras.t: Cumque proposuissent eas sacerdotes Naneæ, id est, quum eas præsentassent Antiocho, ut magis crederet ipsis, et amore pecuniarum allectus, ingrederetur loca secretiora ad paratas insidias. Unde subjungitur: et ipse cum paucis ingressus esset intra ambitum fani, id est templi, clauserunt templum; apertoque occulto aditu, id est ingressu seu ostio templi, mittentes lapides percusserunt ducem, id est Antiochum lapidaverunt hi qui erant absconditi in abditis templi, quo ipse fuit inductus, et eos qui cum eo erant in templo, quoniam templorum exstitit spoliator; et diviserunt membratim, et capitibus amputatis foras projecerunt, in detestationem criminum ejus.
paras.en: [[1:15|And when the priests of Nanea had set it forth|Cumque proposuissent eas sacerdotes Naneæ]], that is, when they had presented the money to Antiochus, so that he might trust them the more and, drawn on by love of money, might go into the more secret places, to the ambush laid for him. Whence it is added: [[1:15|and he with a small company had entered into the compass of the temple|et ipse cum paucis ingressus esset intra ambitum fani]], that is, of the shrine, [[1:15|they shut the temple|clauserunt templum]]; [[1:16|and opening a secret entrance|apertoque occulto aditu]], that is, a way in or door of the temple, [[1:16|they cast stones and slew the leader|mittentes lapides percusserunt ducem]], that is, those who were hidden in the hidden parts of the temple, into which he had been led, stoned Antiochus, [[1:16|and them that were with him|et eos qui cum eo erant]] in the temple, since he was a plunderer of temples; [[1:16|and hewed them in pieces|et diviserunt membratim]], [[1:16|and cutting off their heads, they threw them forth|et capitibus amputatis foras projecerunt]], in detestation of his crimes.

paras.t: Per omnia benedictus Deus, qui tradidit impios illos in mortem: id est, divina justitia benedicatur in isto effectu, in quantum impii, Deo volente, ita puniti sunt, non in quantum in illa impiorum occisione fuerant multa peccata admixta, videlicet fraus, mendacium, prava intentio interficientium illos.
paras.en: [[1:17|Blessed be God in all things, who hath delivered up the wicked|Per omnia benedictus Deus, qui tradidit impios]], those men, unto death: that is, let the divine justice be blessed in this outcome, in so far as the wicked were punished thus by the will of God, not in so far as many sins were mingled in that slaying of the wicked, namely fraud, lying, and the evil intention of those who killed them.

paras.t: Facturi ergo, id est celebraturi, Purificationem templi, sicut expositum est, necessarium duximus, id est utile ad salutem significare vobis, ut et vos quoque agatis diem Scenopegiæ, id est, non solum celebretis nobiscum templi Dedicationem, sed nec omittatis ob hoc Tabernaculorum celebritatem, nec festum de incensione ignis. Nam subditur: et celebretis diem ignis qui datus est miraculose a Deo, quando Nehemias ædificato templo et altari obtulit sacrificia. Fuit enim sacerdos, quemadmodum Esdras.
paras.en: [[1:18|Therefore, whereas we purpose to keep|Facturi ergo]], that is, to celebrate, [[1:18|the purification of the temple|Purificationem templi]], as has been explained, [[1:18|we thought it necessary|necessarium duximus]], that is, useful for salvation, [[1:18|to signify it to you|significare vobis]]: [[1:18|that you also may keep the day of Scenopegia|ut et vos quoque agatis diem Scenopegiæ]]: that is, that you may not only celebrate with us the Dedication of the temple, but may not on that account leave out the solemnity of Tabernacles, nor the feast of the kindling of the fire. For it goes on: and that you keep [[1:18|the day of the fire|diem ignis]], [[1:18|that was given|qui datus est]] miraculously by God, [[1:18|when Nehemias offered sacrifice, after the temple and the altar was built|quando Nehemias ædificato templo et altari obtulit sacrificia]]. For he was a priest, as Esdras was [the margin gives a reference to Esdras here that cannot be read].

paras.t: Nam quum in Persidem ducerentur patres nostri. Istud exponitur de captivitate Judæorum sub Nabuchodonosor rege, qui eos jussit duci in Babylonem ac Babyloniæ regionem. Attamen ex illa multi Judæorum devenerunt in regionem Persarum atque Medorum: sicque ducebantur et illuc, quando in Babyloniam ducebantur. Sacerdotes qui tunc Dei cultores erant, acceptum ignem de altari absconderunt in valle; id est, sacerdotes cum aliis in captivitatem ducendi, ignem qui sub altari holocaustorum jugiter arsit, secum sumpserunt, atque in valle (ut dicitur) Josaphat absconderunt, ubi erat puteus altus, id est profundus, et siccus. Sic et in Joanne legitur: Puteus altus est. Et in Psalmo: Veni in altitudinem maris. Atque in eo contutati sunt eum, id est, in lacu illo tute et clam posuerunt hunc ignem. Ex quo elicitur, quod et tunc erant aliqui sacerdotes devoti et justi, quamvis perpauci. Ita ut omnibus, præter hos sacerdotes, ignotus esset locus in quo ignis ille fuit absconditus, quoad hoc, quod erat locus absconsionis ignis ipsius. Puteus tamen ille pluribus fuit notus.
paras.en: [[1:19|For when our fathers were led into Persia|Nam quum in Persidem ducerentur patres nostri]]. This is explained of the captivity of the Jews under king Nabuchodonosor, who ordered them to be led to Babylon and the country of Babylon[[4 Kings 25:11||]][[2 Par 36:20||]]. Yet from that country many of the Jews came into the country of the Persians and Medes: and so they were led thither too, when they were led into Babylonia. The [[1:19|priests that then were worshippers of God|Sacerdotes qui tunc Dei cultores erant]], taking [[1:19|the fire from the altar|ignem de altari]], [[1:19|hid it in a valley|absconderunt in valle]]: that is, the priests who were to be led into captivity with the rest took with them the fire that burned continually under the altar of holocausts, and hid it in the valley (it is said) of Josaphat, [[1:19|where there was a deep pit|ubi erat puteus altus]], *deep*, that is, profound, [[1:19|without water|et siccus]] [literally, “dry”]. So too we read in John: [[John 4:11|the well is deep|Puteus altus est]]. And in the Psalm: [[Ps 68:3|I am come into the depth of the sea|Veni in altitudinem maris]]. And [[1:19|there they kept it safe|in eo contutati sunt eum]], that is, in that pit they put this fire safely and secretly. From which it is gathered that even then there were some devout and just priests, though very few; [[1:19|so that the place was unknown to all men|Ita ut omnibus, præter hos sacerdotes, ignotus esset locus]] (all, that is, but these priests), the place in which that fire was hidden: as regards this, that it was the place where the fire itself was hidden. The pit itself, however, was known to many.

paras.t: Quum præterissent autem dies multi, post septuaginta annos Babylonicæ captivitatis et amplius, et placuit Deo ut mitteretur Nehemias a rege Persidis ad reædificandum Jerusalem: a rege (inquam) Artaxerxe, a quo Nehemias licentiam petiit redeundi, ut in Nehemia habetur; nepotes sacerdotum illorum qui absconderant ignem, misit Nehemias ad requirendum ignem præfatum in valle prædicta; et sicut narraverunt nobis, non invenerunt ignem illum, quia jam fuit exstinctus, sed aquam crassam.
paras.en: [[1:20|But when many years had passed|Quum præterissent autem dies multi]] [Denis reads *dies*, “days”, where the Vulgate has *anni*, “years”], after the seventy years of the Babylonian captivity and more, [[1:20|and it pleased God that Nehemias should be sent by the king of Persia|et placuit Deo ut mitteretur Nehemias a rege Persidis]] to rebuild Jerusalem: by the king (I say) Artaxerxes, from whom Nehemias asked leave to return, as is found in Nehemias[[2 Esd 2:5||]] [the margin gives II Esdr. ii, with a verse not clearly legible, et seq.]; [[1:20|some of the posterity of those priests that had hid it|nepotes sacerdotum illorum qui absconderant]] (the fire), Nehemias sent [[1:20|to seek for the fire|ad requirendum ignem]] aforesaid in the valley aforesaid: [[1:20|and as they told us|et sicut narraverunt nobis]], [[1:20|they found no fire|non invenerunt ignem illum]], because it had already gone out, [[1:20|but thick water|sed aquam crassam]].

paras.t: Et jussit eos haurire ex puteo illo aquam crassam; et sacrificia quæ imposita erant altari holocausti, jussit sacerdos Nehemias adspergi aqua ipsa, et ligna quæ erant superposita sacrificiis, jussit similiter aqua illa adspergi.
paras.en: [[1:21|Then he bade them draw it up|Et jussit eos haurire]] from that pit, the thick water; and [[1:21|the priest, Nehemias, commanded|jussit sacerdos Nehemias]] [[1:21|the sacrifices that were laid on|sacrificia quæ imposita erant]] the altar of holocaust [[1:21|to be sprinkled with the same water|adspergi aqua ipsa]]; and [[1:21|the wood|et ligna]], [[1:21|and the things that were laid|quæ erant superposita]] upon the sacrifices, he commanded to be sprinkled likewise with that water.

paras.t: Utque, id est postquam, hoc factum est, et tempus adfuit quo sol refulsit, radios sensibiliter emittendo, qui prius erat in nubilo, id est sub obscuro seu nube densa, accensus est ignis magnus divina virtute, angelico ministerio: quo ligna illa subito fuerunt incensa, ita ut omnes hic intuentes ac percipientes, mirarentur: quum aqua soleat ignem exstinguere, non inflammare. Porro, de hac re nihil habetur in Esdra et Nehemia.
paras.en: [[1:22|And when|Utque]], that is, after, [[1:22|this was done|hoc factum est]], [[1:22|and the time came that the sun shone out|et tempus adfuit quo sol refulsit]], sending forth its rays so as to be seen, [[1:22|which before was in a cloud|qui prius erat in nubilo]], that is, under darkness or a thick cloud, [[1:22|there was a great fire kindled|accensus est ignis magnus]] by divine power, through the ministry of angels, by which that wood was suddenly set alight, [[1:22|so that all|ita ut omnes]] who looked on and perceived this [[1:22|wondered|mirarentur]]: since water is wont to put out fire, not to kindle it. Moreover, nothing of this matter is found in Esdras and Nehemias.

paras.t: Orationem autem faciebant omnes sacerdotes dum consummaretur sacrificium: quia ab igne illo desuper dato devorabatur, sicut et sacrificium Eliæ, ut tertio Regum volumine habetur. Erant autem magna devotione succensi ex miraculo illo. Orabantque Deum ut sacrificium ipsorum esset Deo acceptum. Jonatha inchoante. Iste non fuit Jonathas frater Judæ, sed quidam inter cantores præcipuus. Et ceteris respondentibus: sicut et nunc in ecclesia incipit cantor.
paras.en: [[1:23|And all the priests made prayer, while the sacrifice was consuming|Orationem autem faciebant omnes sacerdotes dum consummaretur sacrificium]]: for it was being devoured by that fire given from above, as was the sacrifice of Elias too, as is found in the third volume of Kings[[3 Kings 18:38||]]. And they were kindled with great devotion by that miracle, and prayed God that their sacrifice might be acceptable to God. [[1:23|Jonathan beginning|Jonatha inchoante]]. This was not Jonathan the brother of Judas, but one who was foremost among the singers. And [[1:23|the rest answering|ceteris respondentibus]]: as now too in the church the cantor begins.

paras.t: Et Nehemiæ erat oratio hunc habens modum. Præterea Nehemias ponit quamdam orationem ejus; sed illam fecit adhuc cum rege Persarum exsistens, hanc vero in templo exsistens Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[1:24|And the prayer of Nehemias was after this manner|Et Nehemiæ erat oratio hunc habens modum]]. Besides this, Nehemias in his own book sets down a certain prayer of his[[2 Esd 1:5||]]; but that one he made while he was still with the king of the Persians, whereas this one he made in the temple at Jerusalem.

paras.t: Domine Deus omnium creator: non quod universa et singula sint immediate a Deo creata, quum multa producantur a causis secundis, multa quoque generentur a principiis ejusdem speciei, ut cernimus; sed vel simpliciter et immediate, aut quoad primordialem materiam, vel quantum ad formam substantialem, omnia sunt a Deo creata. Terribilis: quoniam ei nullus potest resistere, neque ab eo appellare; suntque occulta judicia ejus, et nescimus an amore simus digni, an odio, aut quid finaliter eveniet nobis. Ideo dixit Apostolus: Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis. Et Psalmista: Venite, et videte opera Dei terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum. Hinc sanctus Job: Considerans (inquit) eum, timore sollicitor. Et fortis, quia omnipotens; et justus, imo omnis justitiæ ac virtutis regula, fons, mensura, et causa; et misericors, non per compassionis affectum, quoad divinam naturam, sed per pietatis effectum; qui solus es rex bonus independenter, essentialiter et incircumscriptibiliter. Unde ait Salvator: Nullus bonus nisi Deus.
paras.en: [[1:24|O Lord God, Creator of all things|Domine Deus omnium creator]]: not that each and every thing is created by God immediately, since many things are produced by second causes, and many too are generated from principles of the same species, as we see; but all things are created by God, either simply and immediately, or as regards their first matter, or as regards their substantial form; [[1:24|dreadful|Terribilis]]: because no one can resist him, nor appeal from him; and his judgments are hidden, and we know not whether we are worthy of love or of hatred[[Eccles 9:1||]], or what will befall us in the end. Therefore the Apostle said: [[Heb 10:31|It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.|Horrendum est incidere in manus Dei viventis.]] And the Psalmist: [[Ps 65:5|Come and see the works of God; who is terrible in his counsels over the sons of men|Venite, et videte opera Dei terribilis in consiliis super filios hominum]]. Hence holy Job: [[Job 23:15|when I consider|Considerans]] (he says) [[Job 23:15|him, I am made pensive with fear|eum, timore sollicitor]]. And [[1:24|strong|fortis]], because almighty; and [[1:24|just|justus]], nay rather the rule, fount, measure and cause of all justice and virtue; and [[1:24|merciful|misericors]], not by the feeling of compassion, as regards the divine nature, but by the effect of loving-kindness; [[1:24|who alone art the good king|qui solus es rex bonus]], independently, essentially and without bounds. Whence the Saviour says: [[Luke 18:19|None is good but God|Nullus bonus nisi Deus]].

paras.t: Solus præstans, id est incomparabiliter dignus, et eminens, seu omnia donans; solus justus pure, perfecte et infinite: cujus comparatione omnis creatura nullius videtur esse justitiæ, omnisque creata justitia, velut injustitia reputatur. Propter quod universæ justitiæ nostræ, sunt tanquam pannus menstruatæ. Qui liberas Israel, id est Israeliticum populum in te confidentem, ab omni malo pœnæ et culpæ in vita præsenti aut futura; qui fecisti patres electos, id est sanctos Patriarchas, quibus dedisti esse naturæ, et sanctificasti eos per infusionem gratiæ ac virtutum.
paras.en: [[1:25|Who alone art gracious|Solus præstans]] [*præstans* means both “excelling” and “bestowing”], that is, incomparably worthy and eminent, or giving all things; [[1:25|who alone art just|solus justus]], purely, perfectly and infinitely: in comparison with whom every creature seems to be of no justice, and all created justice is reckoned as injustice (wherefore [[Is 64:6|all our justices as the rag of a menstruous woman|universæ justitiæ nostræ, sunt tanquam pannus menstruatæ]]); [[1:25|who deliverest Israel|Qui liberas Israel]], that is, the people of Israel trusting in thee, [[1:25|from all evil|ab omni malo]] of punishment and of guilt, in the present life or the life to come; [[1:25|who didst choose the fathers|qui fecisti patres electos]], that is, the holy Patriarchs, to whom thou gavest the being of nature, [[1:25|and didst sanctify them|et sanctificasti eos]] by the infusion of grace and virtues.

paras.t: Accipe sacrificium pro universo populo tuo Israel, et custodi partem tuam, id est Israeliticam plebem quam tibi præ ceteris elegisti. Congrega dispersionem nostram, id est populum nostrum hinc inde per diversas regiones dispersum, et reduc ad terram hanc patrum nostrorum; atque per fidem, spem et caritatem spiritualiter collige eos, ut sint unum mysticum corpus in te vivificatum Spiritu Sancto. Libera eos qui serviunt gentibus, sub tributo, vel in servos et ancillas eis venundati sunt, aut præ paupertate in exsilio obsequuntur gentilibus, a quibus spernuntur. Unde subjungitur: contemptos et abominatos respice oculo pietatis, ut sciant gentes ex nostra gratiosa et miraculosa liberatione a te facta, quia tu es Deus noster: qui licet sis Deus omnium jure creationis et generalis dominationis ac gubernationis, specialiter tamen es Deus noster per providentiam specialem et gratiosam directionem, et per cultum ac adhæsionem, qua tibi fideliter adhæremus.
paras.en: [[1:26|Receive the sacrifice for all thy people Israel|Accipe sacrificium pro universo populo tuo Israel]], [[1:26|and preserve thy own portion|et custodi partem tuam]], that is, the people of Israel, whom thou hast chosen for thyself before the rest. [[1:27|Gather together our scattered people|Congrega dispersionem nostram]], that is, our people dispersed hither and thither through divers countries, and bring them back to this land of our fathers; and gather them spiritually through faith, hope and charity, that they may be one mystical body in thee, quickened by the Holy Ghost; [[1:27|deliver them that are slaves to the Gentiles|Libera eos qui serviunt gentibus]], under tribute, or who have been sold to them as bondmen and bondwomen, or who through poverty in exile wait upon the Gentiles, by whom they are despised. Whence it is added: [[1:27|look upon them that are despised and abhorred|contemptos et abominatos respice]] with the eye of loving-kindness, [[1:27|that the Gentiles may know|ut sciant gentes]] by our gracious and miraculous deliverance wrought by thee, [[1:27|that thou art our God|quia tu es Deus noster]]: for though thou art the God of all by right of creation and of general dominion and governance, yet thou art specially our God through a special providence and gracious guidance, and through the worship and the cleaving by which we faithfully cleave to thee.

paras.t: Afflige opprimentes nos, id est, in hac vita eos pie et juste castiga, et eorum tyrannidem reprime, qui adversantur bono communi cultuique divino, et contumeliam facientes cultoribus tuis in superbia, id est ex elatione: quod zelo justitiæ, non æmulatione aut affectu vindictæ, Nehemias rogavit. Constitue populum tuum in loco sancto tuo, id est in terra promissionis et in Jerusalem, sicut dixit Moyses: qui eis promisit hanc terram; et in Deuteronomio dixit: Si ad cardines cœli fueris dissipatus, inde retrahet te Dominus, et introducet in terram pro qua juravit patribus tuis.
paras.en: [[1:28|Punish them that oppress us|Afflige opprimentes nos]], that is, chastise them in this life with kindness and justice, and curb the tyranny of those who set themselves against the common good and the worship of God, [[1:28|and that treat us injuriously|et contumeliam facientes]], thy worshippers, [[1:28|with pride|in superbia]], that is, out of haughtiness: which Nehemias asked out of zeal for justice, not out of envy or the desire of vengeance. [[1:29|Establish thy people in thy holy place|Constitue populum tuum in loco sancto tuo]], that is, in the land of promise and in Jerusalem, [[1:29|as Moses hath spoken|sicut dixit Moyses]], who promised them this land; and in Deuteronomy he said: [[Deut 30:4|If thou be driven as far as the poles of heaven, the Lord thy God will fetch thee back|Si ad cardines cœli fueris dissipatus, inde retrahet te Dominus]], [[Deut 30:5|and bring thee into the land|et introducet in terram]], for which he swore to thy fathers [these last words are closer to Deut 30:20].

paras.t: Quum autem consumptum esset sacrificium, id est omnino combustum ab igne prædicto: nam oblatum fuit in holocaustum; ex residua aqua quæ super sacrificia non fuerat fusa, Nehemias jussit lapides majores in altari exsistentes, videlicet lapides (ut dicitur) laterales, perfundi.
paras.en: [[1:31|And when the sacrifice was consumed|Quum autem consumptum esset sacrificium]], that is, wholly burnt by the aforesaid fire: for it was offered as a holocaust; [[1:31|Nehemias commanded|Nehemias jussit]] [[1:31|the water that was left|ex residua aqua]], which had not been poured on the sacrifices, [[1:31|to be poured out upon the great stones|lapides majores]] that stood on the altar, namely (as it is said) the side stones.

paras.t: Quod ut factum est, flamma ex eis accensa est divina virtute: quemadmodum de prætacto igne est dictum; sed ex lumine, id est splendido igne, quod lumen refulsit ab altari, in quo fuit ignis prædictus, consumpta est: ita quod minor flamma videbatur absorberi a majore, et a duabus fieri una.
paras.en: [[1:32|Which being done|Quod ut factum est]], [[1:32|there was kindled a flame from them|flamma ex eis accensa est]] by divine power, as was said of the fire before; but [[1:32|by the light|ex lumine]], that is, by the shining fire, the light [[1:32|that shined from the altar|refulsit ab altari]] on which the aforesaid fire was, [[1:32|it was consumed|consumpta est]]: so that the lesser flame seemed to be swallowed up by the greater, and one to be made of the two.

paras.t: Ut vero manifestata est res, id est facto isto miraculoso de ignium horum productione et holocausti consumptione undique divulgato, renuntiatum est regi Persarum Artaxerxi, a quo missus fuerat Nehemias, quod in loco in quo ignem absconderant sacerdotes, videlicet in valle prætacta, aqua apparuit, de, id est cum, qua Nehemias, et qui cum eo erant purificaverunt sacrificia, id est, carnes hostiarum laverunt (sicut in Levitico jussum est de carnibus animalium immolatitiorum), et igne inde succenso, sacrificia consummavit.
paras.en: [[1:33|And when this matter became public|Ut vero manifestata est res]], that is, when this miraculous deed of the producing of these fires and the consuming of the holocaust had been spread abroad on every side, [[1:33|it was told to the king of Persia|renuntiatum est regi Persarum]], Artaxerxes, by whom Nehemias had been sent[[2 Esd 2:6||]], [[1:33|that in the place where the priests that were led away, had hid the fire|quod in loco in quo ignem absconderant sacerdotes]], namely in the valley aforesaid, [[1:33|there appeared water|aqua apparuit]], *de* [literally “of”], that is, *with*, [[1:33|which Nehemias and they that were with him had purified the sacrifices|qua Nehemias, et qui cum eo erant purificaverunt sacrificia]]: that is, they washed the flesh of the victims (as was commanded in Leviticus concerning the flesh of the animals for sacrifice[[Lev 1:9||]][[Lev 1:13||]]), and, the fire being kindled from it, he consummated the sacrifices.

paras.t: Considerans autem rex Artaxerxes factum illud mirabile, et rem diligenter examinans, per testes et inquisitores, ne forte esset conficta, fecit ei, scilicet Deo; vel Ei, utpote Nehemiæ, hoc est ad instantiam et propter reverentiam ejus; templum Deo in Jerusalem.
paras.en: [[1:34|And the king considering|Considerans autem rex]], Artaxerxes, that wonderful deed, [[1:34|and diligently examining the matter|et rem diligenter examinans]] through witnesses and investigators, lest perhaps it had been made up, [[1:34|made|fecit]] for him [Latin *ei*, which the Douay-Rheims renders “for it”], that is, for God; or for him, that is, for Nehemias, meaning at his urging and out of reverence for him, [[1:34|a temple|templum]] to God in Jerusalem.

paras.t: Certum est autem, Nehemiam esse missum a rege Artaxerxe ad Jerusalem anno regni Artaxerxis vicesimo, scilicet diu post Esdram, sicut legitur in Nehemia; et tunc templum fuit factum et consummatum, quantum ad suam structuram; imo sexto anno Darii regis Persarum, ut legitur in Esdra, exstitit consummatum: ideo factio templi non potest hic accipi proprie pro ejus ædificatione. Idcirco dictum istud non consonat opinioni erroneæ Judæorum, et suorum sequacium, dicentium quod inter Cyrum et Darium istum non fuerunt intermedii reges, nisi Cambyses et Assuerus, ita quod Darius iste secundum eos fuit Artaxerxes. Imo ex isto loco probatur falsitas opinionis illius, si factio proprie accipiatur: quoniam factio ista templi, contigit diu post vicesimum annum regni Artaxerxis, ut patuit. Et tamen si Artaxerxes iste fuit Darius, necesse est dicere, quod sexto anno regni ejus factum et completum sit ædificium templi. Quod autem inter Cyrum et Darium plures intermedii erant, constat ex dictis, et super Esdram magis est approbatum.
paras.en: Now it is certain that Nehemias was sent to Jerusalem by king Artaxerxes in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes' reign, that is, long after Esdras, as we read in Nehemias[[2 Esd 2:1||]]; and by then the temple had been made and finished as regards its structure; indeed it was finished in the sixth year of Darius king of the Persians, as we read in Esdras[[1 Esd 6:15||]]: therefore the *making* of the temple cannot be taken here properly for its building. And so this saying does not agree with the erroneous opinion of the Jews and their followers, who say that between Cyrus and this Darius there were no kings in between except Cambyses and Assuerus, so that this Darius, according to them, was Artaxerxes. Nay, the falsity of that opinion is proved from this place, if the *making* is taken properly: since this making of the temple came about long after the twentieth year of Artaxerxes' reign, as has been shown. And yet, if this Artaxerxes was Darius, it must be said that the building of the temple was made and completed in the sixth year of his reign. But that there were more kings between Cyrus and Darius is plain from what has been said, and has been more fully proved in the commentary on Esdras [the margin refers here to Denis's commentary on I Esdras; its further figures cannot be read].

paras.t: Quod ergo Artaxerxes dicitur templum Deo fecisse, intelligendum est, quod templum illud ornavit et honoravit, atque per hoc opere demonstravit templum hoc esse factum Deo vero et summo. Et talis modus loquendi frequens est in Scripturis veteris Testamenti, ut aliquis dicatur quid facere, quia ostendit aut dicit hoc factum esse sive futurum. Hinc subditur: ut probaret, id est, opere approbaret aut testaretur, quod factum erat, videlicet miraculum illud de ignis productione et holocausti consumptione vere esse divinum.
paras.en: So when Artaxerxes is said to have made a temple to God, it is to be understood that he adorned and honoured that temple, and by this showed in deed that this temple had been made to the true and most high God. And such a way of speaking is frequent in the Scriptures of the Old Testament, that someone is said to do a thing because he shows or says that it has been done or will be. Hence it is added: [[1:34|that he might prove|ut probaret]], that is, approve or bear witness by deed, [[1:34|what had happened|quod factum erat]], namely that that miracle of the producing of the fire and the consuming of the holocaust was truly divine.

paras.t: Et quum probasset, id est, factum illud taliter approbasset, sacerdotibus tanquam veri Dei ministris, dedit multa bona, et alia atque alia munera, ut orarent pro ipso ac regno suo, et ex donis illis sacrificia procurarent; et multa talia dedit illis per principes suos, qui præsidebant trans flumen: et accipiens manu sua tribuebat illis, id est, etiam propria manu contulit ipsis aliqua quæ accepit de bonis suis. Nam et Nehemias post duodecim annos cum sua comitiva ad Artaxerxem reversus est, et postmodum de licentia regis, rursus ad Jerusalem rediit, ut in Nehemia legitur: et tunc rex munera pretiosa contulit Nehemiæ ac suis.
paras.en: [[1:35|And when he had proved it|Et quum probasset]], that is, had so approved that deed, [[1:35|he gave the priests|sacerdotibus]], as ministers of the true God, [[1:35|many goods, and divers presents|multa bona, et alia atque alia munera]], that they might pray for him and his kingdom, and provide sacrifices from those gifts; and he gave them many such things through his governors, who were over the country beyond the river: [[1:35|and he took and distributed them to them with his own hand|et accipiens manu sua tribuebat illis]]: that is, he also bestowed on them with his own hand some things which he took from his own goods. For Nehemias too, after twelve years, went back with his company to Artaxerxes, and afterwards, by the king's leave, returned again to Jerusalem, as we read in Nehemias[[2 Esd 13:6||]][[2 Esd 13:7||]]: and then the king bestowed precious gifts on Nehemias and his men.

paras.t: Appellavit autem Nehemias hunc locum, id est diem seu festum loci istius, puta altaris seu templi, Nephthar, quod interpretatur purificatio. Et supra in isto capitulo vocatus est, dies ignis, etc., qui datus est de aqua crassa. Vocatur autem apud plures, id est ab aliis multis, Nephi: quod idem designat quod Nephthar.
paras.en: [[1:36|And Nehemias called this place|Appellavit autem Nehemias hunc locum]], that is, the day or feast of this place, namely of the altar or temple, [[1:36|Nephthar, which is interpreted purification|Nephthar, quod interpretatur purificatio]]. And above in this chapter it was called [[1:18|the day of the fire|dies ignis]], etc., which was given from the thick water. [[1:36|But many call it|Vocatur autem apud plures]], that is, many others, [[1:36|Nephi|Nephi]]: which means the same as Nephthar.

2.title: Elucidatio capituli secundi: Invenitur autem in descriptionibus Jeremiæ prophetæ.
2.title_en: Explanation of the second chapter: Now it is found in the descriptions of Jeremias the prophet.

paras.t: Hoc loco declarantur quædam in præcedenti capitulo dicta, præsertim de asportatione ignis altaris holocausti. Invenitur autem in descriptionibus Jeremiæ, id est in sermonibus a Jeremia, vel ex ore ipsius scriptis: quæ tamen descriptiones, nec a Catholicis, nec ab Hebræis habentur; quod jussit accipere ignem eos qui transmigrabantur, id est, quod Jeremias præcepit sacerdotibus Dei cultoribus, qui a Judæa in Babyloniam transferebantur, quod secum acciperent ignem altaris holocaustorum, ut eum in valle absconderent Josaphat, ut significatum est, id est, prout dictum est capitulo præcedenti, et ut mandavit transmigratis, id est, sicut jussit sacerdotibus in Chaldæam translatis. Sic continetur in descriptionibus illis.
paras.en: In this place some things said in the preceding chapter are explained, especially about the carrying away of the fire of the altar of holocausts[[2 Mach 1:19||]]. [[2:1|Now it is found in the descriptions of Jeremias|Invenitur autem in descriptionibus Jeremiæ]], that is, in discourses written by Jeremias, or from his mouth: which descriptions, however, are held neither by the Catholics nor by the Hebrews; [[2:1|that he commanded them that went into captivity, to take the fire|quod jussit accipere ignem eos qui transmigrabantur]], that is, that Jeremias charged the priests, the worshippers of God, who were being carried away from Judæa into Babylonia, to take with them the fire of the altar of holocausts, so as to hide it in the valley of Josaphat, [[2:1|as it hath been signified|ut significatum est]], that is, as was said in the preceding chapter[[2 Mach 1:19||]] [the margin gives II Mach. i, its verse unread; the hiding of the fire is told at 2 Mach 1:19, where the valley is not named], [[2:1|and how he gave charge to them that were carried away into captivity|et ut mandavit transmigratis]], that is, as he commanded the priests carried over into Chaldæa. So it is contained in those descriptions.

paras.t: Et dedit illis legem, id est, legem Moysis commisit Jeremias illis, ut eam implerent: et forsan librum legis Moysis præstitit eis ad legendum, recolendum, custodiendumque legem. Hinc subditur: ne obliviscerentur præcepta Domini, et ut non exerrarent mentibus, id est, ne corda eorum per infidelitatem errarent, videntes simulacra, id est idola, aurea et argentea, et ornamenta eorum, quæ in Babylone viderunt a Chaldæis adorari et coli. Et de hoc habetur in epistola Jeremiæ missa Judæis in Babylone morantibus. Et alia hujusmodi salubria documenta dicens Jeremias, hortabatur præfatos ne legem, id est assiduam memoriam et observantiam legis, amoverent a corde suo.
paras.en: [[2:2|And how he gave them the law|Et dedit illis legem]], that is, Jeremias committed the law of Moses to them, that they might fulfil it; and perhaps he furnished them with the book of the law of Moses, for reading, calling to mind and keeping the law. Hence there follows: [[2:2|that they should not forget the commandments of the Lord|ne obliviscerentur præcepta Domini]], [[2:2|and that they should not err in their minds|et ut non exerrarent mentibus]], that is, lest their hearts should stray through unbelief, [[2:2|seeing the idols|videntes simulacra]], that is, false gods, [[2:2|of gold, and silver, and the ornaments of them|aurea et argentea, et ornamenta eorum]], which they saw adored and worshipped by the Chaldeans in Babylon. And of this there is mention in the epistle of Jeremias sent to the Jews dwelling in Babylon[[Bar 6:3||]][[Bar 6:4||]]. [[2:3|And with other such like speeches|Et alia hujusmodi salubria documenta dicens]], wholesome teachings, Jeremias [[2:3|exhorted|hortabatur]] the aforesaid [[2:3|that they would not remove the law|ne legem]], that is, the constant remembrance and observance of the law, [[2:3|from their heart|amoverent a corde suo]].

paras.t: Erat autem in ipsa scriptura, id est præfatis descriptionibus Jeremiæ contentum, quomodo tabernaculum Moysis et arcam per Beseleel factam jussit Propheta Jeremias, divino responso ad se facto, comitari, id est per comites seu socios viæ portari secum ad spatium certum. Ex hoc apparet, quod Jeremias præscius destructionis civitatis Jerusalem, combustionisque templi a Chaldæis, sollicitus fuit pro arca ceterisque prædictis, et Dominum exoravit, ut sibi revelare dignaretur, qualiter illa essent conservanda. Cujus piæ petitioni Dominus dedit responsum ut faceret quæ sequuntur, videlicet quod duceret ea secum, usque quo exiit, id est, quousque ipse Jeremias eundo pertingeret, in montem in quo Moyses ascendit et vidit Dei hæreditatem, id est in montem Nebo in verticem Phasga, in cujus montis altitudinem Moyses Deo jubente ascendit, ad videndum terram promissionis: quæ vocatur hæreditas Dei, id est terra quam Omnipotens filiis Israel præstitit hæreditarie possidendam. Hinc scriptum est Deuteronomii ultimo: Ascendit Moyses de campestribus Moab super montem Nebo, etc.
paras.en: [[2:4|It was also contained in the same writing|Erat autem in ipsa scriptura]], that is, it was contained in the aforesaid descriptions of Jeremias, [[2:4|how|quomodo]] [[2:4|the prophet|Propheta]] Jeremias, [[2:4|being warned by God|divino responso ad se facto]], [[2:4|commanded|jussit]] [[2:4|that the tabernacle|tabernaculum]] of Moses [[2:4|and the ark|et arcam]] made by Beseleel[[Ex 25:9||]][[Ex 36:1||]] [[2:4|should accompany him|comitari]], that is, should be carried with him by companions or fellows of the way, for a certain distance. From this it appears that Jeremias, foreknowing the destruction of the city of Jerusalem and the burning of the temple by the Chaldeans, was anxious for the ark and the other things mentioned, and besought the Lord that he would deign to reveal to him how they were to be preserved. To his godly petition the Lord gave the answer that he should do what follows, namely that he should take them with him [[2:4|till he came forth|usque quo exiit]], that is, until Jeremias himself, going on his way, should reach it, [[2:4|to the mountain where Moses went up, and saw the inheritance of God|in montem in quo Moyses ascendit et vidit Dei hæreditatem]]: that is, to mount Nebo, to the top of Phasga, to the height of which mountain Moses went up at God's command to see the land of promise, which is called the inheritance of God, that is, the land which the Almighty gave the children of Israel to possess as an inheritance. Hence it is written in the last chapter of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 34:1|Moses went up from the plains of Moab upon mount Nebo|Ascendit Moyses de campestribus Moab super montem Nebo]], etc.

paras.t: Et veniens ibi Jeremias, invenit locum speluncæ, quam ex revelatione divina cognovit, et tabernaculum, id est materias tabernaculi, et arcam, et altare incensi, id est thymiamatis, intulit illuc, et ostium speluncæ obstruxit.
paras.en: [[2:5|And when Jeremias came thither|Et veniens ibi Jeremias]] [[2:5|he found a hollow cave|invenit locum speluncæ]], which he knew of by divine revelation; and [[2:5|the tabernacle|et tabernaculum]], that is, the materials of the tabernacle, [[2:5|and the ark, and the altar of incense|et arcam, et altare incensi]], that is, of thymiama, [[2:5|he carried in thither|intulit illuc]], [[2:5|and so stopped the door|et ostium speluncæ obstruxit]] of the cave.

paras.t: Et accesserunt quidam simul, id est, pariter properaverunt ad locum prædictum, qui sequebantur Jeremiam, ut notarent sibi locum, in quo prædicta erant abscondita. Ut autem cognovit Jeremias curiositatem illorum in inquirendo locum præfatum, culpans, id est increpans, illos, dixit quod ignotus erit locus ille tabernaculi et altaris et arcæ, donec congreget Deus congregationem populi, id est, populum Judæorum hinc inde dispersum, in unum recolligat, et propitius fiat populo propitiatione perfecta; et tunc Dominus ostendet hæc, scilicet tabernaculum, arcam, altare, et apparebit majestas Domini, id est, Deus omnipotentiam et gloriam suam ostendet per effectus præclaros, et nubes erit obumbrans populo Dei, sicut et Moysi manifestabatur columna nubis, et nubes quædam in consecratione tabernaculi, juxta illud Exodi, Postquam cuncta perfecta sunt, operuit nubes tabernaculum testimonii, et gloria Domini implevit illud.
paras.en: [[2:6|Then some of them|Et accesserunt quidam simul]], that is, together they hastened to the aforesaid place, [[2:6|that followed him|qui sequebantur]], that is, Jeremias, [[2:6|came up to mark the place|ut notarent sibi locum]] in which the aforesaid things had been hidden. [[2:7|And when Jeremias perceived it|Ut autem cognovit Jeremias]], that is, their curiosity in seeking out the aforesaid place, [[2:7|he blamed|culpans]], that is, rebuked, [[2:7|them, saying|illos, dixit]] that that place of the tabernacle and altar and ark [[2:7|shall be unknown|ignotus erit]], [[2:7|till God gather together the congregation of the people|donec congreget Deus congregationem populi]], that is, gather into one the people of the Jews scattered this way and that, [[2:7|and receive them to mercy|et propitius fiat]] [literally “and be propitious”] to the people with a perfect propitiation. [[2:8|And then the Lord will shew these things|et tunc Dominus ostendet hæc]], namely the tabernacle, the ark and the altar, [[2:8|and the majesty of the Lord shall appear|et apparebit majestas Domini]], that is, God will show his almighty power and his glory by glorious effects, [[2:8|and there shall be a cloud|et nubes erit]] overshadowing the people of God, [[2:8|as it was also shewed to Moses|sicut et Moysi manifestabatur]], the pillar of the cloud, and a cloud also at the consecration of the tabernacle, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 40:31|After all things were perfected|Postquam cuncta perfecta sunt]], [[Ex 40:32|The cloud covered the tabernacle of the testimony, and the glory of the Lord filled it|operuit nubes tabernaculum testimonii, et gloria Domini implevit illud]].

paras.t: Quæritur, an ista impleta sunt, an implenda. Circa hoc scribit Nicolaus de Lyra: Hanc congregationem et propitiationem exspectant Judæi futuram in adventu Messiæ; et nos intelligimus eas factas in Christi adventu, juxta illud Joannis: Jesus moriturus erat pro gente; et non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Quum ergo prædicta non sint in Christi adventu ostensa, quia secundum Hebræos a tempore captivitatis Babylonicæ usque nunc, non est ostensa aut habita arca Dei: propter hoc locus iste videtur aliquibus falsus aut saltem dubius. Posset tamen ad hoc dici, quod prædicta apparebunt in fine mundi, in conversione Judæorum ad fidem Christi. Sed hoc videtur esse contra illud Jeremiæ: Non dicent ultra, Arca Domini; neque ascendet super cor, neque recordabuntur illius, nec fiet ultra. Item, quod hic dicitur de absconsione altaris et arcæ per Jeremiam, non habet apparentiam magnam: quoniam Jeremias fuit incarceratus usque ad captionem Jerusalem per Chaldæos, ut patet in Jeremiæ capitulis; et sicut ante captionem civitatis ista non fecit, nec postea, ut videtur: quoniam capta civitate, Chaldæi mox confregerunt omnia pretiosa, non solum aurea et argentea, sed etiam ærea, abstuleruntque secum, ut dicitur quarto Regum. Propter quod non videtur verisimile, quod Jeremiæ dimiserunt arcam et altare incensi, quæ erant de auro purissimo, ut habetur in Exodo. Igitur propter ista et alia supradicta de morte Antiochi et de tempore Demetrii, quæ cum difficultate magna vix possunt cum aliis Scripturæ locis concordari, ut patet ex supradictis, liber iste secundus, et maxime quantum ad suam præfationem, reputatur a multis multum apocryphus. Istud tamen majorum judicio derelinquo. Hæc Lyra.
paras.en: It is asked whether these things have been fulfilled, or are yet to be fulfilled. On this Nicholas of Lyra writes: The Jews await this gathering and propitiation as something to come at the advent of the Messias; and we understand them as having been accomplished at the advent of Christ, according to that of John: [[John 11:51|Jesus should die for the nation|Jesus moriturus erat pro gente]]; [[John 11:52|And not only for the nation, but to gather together in one the children of God that were dispersed|et non tantum pro gente, sed ut filios Dei qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum]]. Since, then, the aforesaid things were not shown at the advent of Christ (for according to the Hebrews the ark of God has not been shown or possessed from the time of the Babylonian captivity until now), this passage seems to some, for that reason, false, or at least doubtful. Yet it might be said to this that the aforesaid things will appear at the end of the world, at the conversion of the Jews to the faith of Christ. But this seems to be against that of Jeremias: [[Jer 3:16|they shall say no more: The ark of the covenant of the Lord|Non dicent ultra, Arca Domini]]: [[Jer 3:16|neither shall it come upon the heart, neither shall they remember it|neque ascendet super cor, neque recordabuntur illius]], [[Jer 3:16|neither shall that be done any more|nec fiet ultra]] [Denis's text has neither “of the covenant” nor “neither shall it be visited”]. Again, what is said here of the hiding of the altar and the ark by Jeremias has no great likelihood: for Jeremias was imprisoned until the taking of Jerusalem by the Chaldeans, as appears in the chapters of Jeremias[[Jer 37:15||]][[Jer 38:28||]] [the margin's references here are only partly legible: Ibid. xxxvii, …; 6, 14, 28]; and as he did not do these things before the taking of the city, so neither afterwards, as it seems: for when the city was taken, the Chaldeans straightway broke up all the precious things, not only those of gold and silver but also those of brass, and carried them away with them, as is said in the fourth book of Kings[[4 Kings 25:13||]].
