[[4:19|Jason sent|Misit Jason]] men [[4:19|to carry three hundred didrachmas of silver for the sacrifice of Hercules|portantes argenti didrachmas trecentas in sacrificium Herculis]]: [[4:19|but the bearers thereof desired|quas postulaverunt hi qui asportaverunt]], that is, those who took it with them, [[4:19|it might not be bestowed on the sacrifices|ne in sacrificiis Herculis erogarentur]] of Hercules, [[4:19|because it was not necessary|quia non oporteret]], that is, it was neither needful, nor indeed useful. But, [[4:20|because of them that carried it|Propter præsentes autem]], that is, at the instance of those who were there, it [[4:20|was employed for the making of galleys|datæ sunt in fabricam navium triremium]], that is, for building ships in which there were three banks of oars.

paras.t: Misso autem in Ægyptum Apollonio, quem illuc misit Antiochus propter primates Ptolemæi Philometoris regis Ægypti, cujus aliqua oppida occupavit Antiochus: quæ primates præfati Ptolemæi adhuc adolescentuli, requirebant ab Antiocho; principes Ptolemæi contra eum, oppida illa reddere non volentem, pugnam moverunt. Quum cognovisset Antiochus alienum se a negotiis regni Ægypti effectum, venit Jerosolymam. Fuit enim ab Ægypto per Romanorum legatos repulsus, ut dictum est plenius in expositione primi libri. Et magnifice a Jasone, quem ad pontificatum simoniace ac perverse promovit, et civitate susceptus, cum facularum luminibus et laudibus ingressus est; et inde in Phœnicen exercitum convertit. Verumtamen tunc, ut videtur, fecit mala multa et magna, quæ primi libri capitulo primo recitantur.
paras.en: [[4:21|Now when Apollonius, the son of Mnestheus was sent into Egypt|Misso autem in Ægyptum Apollonio]], whom Antiochus sent there [[4:21|to treat with the nobles of king Philometor|propter primates Ptolemæi Philometoris regis Ægypti]], some of whose towns Antiochus had seized (towns which the nobles of the aforesaid Ptolemee, still a youth, were demanding back from Antiochus; and Ptolemee's princes made war on him when he would not give those towns back): when [[4:21|Antiochus understood that he was wholly excluded from the affairs of the kingdom|cognovisset Antiochus alienum se a negotiis regni Ægypti effectum]] of Egypt, he came [[4:21|to Jerusalem|venit Jerosolymam]]. For he was driven back from Egypt by the envoys of the Romans, as was said more fully in the exposition of the first book. [[4:22|Where he was received in a magnificent manner by Jason|Et magnifice a Jasone]], whom he had promoted to the high priesthood simoniacally and perversely, [[4:22|and the city|et civitate susceptus]], [[4:22|and came in with torch lights, and with praises|cum facularum luminibus et laudibus ingressus est]], [[4:22|and from thence he returned with his army into Phenicia|et inde in Phœnicen exercitum convertit]]. Yet at that time, it seems, he did many great evils, which are related in the first chapter of the first book[[1 Mach 1:22||]].

paras.t: Et post triennii tempus misit Jason frater Oniæ, Menelaum, supradicti Simonis fratrem, portantem pecunias regi Antiocho, et de negotiis necessariis, id est de causis sibi commissis, responsa perlaturum, id est reportaturum a rege. Circa hæc incidit quæstio, quomodo Menelaus iste dicatur frater Simonis supradicti, qui (ut præcedenti fertur capitulo) de Benjamin fuit tribu; Jason autem et Onias de tribu Levi et Aaron erant. Josephus autem apertissime scribit duodecimo Antiquitatum libro, quod Jason et Menelaus fuerunt fratres Oniæ. Hinc Lyra hoc loco negat Josephum, propter hujus libri auctoritatem. Verum Magister in historiis et alii multi authentici et antiqui Catholici, secuti sunt Josephum: et rationabiliter, ut videtur. Judæi enim non sustinuissent Menelaum in pontificatu, nisi de genere Aaron exstitisset. Nec post reditum a Babylonica captivitate leguntur Judæi unquam aliquem habuisse pontificem, nisi de stirpe Levi et Aaron. Quod autem Menelaus dicitur fuisse frater Simonis supradicti, quidam exponunt dicentes, quod fuit frater ejus non carnis propagatione, sed imitatione et conformitate malitiæ. Juxta quem modum in Ecclesiastico scriptum est: Qui effundit sanguinem, et qui fraudem facit mercenario, fratres sunt. Posset etiam dici, quod quia tribus Levi poterat cum ceteris tribubus Israel matrimonia sociare, Menelaus iste ex parte unius parentis, præsertim matris, forsitan fuit de Benjamin tribu et Simonis frater.
paras.en: [[4:23|Three years afterwards Jason sent|Et post triennii tempus misit Jason]], the brother of Onias, [[4:23|Menelaus, brother of the aforesaid Simon|Menelaum, supradicti Simonis fratrem]], [[4:23|to carry money to the king|portantem pecunias regi]] Antiochus, and, [[4:23|concerning certain necessary affairs|et de negotiis necessariis]], that is, the matters committed to him, [[4:23|to bring answers from him|responsa perlaturum]], that is, to carry them back from the king. Here a question arises: how this Menelaus can be called the brother of the aforesaid Simon, who (as is told in the preceding chapter) was of the tribe of Benjamin[[2 Mach 3:4||]], whereas Jason and Onias were of the tribe of Levi and of Aaron. Josephus, indeed, writes most plainly in the twelfth book of the Antiquities that Jason and Menelaus were brothers of Onias. Hence Lyra, in this place, rejects Josephus, on account of the authority of this book. But the Master in the Histories [Peter Comestor, in the *Historia scholastica*] and many other authentic and ancient Catholics have followed Josephus: and reasonably, as it seems. For the Jews would not have borne Menelaus in the high priesthood unless he had been of the race of Aaron. Nor after the return from the Babylonian captivity are the Jews ever read to have had any high priest except of the stock of Levi and Aaron. As for Menelaus being called the brother of the aforesaid Simon, some explain it by saying that he was his brother not by descent in the flesh, but by imitation of his malice and likeness to it; in which manner it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 34:27|He that sheddeth blood, and he that defraudeth the laborer of his hire, are brothers|Qui effundit sanguinem, et qui fraudem facit mercenario, fratres sunt]]. It could also be said that, since the tribe of Levi could join in marriage with the other tribes of Israel, this Menelaus was perhaps of the tribe of Benjamin on one parent's side, especially the mother's, and so Simon's brother.

paras.t: At ille, videlicet Menelaus, commendatus regi Antiocho ab ejus ministris, qui ad hoc faciendum erant (ut creditur) a Menelao per dona inducti, quum magnificasset faciem potestatis ejus, id est, regem et ejus potentiam magnifice commendasset, in semetipsum retorsit summum sacerdotium, id est, procuravit illud sibi a rege donari ambitiose, simoniace, fraudulenter. Acceptisque a rege mandatis quid ageret, et ut pro pontifice susciperetur, venit, etc. Et Jason, qui proprium fratrem captivaverat, id est, causa fuit quod Onias seorsum reclusit se, ut infra habetur, in Ammanitem, id est regionem Ammonitarum, expulsus est. Huc enim sacerdotii principatu privatus aufugit. De pecuniis vero regi promissis Menelaus nihil agebat, id est, eas Antiocho non persolvit, quum exactionem faceret, id est, persolvi eas regi exigeret, Sostratus, sicut et vectigalia persolvi exegit; qui Sostratus arci quæ fuit in monte Sion, præsidebat. Quam ob causam utrique, videlicet Menelaus et Sostratus, ad regem sunt evocati, ad reddendum rationem, cur Menelaus regi non solvit quod debuit. Et comperto quod Menelaus fuit in culpa, amotus est a sacerdotio, id est pontificatu, succedente Lysimacho fratre suo, qui de semine Aaron fuit, ut probabilius reputatur.
paras.en: [[4:24|But he|At ille]], namely Menelaus, [[4:24|being recommended to the king|commendatus regi]] Antiochus by his ministers, who had been induced to do this (as is believed) by Menelaus with gifts, [[4:24|when he had magnified the appearance of his power|quum magnificasset faciem potestatis ejus]], that is, had magnificently praised the king and his might, [[4:24|got the high priesthood for himself|in semetipsum retorsit summum sacerdotium]] [literally 'turned the high priesthood back upon himself'], that is, procured that it be given him by the king, ambitiously, simoniacally, fraudulently. [[4:25|So having received the king's mandate|Acceptisque a rege mandatis]] as to what he should do, and that he should be received as high priest, [[4:25|he returned|venit]], etc. [[4:26|Then Jason, who had undermined his own brother|Et Jason, qui proprium fratrem captivaverat]] [*captivaverat*, literally 'had taken captive'], that is, was the cause that Onias shut himself away apart, as is told below, [[4:26|was driven out|expulsus est]] [[4:26|into the country of the Ammonites|in Ammanitem]] (*Ammanites*, that is, the region of the Ammonites). For he fled there, deprived of the leadership of the priesthood. As for [[4:27|the money he had promised to the king|De pecuniis vero regi promissis]], Menelaus [[4:27|took no care|nihil agebat]], that is, did not pay it to Antiochus, when Sostratus [[4:27|called for it|quum exactionem faceret]], that is, required it to be paid to the king, as he also required the taxes to be paid; for this Sostratus was in charge of the castle that was on mount Sion. This is why [[4:28|they were both|utrique]], namely Menelaus and Sostratus, [[4:28|called before the king|ad regem sunt evocati]], to give account why Menelaus had not paid the king what he owed. And when it was found that Menelaus was at fault, he [[4:29|was removed from the priesthood|amotus est a sacerdotio]], that is, the high priesthood, [[4:29|Lysimachus, his brother, succeeding|succedente Lysimacho fratre suo]], who was of the seed of Aaron, as is more probably held.

paras.t: Et quum hæc agerentur, contigit Tharsenses et Mallotas, id est cives ab urbibus suis sic nuncupatos, seditionem movere contra regem suum Antiochum, a quo videbantur contempti, eo quod Antiochi regis concubinæ dono essent dati, id est ob hoc, quod Antiochus dedit eos pro munere suæ concubinæ, ut essent sub illius dominatione. Festinanter itaque rex venit sedare illos, ne et concubinam suam contristaret, aut subditos contra se acrius provocaret, relicto suffecto, id est substituto, uno ex comitibus, id est principibus seu sociis sui regiminis, Andronico in Antiochia, ex qua venit sedare præfatos. Ratus autem, id est existimans, Menelaus accepisse se tempus opportunum procurandi interfectionem Oniæ, rege absente, aurea quædam vasa de templo furatus (quod sacrilegium fuit) donavit Andronico, ut ejus sibi amicitiam procuraret, sicque per eum obtineret Oniam occidi.
paras.en: [[4:30|When these things were in doing, it fell out that they of Tharsus, and Mallos|Et quum hæc agerentur, contigit Tharsenses et Mallotas]], that is, citizens so named from their cities, [[4:30|raised a sedition|seditionem movere]] against their king Antiochus, by whom they seemed to be slighted, [[4:30|because they were given for a gift to Antiochus, the king's concubine|eo quod Antiochi regis concubinæ dono essent dati]] [Denis's text reads 'to the concubine of King Antiochus'; the Vulgate names her, Antiochis], that is, because Antiochus gave them as a present to his concubine, to be under her dominion. [[4:31|The king, therefore, went in all haste to appease them|Festinanter itaque rex venit sedare illos]] [the words of this lemma are damaged in the scan and are given as in the Vulgate], lest he should both grieve his concubine and provoke his subjects more sharply against himself, leaving, [[4:31|for his deputy|relicto suffecto]], that is, as his substitute, [[4:31|one of his nobles|uno ex comitibus]], that is, one of the princes or companions of his government, [[4:31|Andronicus|Andronico]], at Antioch, from which he came to quiet the aforesaid. [[4:32|Then Menelaus supposing|Ratus autem]], that is, thinking, [[4:32|that he had found a convenient time|Menelaus accepisse se tempus opportunum]] to bring about the slaying of Onias while the king was away, [[4:32|having stolen certain vessels of gold out of the temple|aurea quædam vasa de templo furatus]] (which was sacrilege), [[4:32|gave them to Andronicus|donavit Andronico]], to win his friendship for himself, and so through him to have Onias killed.

paras.t: Qui Andronicus quum venisset ad Oniam, et suasisset ei de asylo procedere, id est, de loco illo in quo tutus fuit, nec poterat lædi, descendere, statim eum peremit. Propter quod, id est ob tam immanissimam impietatem, indignati sunt Judæi et Græci in Antiochia exsistentes, atque regresso regi conquesti sunt: qui Deo instigante usque ad lacrimas condoluit interfecto; et Andronicum purpura exutum, veluti degradatum, fecit occidi.
paras.en: [[4:34|And he went to Onias|Qui Andronicus quum venisset ad Oniam]], and [[4:34|persuaded him to come forth out of the sanctuary|et suasisset ei de asylo procedere]], that is, to come down from that place in which he was safe and could not be harmed, [[4:34|and immediately slew him|statim eum peremit]]. [[4:35|For which cause|Propter quod]], that is, on account of so monstrous an impiety, the Jews and the Greeks living at Antioch were indignant, and complained to the king on his return: and he, at God's prompting, grieved even to tears for the slain man; and [[4:38|he commanded Andronicus to be stripped of his purple|et Andronicum purpura exutum]], as though degraded, and had him put to death.

paras.t: Multis autem sacrilegiis, id est rerum sacrarum abusionibus, a Lysimacho in templo commissis, et divulgata fama de tantis criminibus, congregata est multitudo Judæorum vitia Lysimachi abominantium, adversus Lysimachum, multo jam auro exportato de templo per Lysimachum, illud in usus proprios convertentem. Turbis autem insurgentibus contra Lysimachum, Lysimachus armatis fere tribus millibus qui erant de parte ipsius, iniquis manibus, id est adjutorio impiorum illorum, uti cœpit. Et multi quidem vulnerati de adjutoribus Lysimachi, quidam autem et prostrati, id est occisi, omnes vero residui de ejus exercitu, in fugam conversi sunt; ipsum etiam sacrilegum Lysimachum, circa ærarium, scilicet extra templum, interfecerunt.
paras.en: [[4:39|Now when many sacrileges|Multis autem sacrilegiis]], that is, abuses of sacred things, [[4:39|had been committed by Lysimachus in the temple|a Lysimacho in templo commissis]], [[4:39|and the rumour of it was spread abroad|et divulgata fama]] of such great crimes, [[4:39|the multitude gathered themselves together|congregata est multitudo]] of the Jews who abhorred the vices of Lysimachus, [[4:39|against Lysimachus|adversus Lysimachum]], [[4:39|a great quantity of gold being already carried away|multo jam auro exportato]] from the temple by Lysimachus, who was turning it to his own uses. [[4:40|Wherefore the multitude making an insurrection|Turbis autem insurgentibus]] against Lysimachus, [[4:40|Lysimachus armed about three thousand men|Lysimachus armatis fere tribus millibus]] who were of his party, [[4:40|and began to use violence|iniquis manibus]] [literally 'to use wicked hands'], that is, the help of those wicked men. [[4:42|And many of them were wounded|Et multi quidem vulnerati]] among the helpers of Lysimachus, [[4:42|and some struck down to the ground|quidam autem et prostrati]], that is, slain, [[4:42|but all|omnes vero]] the rest of his force [[4:42|were put to flight|in fugam conversi sunt]]; [[4:42|and as for the sacrilegious fellow himself|ipsum etiam sacrilegum]] Lysimachus, [[4:42|they slew him|interfecerunt]] [[4:42|beside the treasury|circa ærarium]], that is, outside the temple.

paras.t: De his ergo cœpit judicium adversus Menelaum agitari, id est, Judæi cœperunt Menelao hæc crimina et sacrilegia Lysimachi imputare, quia consilio Menelai facta fuerunt. Et quum venisset rex Tyrum, ad ipsum detulerunt negotium missi viri tres a senioribus Judæorum: qui tres accusaverunt Menelaum coram rege. Et quum superaretur Menelaus, id est, objectionibus et accusationibus contra se factis respondere non posset, promisit Ptolemæo, amico seu consiliario regis, multas pecunias ad suadendum regi, id est, ut persuaderet Antiocho Menelaum reum non esse, sed accusatores ipsius. Et ad sententiam deduxit, id est, Ptolemæus ille iniquus induxit regem ad proferendum sententiam pro Menelao. Miseros autem, id est accusatores Menelai miserabiliter criminatos et circumventos, qui etiam si apud Scythas, id est homines sic vocatos, qui crudeles irrationabilesque dicuntur, causam dixissent, id est, negotium contra Menelaum proposuissent, innocentes judicarentur a Scythis, quia apertissime justa fuit eorum causa; hos morte damnavit Antiochus.
paras.en: [[4:43|Now concerning these matters, an accusation was laid against Menelaus|De his ergo cœpit judicium adversus Menelaum agitari]], that is, the Jews began to impute to Menelaus these crimes and sacrileges of Lysimachus, because they had been done by Menelaus's counsel. [[4:44|And when the king was come to Tyre|Et quum venisset rex Tyrum]], [[4:44|three men were sent from the ancients to plead the cause before him|ad ipsum detulerunt negotium missi viri tres a senioribus]] of the Jews: and these three accused Menelaus before the king. [[4:45|But Menelaus being convicted|Et quum superaretur Menelaus]], that is, being unable to answer the objections and accusations made against him, [[4:45|promised Ptolemee|promisit Ptolemæo]], the king's friend or counsellor, [[4:45|much money to persuade the king|multas pecunias ad suadendum regi]], that is, to persuade Antiochus that not Menelaus was guilty, but his accusers. And he [[4:46|brought him to be of another mind|Et ad sententiam deduxit]] [Denis reads *ad sententiam*, 'brought him to a sentence', where the Vulgate has *a sententia*, 'from his opinion'], that is, that wicked Ptolemee brought the king to pronounce sentence for Menelaus. As for [[4:47|those poor men|Miseros autem]], that is, the accusers of Menelaus, pitiably charged and circumvented, who, even if [[4:47|before Scythians|apud Scythas]] (that is, men so called, who are said to be cruel and unreasoning) [[4:47|they had pleaded their cause|causam dixissent]], that is, had set out their case against Menelaus, [[4:47|should have been judged innocent|innocentes judicarentur]] by the Scythians, since their cause was most plainly just: these [[4:47|were condemned to death|hos morte damnavit]] by Antiochus.

paras.t: Cito ergo injustam pœnam dederunt, id est, passi sunt (juxta quem modum loquendi ait Apostolus: Qui pœnas dabunt in interitu æternas), qui pro civitate Jerusalem et populo Judæorum, et sacris vasis templi, causam prosecuti sunt contra Menelaum coram rege. Menelaus autem propter eorum qui in potentia erant avaritiam, id est propter cupiditatem principum Antiochi, quibus munera contulit Menelaus, permanebat in potestate, id est sacerdotii principatu.
paras.en: So they [[4:48|did soon suffer unjust punishment|Cito ergo injustam pœnam dederunt]] (*dederunt*, literally 'gave', that is, suffered; in which manner of speaking the Apostle says: [[2 Thess 1:9|Who shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction|Qui pœnas dabunt in interitu æternas]]), [[4:48|that persecuted the cause for the city, and for the people, and the sacred vessels|qui pro civitate Jerusalem et populo Judæorum, et sacris vasis templi, causam prosecuti sunt]] against Menelaus before the king. [[4:50|And so through the covetousness of them that were in power|Menelaus autem propter eorum qui in potentia erant avaritiam]], that is, through the greed of the princes of Antiochus, on whom Menelaus bestowed gifts, [[4:50|Menelaus continued in authority|permanebat in potestate]], that is, in the leadership of the priesthood.

paras.t: Ecce quanta fiunt in hoc mundo facinora, et qualiter justi ac pii ab impiis opprimuntur, ipsique impii prosperantur ad tempus, secundum dispensationem secretorum judiciorum Altissimi. Propter quod Isaias dicit: Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet in corde suo; et viri misericordiæ colliguntur, et non est qui intelligat. Quæ res interdum movet fideles in admirationem, juxta illud Habacuc primo: Quare, Domine, respicis contemptores, et taces, conculcante impio justiorem se? Propter hoc lacerata est lex, quia impius prævalet adversus justum. Propterea egreditur judicium perversum. Sed si respicimus ad futuri sæculi retributiones, atque ad ordinem infinitæ sapientiæ providentiæque Dei, admiratio cessat.
paras.en: Behold how great crimes are done in this world, and how the just and godly are oppressed by the wicked, and the wicked themselves prosper for a time, according to the dispensation of the secret judgments of the Most High. Wherefore Isaias says: [[Is 57:1|The just perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart, and men of mercy are taken away, because there is none that understandeth|Justus perit, et non est qui recogitet in corde suo; et viri misericordiæ colliguntur, et non est qui intelligat]]. This thing sometimes moves the faithful to wonder, according to that of Habacuc, chapter one: [[Hab 1:13|Why lookest thou upon them that do unjust things, and holdest thy peace when the wicked devoureth the man that is more just than himself?|Quare, Domine, respicis contemptores, et taces, conculcante impio justiorem se?]] [Denis's wording, 'Why, O Lord, dost thou look upon the despisers … while the wicked treads down', differs a little from the Vulgate's] [[Hab 1:4|Therefore the law is torn in pieces|Propter hoc lacerata est lex]], [[Hab 1:4|because the wicked prevaileth against the just, therefore wrong judgment goeth forth|quia impius prævalet adversus justum. Propterea egreditur judicium perversum]]. But if we look to the rewards of the world to come, and to the order of the infinite wisdom and providence of God, the wonder ceases.

5.title: Declaratio capituli quinti: Eodem tempore Antiochus secundam profectionem paravit in Ægyptum.
5.title_en: Explanation of the fifth chapter: At the same time Antiochus prepared for a second journey into Egypt.

paras.t: Gravissima persecutio Judæorum per Antiochum facta hic recitatur. Præmittitur tamen impugnatio Jasonis, et expugnatio ejus. Eodem tempore Antiochus secundam profectionem paravit in Ægyptum, id est, disposuit se ad ingrediendum et expugnandum Ægyptum altera vice. Qualiter autem bis intravit Ægyptum, in expositione primi libri narratum est.
paras.en: A most grievous persecution of the Jews carried out by Antiochus is recounted here. First, however, comes the attack of Jason, and his overthrow. [[5:1|At the same time Antiochus prepared for a second journey into Egypt|Eodem tempore Antiochus secundam profectionem paravit in Ægyptum]], that is, he made ready to enter and conquer Egypt a second time. How he entered Egypt twice was told in the exposition of the first book[[1 Mach 1:17||]] [the margin gives I Mach. i, with a second figure that reads 30; Antiochus's entry into Egypt is told at 1 Mach 1:17–21].

paras.t: Consequenter describitur, qualiter Deus futuram Jerosolymitarum prostrationem præmonstravit, per visiones et signa admonens illos ad vitæ correctionem. Contigit autem per universam Jerosolymorum civitatem videri a civibus ejus, diebus quadraginta, certis horis ac quibusdam diebus infra spatium quadraginta dierum, quamvis, ut probabile est, non singulis illis diebus, per aera equites discurrentes, auratas stolas, id est vestes quæ super arma indui solent, habentes; et cursus equorum per ordinem digestos, id est, ordinate dispositos secundum bellicam artem; et congressiones fieri cominus, id est de prope prælia exerceri; et scutorum motus, qui in bellis variis modis moventur, et ictibus opponuntur ad tuendum se; et galeatorum multitudinem, id est plurimos hominum galeas habentium, gladiis districtis, etc., id est multipliciter agitatis, extentis, retractis. Denique hæc fiebant in aere ministerio angelorum bonorum sive malorum. Sic et S. Gregorius in homilia prima refert se igneas acies vidisse in cœlo, antequam percuteretur Italia gladio. Similiter ante eversionem Jerusalem a Romanis, signa varia præcesserunt et visa fuerunt, quæ hic partim tanguntur in textu, pleniusque describuntur a Josepho libro de Judaico bello. Quapropter omnes habitatores Jerusalem rogabant in bonum monstra converti, id est, signa illa monstratione digna, bonum aliquid præsignare, videlicet Judæorum victoriam: quorum tamen significabant ruinam.
paras.en: Next it is described how God foreshowed the coming overthrow of the people of Jerusalem, warning them by visions and signs to amend their lives. [[5:2|And it came to pass, that through the whole city of Jerusalem|Contigit autem per universam Jerosolymorum civitatem]] there were seen by its citizens, [[5:2|for the space of forty days|diebus quadraginta]] (at certain hours and on certain days within the space of forty days, though, as is probable, not on every one of those days), [[5:2|horsemen running in the air|per aera equites discurrentes]], [[5:2|in gilded raiment|auratas stolas]], that is, in the garments that are usually worn over armour; [[5:3|And horses set in order by ranks|et cursus equorum per ordinem digestos]], that is, drawn up in order according to the art of war; [[5:3|running one against another|et congressiones fieri cominus]], that is, battles fought at close quarters; [[5:3|with the shakings of shields|et scutorum motus]], which in battle are moved in various ways and set against the blows for defence; [[5:3|and a multitude of men in helmets|et galeatorum multitudinem]], that is, a great many men wearing helmets, [[5:3|with drawn swords|gladiis districtis]], etc., that is, brandished in many ways, thrust out, drawn back. These things, then, were done in the air by the ministry of angels, good or bad. So too St Gregory, in his first homily [on the Gospels], relates that he saw fiery battle lines in the sky before Italy was struck by the sword. Likewise before the destruction of Jerusalem by the Romans various signs went before and were seen, which are partly touched on here in the text and are described more fully by Josephus in his book On the Jewish War [the margin gives De bello Jud., with a book and chapter that cannot be read clearly]. [[5:4|Wherefore all men|Quapropter omnes]] dwelling in Jerusalem [[5:4|prayed that these prodigies might turn to good|rogabant in bonum monstra converti]], that is, that those signs, worthy to be shown forth [Denis derives monstra, 'prodigies', from monstrare, 'to show'], might foreshow something good, namely victory for the Jews: whereas what they signified was their ruin.

paras.t: Sed quum falsus rumor exisset, quasi vita excessisset, id est, quod obisset, Antiochus, assumptis Jason non minus mille viris, repente aggressus est civitatem Jerusalem, volens opprimere Menelaum, a quo fuit privatus pontificali officio, et illud recuperare, putans regem obisse, a quo erat depositus. Jason vero non parcebat civibus suis in cæde, id est, sine misericordia eos crudeliter interfecit; nec cogitabat prosperitatem adversus cognatos, id est, circa Jerosolymitas quorum multi erant consanguinei sui, non cogitavit prospera, sed adversa eis infligere; malum esse maximum, id est præcipuum damnum, arbitrans, hostium, et non civium se trophæa capturum, id est obtinere victoriam de vere hostibus suis, et non potius de suis concivibus, quos magis oderat quam gentiles vere inimicos et adversarios suos. Propter quod potius affectavit Judæos quam gentiles occidere. Et profugus iterum abiit in Ammonitem, id est in regionem Ammonitarum.
paras.en: [[5:5|Now when there was gone forth a false rumour as though Antiochus had been dead|Sed quum falsus rumor exisset, quasi vita excessisset]], that is, that he had died, [[5:5|Jason taking with him no fewer than a thousand men, suddenly assaulted the city|assumptis Jason non minus mille viris, repente aggressus est civitatem]] of Jerusalem, wishing to crush Menelaus, by whom he had been deprived of the high priest's office, and to recover it, thinking that the king who had deposed him was dead. [[5:6|But Jason slew his countrymen without mercy|Jason vero non parcebat civibus suis in cæde]], that is, he killed them cruelly and without pity; [[5:6|not considering that prosperity against one's own kindred|nec cogitabat prosperitatem adversus cognatos]], that is, toward the people of Jerusalem, many of whom were his blood relations, he thought not to bring prosperity upon them, but adversity; [[5:6|is a very great evil|malum esse maximum]], that is, the chief loss, [[5:6|thinking they had been enemies, and not citizens, whom he conquered|arbitrans, hostium, et non civium se trophæa capturum]] [Denis takes the words together thus: thinking it the greatest evil, the chief loss, to win trophies over enemies and not over citizens], that is, to gain the victory over his true enemies and not rather over his own fellow citizens, whom he hated more than the Gentiles, who were truly his foes and adversaries. For this reason he was more eager to kill Jews than Gentiles. [[5:7|and fled again into the country of the Ammonites|Et profugus iterum abiit in Ammonitem]], that is, into the region of the Ammonites.

paras.t: Ad ultimum, [in] exitium, id est exterminium sui, conclusus ab Areta Arabum tyranno, omnibus odiosus, ut refuga legum, id est apostata a Mosaicis legibus, peregre periit, Lacedæmonas, id est ad regionem, urbem seu populum Lacedæmoniacum, profectus quasi pro cognatione refugium habiturus, id est tanquam defendendus et pie tractandus ab illis veluti a cognatis. Lacedæmonii etenim erant Spartiatæ, nati de semine Abrahæ, ut dictum est plenius in primo libro. Et qui insepultos multos abjecerat, quos occidit, ipse et illamentatus, id est non deploratus, et insepultus abjicitur, sepultura neque peregrina, id est alterius terræ monumento, neque patrio sepulcro participans. Unde elicitur, quod apud Spartiatas ejus pravitatem et apostasiam a lege noscentes, gratiam non invenit, sed occisus fuit ac insepultus abjectus.
paras.en: [[5:8|At the last|Ad ultimum]], [[5:8|for his destruction|exitium]], that is, his extermination, [[5:8|having been shut up by Aretas, the king of the Arabians|conclusus ab Areta Arabum tyranno]], [[5:8|hated by all men, as a forsaker of the laws|omnibus odiosus, ut refuga legum]], that is, an apostate from the laws of Moses, [[5:9|perished in a strange land|peregre periit]], [[5:9|going to Lacedemon|Lacedæmonas]], that is, to the region, city or people of Lacedemon, [[5:9|as if for kindred sake he should have refuge there|profectus quasi pro cognatione refugium habiturus]], that is, as one who would be defended and kindly treated by them, as by kinsmen. For the Lacedemonians were Spartans, born of the seed of Abraham, as was said more fully in the first book[[1 Mach 12:21||]] [the margin's figures read xu, 31; the passage is 1 Mach 12:21]. [[5:10|But he that had cast out many unburied|Et qui insepultos multos abjecerat]], whom he had killed, [[5:10|was himself cast forth both unlamented|ipse et illamentatus]], that is, not mourned, [[5:10|and unburied|et insepultus abjicitur]], [[5:10|neither having foreign burial|sepultura neque peregrina]], that is, a tomb in another land, [[5:10|nor being partaker of the sepulchre of his fathers|neque patrio sepulcro participans]]. Hence it is gathered that among the Spartans, who knew his wickedness and his apostasy from the law, he found no favour, but was slain and cast out unburied.

paras.t: His ita gestis, suspicatus est rex Antiochus societatem deserturos Judæos, id est recessuros a sua obedientia, communione ac tributorum persolutione: quod impiissimus Menelaus sibi forsitan persuasit per scripta seu alio modo. Crevit namque in malitia, et ad insidias civium, ut in fine præcedentis habetur capituli. Et ob hoc rex profectus ex Ægypto: quia Romani per legatos jusserunt ei ab Ægyptiorum impugnatione recedere; efferatis, id est crudelibus, animis, civitatem quidem Jerusalem armis cepit. Habitatores enim urbis inter se discordes, ei non multum restiterunt: imo faventes ei, intromiserunt eum. Tuncque fecit per milites suos inhumanissimam et atrocissimam stragem in civitate, ut fertur in textu qui planus est.
paras.en: [[5:11|Now when these things were done|His ita gestis]], [[5:11|the king suspected that the Jews would forsake the alliance|suspicatus est rex Antiochus societatem deserturos Judæos]], that is, would withdraw from obedience to him, from fellowship with him and from paying him tribute: of which the most wicked Menelaus perhaps persuaded him, by letters or in some other way. For he grew [[2 Mach 4:50|in malice to the betraying of the citizens|in malitia, et ad insidias civium]], as is found at the end of the preceding chapter. [[5:11|whereupon departing out of Egypt|Et ob hoc rex profectus ex Ægypto]], because the Romans by their envoys ordered him to give up his attack on the Egyptians, [[5:11|with a furious|efferatis]], that is, cruel, [[5:11|mind|animis]], [[5:11|he took the city by force of arms|civitatem quidem Jerusalem armis cepit]]. For the inhabitants of the city, being at odds among themselves, did not resist him much: nay, favouring him, they let him in. And then by his soldiers he made a most inhuman and atrocious slaughter in the city, as is told in the text, which is plain.

paras.t: Ausus est etiam intrare templum universæ terræ sanctius, id est sacratius fanis et templis gentilium, utpote vero Deo consecratum; et scelestis, id est vitiosis, manibus sumens sancta, vasa templi, quæ ab aliis regibus et civitatibus, id est civitatum quarumdam rectoribus, erant posita, id est data, et per ministros templi collocata, ad ornatum loci et gloriam, ut Deo serviretur in eis. Cyrus enim rex Persarum, et Darius ac Artaxerxes atque Antiochus Magnus, et filius ejus Seleucus, rectores quoque nonnulli urbium aliquarum, exemplo regum suorum multa pretiosa decoraque vasa transmiserunt ad templum Jerusalem, ut partim ex dictis, et ex Esdra patescit. Contrectabat indigne, id est irreverenter, tanquam vasa communia, et contaminabat, applicando ea sacrilege usibus suis ac alienis.
paras.en: [[5:15|he presumed also to enter into the temple, the most holy in all the world|Ausus est etiam intrare templum universæ terræ sanctius]], that is, more sacred than the shrines and temples of the Gentiles, since it was consecrated to the true God; [[5:16|And taking in his wicked|et scelestis]], that is, vicious, [[5:16|hands the holy vessels|manibus sumens sancta]], the vessels of the temple, [[5:16|which were given by other kings and cities|quæ ab aliis regibus et civitatibus]], that is, by the rulers of certain cities, which had been placed, that is, given, and set in place by the ministers of the temple, [[5:16|for the ornament and the glory of the place|ad ornatum loci et gloriam]], that God might be served with them. For Cyrus king of the Persians, and Darius and Artaxerxes, and Antiochus the Great and his son Seleucus, and also some rulers of certain cities, following the example of their kings, sent many precious and beautiful vessels to the temple of Jerusalem, as is evident partly from what has been said[[2 Mach 3:2||]] and from Esdras[[1 Esd 1:7||]][[1 Esd 6:5||]][[1 Esd 7:15||]] [the margin here can hardly be read; it seems to give I Esdr. i, 7; vi, 5, 8; vii, 15, which fit, and a reference to the preceding chapters of this book]. [[5:16|he unworthily handled|Contrectabat indigne]], that is, irreverently, as if they were common vessels, [[5:16|and profaned them|et contaminabat]], putting them sacrilegiously to his own uses and those of others.

paras.t: Ita alienatus mente, id est vitiis et passionibus obscuratus, Antiochus, non considerabat quod propter peccata habitantium, civitati Dominus modicum fuit iratus, permittens eam ac templum ipsius sic profanari ad breve tempus, et citra condignum. Et hoc probat per castigationem Heliodoro inflictam, ut supra habetur.
paras.en: [[5:17|Thus Antiochus going astray in mind|Ita alienatus mente]], that is, darkened by vices and passions, [[5:17|did not consider|Antiochus, non considerabat]] [[5:17|that God was angry for a while, because of the sins of the inhabitants of the city|quod propter peccata habitantium, civitati Dominus modicum fuit iratus]], permitting it and its temple to be thus profaned for a short time, and less than it deserved. And he proves this by the chastisement inflicted on Heliodorus, as is found above[[2 Mach 3:25||]] [the margin note here cannot be read; Heliodorus is scourged at 2 Mach 3:25–27].

paras.t: Verum non propter locum gentem, sed propter gentem locum Dominus elegit. Nam minus principale ordinatur ad principale. Ideo locus ordinatur ad habitatores suos, et propter illorum profectum eligitur, non econtra. Ideoque et ipse locus, videlicet templum et civitas, factus est particeps malorum pœnalium, id est punitionum, populi sui, ita quod populus puniebatur in profanatione et contemptu loci sui et templi; postea fiet socius, id est participator, et bonorum, id est prosperitatum. Ista tamen est impropria locutio, quoniam inter rationalia et irrationalia ac inanimata, non est proprie loquendo societas. Et qui derelictus est in ira, id est justa ultione, Omnipotentis, iterum in magna Dei reconciliatione cum summa gloria exaltabitur: quod fuit impletum aliquo modo, quando Judas et fratres ejus templum recuperaverunt, purgaverunt et ornaverunt: sicut in primo libro et infra quoque habetur; plenius autem in Christi adventu, oblatione, prædicatione et miraculosa operatione in templo. Tunc enim impletum est quod Aggeus prædixit: Magna erit gloria domus hujus novissimæ magis quam primæ.
paras.en: [[5:19|But God did not choose the people for the place's sake, but the place for the people's sake|Verum non propter locum gentem, sed propter gentem locum Dominus elegit]]. For the less principal is ordered to the principal; so the place is ordered to its inhabitants, and is chosen for their good, not the other way round. [[5:20|And, therefore, the place also itself|Ideoque et ipse locus]], namely the temple and the city, [[5:20|was made partaker of the evils|factus est particeps malorum]] of penalty, that is, of the punishments, [[5:20|of the people|populi sui]], so that the people was punished in the profanation and contempt of its place and temple; [[5:20|but afterwards shall communicate|postea fiet socius]], that is, shall share, [[5:20|in the good things thereof|et bonorum]], that is, in its prosperity. This, however, is an improper way of speaking, since between rational beings and irrational and lifeless things there is, properly speaking, no fellowship. [[5:20|and as it was forsaken in the wrath|Et qui derelictus est in ira]], that is, the just vengeance, [[5:20|of Almighty God|Omnipotentis]], [[5:20|shall be exalted again with great glory, when the great Lord shall be reconciled|iterum in magna Dei reconciliatione cum summa gloria exaltabitur]]: which was fulfilled in some manner when Judas and his brethren recovered, cleansed and adorned the temple, as is found in the first book[[1 Mach 4:36||]] and below also[[2 Mach 10:1||]]; but more fully in the coming of Christ, his offering, his preaching and his miraculous works in the temple. For then was fulfilled what Aggeus foretold: [[Agg 2:10|Great shall be the glory of this last house more than of the first|Magna erit gloria domus hujus novissimæ magis quam primæ]] [the margin note here is unreadable].

paras.t: Igitur Antiochus mille et octingentis ablatis de templo talentis, velociter Antiochiam regressus est, æstimans se præ superbia terram ad navigandum, etc. Quod per hyperbolen dictum est, ad insinuandum indicibilem impiissimi illius elationem.
paras.en: [[5:21|So when Antiochus had taken away out of the temple a thousand and eight hundred talents, he went back in all haste to Antioch|Igitur Antiochus mille et octingentis ablatis de templo talentis, velociter Antiochiam regressus est]], [[5:21|thinking through pride that he might now make the land navigable|æstimans se præ superbia terram ad navigandum]], etc. This is said by hyperbole [that is, deliberate exaggeration], to convey the unspeakable pride of that most wicked man.

paras.t: Reliquit autem præpositos, id est quosdam de principibus suis, ad affligendum gentem Judæorum: Jerosolymis quidem Philippum; in Garizim loco Samariæ, Andronicum, non illum quem præcedenti capitulo legitur in Antiochia occidisse. Porro de hac templi spoliatione et civitatis Jerusalem afflictione, sanctique loci et vasorum ejus contaminatione, plenius dictum est in primo libro.
paras.en: [[5:22|He left also governors|Reliquit autem præpositos]], that is, certain of his princes, [[5:22|to afflict the people|ad affligendum gentem]] of the Jews: [[5:22|at Jerusalem, Philip|Jerosolymis quidem Philippum]]; [[5:23|And in Gazarim|in Garizim]], a place in Samaria, [[5:23|Andronicus|Andronicum]]: not the one who, as we read in the preceding chapter, did the killing at Antioch[[2 Mach 4:38||]] [the margin gives II Mach. iv, 38, where that Andronicus is put to death; his killing of Onias is at 4:34]. Moreover, of this plundering of the temple and affliction of the city of Jerusalem, and the defiling of the holy place and its vessels, more has been said in the first book[[1 Mach 1:23||]].

paras.t: Quumque oppositus esset contra Judæos, etc. Hoc ipsum scriptum est in primo libro, et est sensus: Quum Antiochus firmasset suum propositum ad persequendum Judæos, misit odiosum principem Apollonium cum exercitu, etc. Ista historia in primo libro habetur, quamvis nomen Apollonii ibi non exprimatur: quod tamen in primo libro est expressum. Et tunc, scilicet sabbato, feriatis Judæis, id est ab operibus cessantibus, arma capere suis præcepit: non quasi ad impugnandum Judæos, sed quasi ad exercendum hastiludia torneamentave aliqua: quia subjungitur, Omnesque simul Judæos, qui ad spectaculum processerant, trucidavit. Unde elicitur, quod Judæi non observabant se ob armationem prætactam.
paras.en: [[5:24|And whereas he was set against the Jews|Quumque oppositus esset contra Judæos]], etc. This very thing is written in the first book[[1 Mach 1:30||]], and the sense is: when Antiochus had settled his purpose to persecute the Jews, [[5:24|he sent that hateful prince, Apollonius, with an army|misit odiosum principem Apollonium cum exercitu]], etc. This story is found in the first book[[1 Mach 1:30||]], though the name of Apollonius is not given there; it is, however, given elsewhere in the first book[[1 Mach 3:10||]]. [[5:25|and then|Et tunc]], namely on the sabbath, [[5:25|the Jews keeping holiday|feriatis Judæis]], that is, resting from their work, [[5:25|he commanded his men to take arms|arma capere suis præcepit]]: not as if to attack the Jews, but as if to hold some jousts or tournaments; for it is added: [[5:26|And he slew all that were come forth|Omnesque simul Judæos, qui ad spectaculum processerant, trucidavit]] [Denis's Latin has 'all the Jews together who had come out to the spectacle'; the Douay-Rheims reads 'to flee']. Hence it is gathered that the Jews did not guard themselves on account of the arming just mentioned.

paras.t: Judas autem Machabæus qui decimus erat. Judas hic dicitur decimus, non in ordine fratrum, inter quos tertius fuit, ut patet primo libro, sed in ordine summorum pontificum: non tamen incipiendo computationem pontificum ab Aaron, inter quem et Judam multo plures fuerunt, sed a principio regni Græcorum. Circa hæc scribit quidam: Regnum Græcorum, ut scribunt quidam expositores, incepit a Seleuco, qui in Syria successit Alexandro Magno. Et tunc, scilicet tempore Seleuci, summus sacerdos fuit Onias Jaddi filius, qui, secundum hoc dictum, fuit primus pontifex; Simon justus, secundus; Eleazarus Oniæ filius, tertius; quartus, Manasses Eleazari avunculus; quintus, Onias Simonis justi filius; sextus, Simon Oniæ filius; septimus, Onias hujus Simonis filius, quem occidit Andronicus; octavus Jason; nonus, Menelaus; decimus, Judas Machabæus. Hoc accipitur de glossa Rabani, quæ sumpta est ex dictis Josephi. Sed videtur deficere in duobus: Primo, quia Menelao successit Lysimachus. Et sic, qua ratione numeratur Jason et Menelaus, numeraretur et iste Lysimachus decimo loco, et non Judas. Secundo deficit, quia ponit regnum Græcorum incipere a Seleuco: quod tamen incepit ab Alexandro Magno.
paras.en: [[5:27|But Judas Machabeus, who was the tenth|Judas autem Machabæus qui decimus erat]]. Judas is here called the tenth, not in the order of the brothers, among whom he was the third, as is plain from the first book[[1 Mach 2:4||]], but in the order of the high priests: not, however, beginning the count of the high priests from Aaron, for between him and Judas there were many more, but from the beginning of the kingdom of the Greeks. On this a certain writer says: The kingdom of the Greeks, as certain expositors write, began from Seleucus, who succeeded Alexander the Great in Syria. And then, namely in the time of Seleucus, the high priest was Onias son of Jaddus, who by this account was the first pontiff; Simon the Just, the second; Eleazar son of Onias, the third; the fourth, Manasses, Eleazar's uncle; the fifth, Onias son of Simon the Just; the sixth, Simon son of Onias; the seventh, Onias son of this Simon, whom Andronicus killed; the eighth, Jason; the ninth, Menelaus; the tenth, Judas Machabeus. This is taken from the gloss of Rabanus, which is drawn from the sayings of Josephus. But it seems to fail on two points. First, because Lysimachus succeeded Menelaus; and so, by the same reasoning by which Jason and Menelaus are counted, this Lysimachus too would be counted in the tenth place, and not Judas. Secondly, it fails because it makes the kingdom of the Greeks begin from Seleucus, whereas it began from Alexander the Great.

paras.t: Circa hæc dico, quod redargutio ista nullius aut modici est valoris. Non enim putandum est, Rabanum ignorasse quod regnum Græcorum monarchicum seu imperiale ab Alexandro inceperit. Idcirco, dato quod dicat id, quod iste ei imponit, intelligendum est de regno Græco diviso: quo diviso in quatuor regna, primus post Alexandrum regnavit in Syria Seleucus pater Magni Antiochi, qui habuit filios duos, videlicet Seleucum et Antiochum Nobilem. Quod autem de Lysimacho objicitur, solveretur dicendo, quod modicissimo tempore præfuit, ita quod Menelaus cui ipse successerat, rursus ei occiso successit, ut patuit præcedenti capitulo: idcirco non numeratur. Nec verum est quod Judas ei successit. Nihilo minus dici potest, quod computatio ista ab Alexandro incipiat, cujus tempore pontifex Judæorum exstitit Jaddus: quo connumerato, aliisque præfatis, atque relictis Jasone et Menelao ac Lysimacho, qui illegitime ac pessime intraverunt, cultumque Dei dissipaverunt, et non exercuerunt, Judas est decimus, scilicet proximus post Oniam ab Andronico interfectum.
paras.en: On this I say that this objection is of no value, or of little. For it is not to be thought that Rabanus did not know that the monarchical or imperial kingdom of the Greeks began from Alexander. Therefore, granting that he says what this writer lays to his charge, it is to be understood of the Greek kingdom once divided: when it was divided into four kingdoms, the first to reign in Syria after Alexander was Seleucus, father of Antiochus the Great, who had two sons, namely Seleucus and Antiochus the Noble. As for the objection about Lysimachus, it would be answered by saying that he held office for a very short time, so that Menelaus, whom he had succeeded, succeeded again when he was slain, as appeared in the preceding chapter[[2 Mach 4:29||]][[2 Mach 4:42||]][[2 Mach 4:47||]][[2 Mach 4:50||]]: and so he is not counted. Nor is it true that Judas succeeded him. Nevertheless it can be said that this reckoning begins from Alexander, in whose time Jaddus was high priest of the Jews[[2 Esd 12:11||]] [the margin gives II Esdr. xii, 11, where he is called Jeddoa]: when he is counted with the others named, and Jason, Menelaus and Lysimachus are left out, who entered unlawfully and most wickedly and wrecked the worship of God rather than carrying it out, Judas is the tenth, namely the next after Onias, who was slain by Andronicus.

paras.t: Itaque Judas cum suis in desertum secesserat, scilicet cum patre suo ac fratribus, ut dictum est in primo libro, ibique inter feras vitam agebat; et fœni cibo vescentes Judas ac sui, [id est] rebus similibus fœno, utpote radicibus quibusdam et herbis ac fructibus terræ, quæ ibi poterant inveniri, ne participes essent coinquinationis, id est idololatriæ, transgressionisque legis Mosaicæ, ad quas Antiochus populum Judæorum coegit.
paras.en: So Judas with his men [[5:27|had withdrawn himself into a desert place|in desertum secesserat]], namely with his father and his brothers, as was said in the first book[[1 Mach 2:28||]], [[5:27|and there lived amongst wild beasts|ibique inter feras vitam agebat]]; [[5:27|and they continued feeding on herbs|et fœni cibo vescentes]], Judas and his men, that is, on things like hay [fœnum, 'hay' or 'grass'; the Douay-Rheims has 'herbs'], such as certain roots and herbs and fruits of the earth that could be found there, [[5:27|that they might not be partakers of the pollution|ne participes essent coinquinationis]], that is, of idolatry and of transgression of the law of Moses, to which Antiochus forced the people of the Jews.

6.title: Expositio capituli sexti: Sed non post multum temporis misit rex senem quemdam
6.title_en: Exposition of the sixth chapter: But not long after the king sent a certain old man

paras.t: Describuntur hic in speciali tribulationes per Antiochum et principes ejus inflictæ Judæis.
paras.en: Here are described in particular the tribulations inflicted on the Jews by Antiochus and his princes.

paras.t: Sed non post multum temporis, id est post breve tempus, misit rex senem quemdam Antiochenum tanquam authenticum, et cum eo alios quosdam, qui compelleret Judæos per minas et pœnas, ut se transferrent a patriis et Dei legibus, id est, leges divinas ab eorum patribus servatas, in patria sua relinquerent. Denique ista et multa subsequentia, dicta sunt atque exposita primo primi libri capitulo. Qui compelleret Judæos contaminare etiam quod in Jerosolymis erat templum: ita ut in eo sacrificarent Jovi, non vero Deo; et cognominare Jovis Olympii, id est, templum illud vocare templum Jovis, cognomento Olympii, a loco illo sublimi in quo colebatur; et in Garizim, prout erant hi qui locum inhabitabant, Jovis Hospitalis, id est, templum quod erat Deo constructum in monte Garizim in Samaria, cognominare templum Jovis Hospitalis, prout erant rogantes qui locum illum inhabitabant. Estque idem Jupiter, qui a diversis locis in quibus colebatur, diversa cognomina sortiebatur. Quocirca pensandum, quia ut Josephus refert, Manasses sacerdos, frater pontificis Judæorum, filiam Sanaballat Samaritani ac gentilis duxit uxorem. Propter quod prohibitus fuit ad altare accedere, nisi uxorem illam abjiceret: quam nolens relinquere, ad patrem uxoris Sanaballat est profectus, qui construxit ad ejus intuitum templum Deo in Garizim monte. Videntes autem Samaritani Judæos ab Antiocho propter cultum Dei ita oppressos, postulaverunt ab ipso, ut templum Dei inter ipsos situm, Jovi consecraretur, ne ab Antiocho aut ejus principibus instar Judæorum affligerentur.
paras.en: [[6:1|But not long after|Sed non post multum temporis]], that is, after a short time, [[6:1|the king sent a certain old man of Antioch|misit rex senem quemdam Antiochenum]], as a man of authority, and certain others with him, [[6:1|to compel the Jews|qui compelleret Judæos]] by threats and punishments [[6:1|to depart from the laws of their fathers and of God|ut se transferrent a patriis et Dei legibus]], that is, to forsake in their own country the divine laws kept by their fathers. These things, indeed, and many that follow, were told and explained in the first chapter of the first book[[1 Mach 1:44||]]. He was to compel the Jews [[6:2|to defile the temple that was in Jerusalem|contaminare etiam quod in Jerosolymis erat templum]], so that in it they should sacrifice to Jove and not to God; [[6:2|and to call it the temple of Jupiter Olympius|et cognominare Jovis Olympii]], that is, to call that temple the temple of Jove surnamed Olympius, from that lofty place in which he was worshipped; [[6:2|and that in Garazim|et in Garizim]], [[6:2|according as they were that inhabited the place|prout erant hi qui locum inhabitabant]], [[6:2|of Jupiter Hospitalis|Jovis Hospitalis]], that is, to call the temple which had been built to God on mount Garizim in Samaria the temple of Jove Hospitalis, as those who dwelt in that place asked. And it is the same Jupiter, who took different surnames from the different places in which he was worshipped. On this it is to be considered that, as Josephus relates, Manasses the priest, brother of the high priest of the Jews, took to wife the daughter of Sanaballat, a Samaritan and a gentile. For this he was forbidden to approach the altar unless he put that wife away; and being unwilling to leave her, he went off to his wife's father Sanaballat, who for his sake built a temple to God on mount Garizim. And the Samaritans, seeing the Jews so oppressed by Antiochus for the worship of God, asked him that the temple of God situated among them be consecrated to Jove, so that they should not be afflicted like the Jews by Antiochus or his princes.

paras.t: Pessima autem et universis Judæis fidelibus gravis erat malorum, id est persecutionum, imo et transgressionum, incursio, id est, boni Judæi incurrebant gravissimas calamitates et persecutiones ex sceleratissimis actibus servorum Antiochi. Nam templum luxuria et comessationibus gentium erat plenum, id est, vitia carnis exercebantur in templo a gentilibus ac Judæis ad paganismum conversis; sacratisque ædibus, scilicet atriis templi et domunculis sacerdotum in gyro templi constructis, mulieres impudicæ se ultro, id est sponte ac libere, ingerebant, intro ferentes, id est in loca sacra secum portantes, ea quæ non licebat ibi inferri, videlicet cibos ac potus lege prohibitos, aut sacrificia profana Jovi sacrificanda. Altare etiam holocausti plenum erat illicitis hostiis Jovis. Neque sabbata custodiebantur a majori parte Judæorum, neque dies solennes patrii servabantur, id est alia festa legalia a patribus olim servata in patria illa, nec simpliciter se quisquam Judæum, confitebatur, id est, tam pauci audebant confiteri se esse fide et ritu Judæos, quod respectu aliorum quasi nulli videbantur. Attamen aliqui erant, prout in primo libro et infra ostenditur.
paras.en: [[6:3|And very bad was this invasion of evils, and grievous to all|Pessima autem et universis Judæis fidelibus gravis erat malorum]] [Denis's text reads 'grievous to all the faithful Jews was the invasion of evils, that is, of persecutions, nay and of transgressions'], that is, the good Jews met with the most grievous calamities and persecutions from the most wicked deeds of the servants of Antiochus. [[6:4|For the temple was full of the riot and revellings of the Gentiles|Nam templum luxuria et comessationibus gentium erat plenum]], that is, the vices of the flesh were practised in the temple by gentiles and by Jews turned to paganism; shameless [[6:4|women thrust themselves|mulieres impudicæ se]] [[6:4|of their accord|ultro]], that is, freely and of their own will, [[6:4|into the holy places|sacratisque ædibus]], namely the courts of the temple and the little houses of the priests built round about the temple, [[6:4|and brought in|intro ferentes]], that is, carrying with them into the holy places, [[6:4|things that were not lawful|ea quæ non licebat]] to bring in there, namely meats and drinks forbidden by the law, or profane sacrifices to be offered to Jove. [[6:5|The altar also|Altare etiam]] of holocaust [[6:5|was filled with unlawful things|plenum erat illicitis]], victims of Jove. [[6:6|And neither were the sabbaths kept|Neque sabbata custodiebantur]] by the greater part of the Jews, [[6:6|nor the solemn days of the fathers observed|neque dies solennes patrii servabantur]], that is, the other feasts of the law kept of old by the fathers in that country, [[6:6|neither did any man plainly profess himself to be a Jew|nec simpliciter se quisquam Judæum, confitebatur]], that is, so few dared to profess themselves Jews in faith and rite that, compared with the others, they seemed as none. Yet there were some, as is shown in the first book[[1 Mach 2:1||]] and below [the margin here is partly unreadable; it seems to give 1 Mach. ii, 1 and further numbers].

paras.t: Ducebantur autem Judæi cum amara necessitate, id est gravi mortis formidine, in die natalis regis Antiochi ad sacrificia Jovis seu aliorum deorum quos coluit. Verumtamen illa non fuit absoluta necessitas, sed conditionata, videlicet si vivere vellent: alioqui fuissent occisi, nisi sacrificassent sic. Ideo illa necessitas non excusavit eos a peccato mortali, quoniam tenebantur potius mori, quam transgredi legem Dei. Et quum Liberi, id est Bacchi, qui credebatur deus vini et vinearum, sacra celebrarentur, a ministris Antiochi, cogebantur Judæi hedera, id est tali herba consimili viti, coronati, scilicet habentes super caput sertum factum de hedera, Libero circuire, id est ad honorem Bacchi ejus fanum seu altare in gyro perambulare, vel ut aliqui dicunt, chorizare. Præterea, sicut dictum est super illud Jonæ, Præparavit Dominus hederam, hedera est arbuscula seu virgultum lata habens folia, et facit densissimam umbram, et oritur crebro in partibus Palæstinæ, secundum Hieronymum, maxime in locis arenosis: et cito crescit in altum, si habeat aliquod solidum aut stipitem, per quod ascendat; alioqui super terram reptat.
paras.en: [[6:7|But they were led by bitter constraint|Ducebantur autem Judæi cum amara necessitate]], that is, by grievous fear of death, [[6:7|on the king's birthday to the sacrifices|in die natalis regis Antiochi ad sacrificia]] of Jove or of the other gods whom he worshipped. Yet that was not an absolute necessity, but a conditional one, namely if they wished to live: otherwise they would have been slain had they not sacrificed so. Therefore that necessity did not excuse them from mortal sin, since they were bound rather to die than to transgress the law of God. Then, [[6:7|when the feast of Bacchus|Et quum Liberi]] (*Liber*, that is, Bacchus, who was believed to be the god of wine and vineyards) [[6:7|was kept|sacra celebrarentur]] by the ministers of Antiochus, the Jews [[6:7|were compelled|cogebantur]], [[6:7|crowned with ivy|hedera]] (*ivy*, that is, a plant like the vine; *crowned*, that is, having on their heads a garland made of ivy), [[6:7|to go about|circuire]] [[6:7|in honour of Bacchus|Libero]], that is, to walk round his shrine or altar in honour of Bacchus, or, as some say, to dance. Moreover, as was said on that saying of Jonas, [[Jon 4:6|the Lord God prepared an ivy|Præparavit Dominus hederam]], ivy is a small tree or shrub with broad leaves, and it makes a very dense shade, and grows commonly in the parts of Palestine, according to Jerome, especially in sandy places: and it quickly grows tall if it has something solid or a stake to climb by; otherwise it creeps along the ground.

paras.t: Decretum autem exiit in proximas gentilium civitates, id est, præceptum Antiochi mittebatur hinc inde per oppida subditorum ipsius, suggerentibus Ptolemæis, id est imitatoribus et fautoribus impii Ptolemæi: qui, ut supra habetur, induxit Antiochum ad proferendum sententiam pro Menelao et contra fideles Judæos; ut pari modo et ipsi gentiles urbium illarum adversus Judæos agerent, id est, Judæos in suis urbibus commorantes ad sacrificandum compellerent. Erat ergo videre miseriam, id est miserabilem et crudelem effectum, qui subditur.
paras.en: [[6:8|And there went out a decree into the neighbouring cities of the Gentiles|Decretum autem exiit in proximas gentilium civitates]] [the opening words of this lemma are damaged in the scan and are given as in the Vulgate], that is, the command of Antiochus was sent here and there through the towns of his subjects, [[6:8|by the suggestion of the Ptolemeans|suggerentibus Ptolemæis]], that is, of the imitators and abettors of the wicked Ptolemee, who, as is told above[[2 Mach 4:46||]], brought Antiochus to pronounce sentence for Menelaus and against the faithful Jews; [[6:8|that they also should act in like manner against the Jews|ut pari modo et ipsi gentiles urbium illarum adversus Judæos agerent]], the gentiles of those cities, that is, should compel the Jews dwelling in their cities to sacrifice. [[6:9|then was misery to be seen|Erat ergo videre miseriam]], that is, a pitiable and cruel outcome, which is told next.

paras.t: Duæ enim mulieres Hebrææ fideles delatæ sunt, id est servis Antiochi accusatæ, natos suos circumcidisse: quas infantibus ad ubera suspensis, quum publice per civitatem circumduxissent, ad aliarum mulierum Hebræarum terrorem, per muros præcipitaverunt: quod fuit crudelissimum opus, tam in matribus, quam in infantulis, qui suspensi fuerunt ad ubera matrum, quibus fuerant nutriendi: præsertim quum tam in Exodo, quam in Deuteronomio Dominus jusserit, Non coques hædum in lacte matris suæ. Alii vero Judæi ad proximas coeuntes, id est simul euntes, speluncas, et latenter diem sabbati celebrantes, flammis succensi sunt, eo quod verebantur propter religionem et observantiam manu sibi auxilium ferre, id est, quia non audebant se defendere, hostibusque resistere, eo quod sabbatum esset, putantes illicitum se pugnare in sabbato: prout istud primi libri secundo capitulo plenius dictum est atque expositum.
paras.en: [[6:10|For two women|Duæ enim mulieres]], faithful Hebrews, [[6:10|were accused|delatæ sunt]], that is, accused to the servants of Antiochus, [[6:10|to have circumcised their children|natos suos circumcidisse]] [these words are damaged in the scan and are given as in the Vulgate]: [[6:10|whom, when they had openly led about through the city, with the infants hanging at their breasts|quas infantibus ad ubera suspensis, quum publice per civitatem circumduxissent]], to strike terror into the other Hebrew women, [[6:10|they threw down headlong from the walls|per muros præcipitaverunt]]: which was a most cruel deed, both to the mothers and to the little infants who hung at the breasts of the mothers by whom they were to be nursed; above all since the Lord commanded, both in Exodus and in Deuteronomy: [[Ex 23:19|Thou shalt not boil a kid in the milk of his dam|Non coques hædum in lacte matris suæ]][[Ex 34:26||]][[Deut 14:21||]]. [[6:11|And others that had met together|Alii vero Judæi ad proximas coeuntes]], that is, going together, [[6:11|in caves that were near|speluncas]], [[6:11|and were keeping the sabbath day privately|et latenter diem sabbati celebrantes]], [[6:11|were burnt with fire|flammis succensi sunt]], [[6:11|because they made a conscience to help themselves with their hands, by reason of the religious observance of the day|eo quod verebantur propter religionem et observantiam manu sibi auxilium ferre]], that is, because they did not dare to defend themselves and resist their enemies, since it was the sabbath, thinking it unlawful for them to fight on the sabbath: as was said and explained more fully in the second chapter of the first book[[1 Mach 2:33||]].

paras.t: Obsecro autem eos qui hunc librum lecturi sunt, aut ejus lectionem audituri, ne abhorrescant propter adversos casus, id est, ne propter gravissimas istas tribulationes Judæis inflictas, scandalizentur sive abhorreant populum Judæorum tanquam Deo odibilem, vel quasi inane sit Deo servire, qui sibi servientes permittit tam atrociter trucidari; sed reputent ea adversa quæ acciderunt Judæis, non ad interitum, id est finalem perditionem seu totalem exstirpationem, sed ad correctionem esse generis nostri: ut scilicet, in hac vita paternaliter castigarentur a Deo, ne in æternum perirent: quod est divinæ dilectionis indicium et effectus. Propter quod scriptum est in Proverbiorum libro: Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et ne deficias quum ab eo corriperis. Quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi.
paras.en: [[6:12|Now I beseech those that shall read this book|Obsecro autem eos qui hunc librum lecturi sunt]], or shall hear it read, [[6:12|that they be not shocked at these calamities|ne abhorrescant propter adversos casus]], that is, that they be not scandalized by these most grievous tribulations inflicted on the Jews, or shrink in horror from the people of the Jews as hateful to God, or as though it were vain to serve God, who lets those who serve him be so cruelly slaughtered; [[6:12|but that they consider the things that happened|sed reputent ea adversa quæ acciderunt]] to the Jews, [[6:12|not as being for the destruction|non ad interitum]], that is, final perdition or utter rooting out, [[6:12|but for the correction of our nation|sed ad correctionem esse generis nostri]]: namely, that they should be chastised by God in a fatherly way in this life, lest they perish for ever; which is the sign and effect of divine love. Wherefore it is written in the book of Proverbs: [[Prov 3:11|My son, reject not the correction of the Lord: and do not faint when thou art chastised by him|Disciplinam Domini, fili mi, ne abjicias, et ne deficias quum ab eo corriperis]]. [[Prov 3:12|For whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth: and as a father in the son he pleaseth himself|Quem enim diligit Dominus, corripit, et quasi pater in filio complacet sibi]].

paras.t: Etenim multo tempore non sinere peccatoribus ex sententia agere, id est non permittere peccatores ad libitum diu peccare, sed statim ultiones adhibere, id est eos per temporales adversitates ac pœnas a peccatis reprimere, magni beneficii est indicium, id est evidenter beneficium grande, quum pœnæ vitæ præsentis sint medicinales, et incomparabiliter melius sit temporaliter castigari, sicque a vitiis refrenari, quam in tempore isto sine freno delectationibus frui, ac postea in æternum puniri.
paras.en: For [[6:13|when sinners are not suffered to go on in their ways for a long time|multo tempore non sinere peccatoribus ex sententia agere]] [Denis's text: 'not to suffer sinners to act after their own mind for a long time'], that is, not to let sinners sin as they please for long, [[6:13|but are presently punished|sed statim ultiones adhibere]], that is, to restrain them from sins by temporal adversities and penalties, [[6:13|is a token of great goodness|magni beneficii est indicium]], that is, plainly a great benefit; since the penalties of the present life are medicinal, and it is incomparably better to be chastised in time, and so be curbed from vices, than to enjoy pleasures without a curb in this time, and afterwards be punished for ever.

paras.t: Non enim, sicut in aliis nationibus idololatris, Dominus patienter exspectat, id est, earum damnationem differt, emendationemque, quantum in se est, præstolatur, ut eas quum judicii particularis in morte singulorum, vel generalis in fine mundi, dies advenerit, in plenitudine peccatorum puniat, id est, secundum exigentiam omnium vitiorum eorum condemnet ac torqueat, quum mensuram iniquitatum suarum impleverint: ita et in nobis Judæis statuit ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis, id est usque ad mortem absque correctione protractis, ita demum in nos vindicet nostra peccata per infernalia et æterna supplicia. Propter quod nunquam misericordiam suam a nobis amovet in toto, seu taliter sicut a gentilibus reprobis. Corripiens vero paternaliter in præsenti in adversis, populum suum non derelinquit finaliter, aut dona gratiæ subtrahendo electis, quamvis ad tempus permittat eos acriter infestari.
paras.en: [[6:14|For, not as with other nations|Non enim, sicut in aliis nationibus]] that worship idols, [[6:14|whom the Lord patiently expecteth|Dominus patienter exspectat]], that is, puts off their damnation and, as far as lies in him, waits for their amendment, [[6:14|that when the day of judgment|ut eas quum judicii]] (the particular judgment at the death of each, or the general one at the end of the world) [[6:14|shall come|dies advenerit]], [[6:14|he may punish them in the fulness of their sins|in plenitudine peccatorum puniat]], that is, may condemn and torment them as all their vices require, when they have filled up the measure of their iniquities: [[6:15|Doth he also deal with us|ita et in nobis]] Jews, [[6:15|so as to suffer our sins to come to their height|statuit ut peccatis nostris in finem devolutis]], that is, drawn out until death without correction, [[6:15|and then take vengeance on us|ita demum in nos vindicet]] for our sins by the eternal torments of hell [Denis's text reads 'so has he appointed for us', the 'not' of the verse before carrying over]. [[6:16|And therefore he never withdraweth his mercy from us|Propter quod nunquam misericordiam suam a nobis amovet]] altogether, or in such a way as from the reprobate gentiles; [[6:16|but though he chastise|Corripiens vero]] in a fatherly way in the present [[6:16|with adversity|in adversis]], [[6:16|he forsaketh them not|populum suum non derelinquit]] [Denis's text: 'he forsaketh not his people'] finally, nor by withdrawing the gifts of grace from the elect, though for a time he lets them be fiercely harassed.

paras.t: Hæc de populo Judæorum pro cursu veteris Testamenti verificantur. Nunc autem ira Dei supervenit eis usque in finem. De populo autem christiano ista nunc dici possunt, qui est genus electum, gens sancta, populus acquisitionis, pars atque hæreditas Dei: non quod universi electi sint, imo et ipsorum credentium multi sunt vocati, pauci vero electi; sed quia præ ceteris gentibus plures electi in isto sunt populo. Itaque reprobos et iniquos ac vitiosos credentes præscitos, Deus omnipotens, justus, sanctus ac metuendus, permittit prosperari ac deliciari in sæculo isto, nec virga ejus est super eos. De quibus ait in Psalmo: Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum; ibunt in adinventionibus suis. Unde hujusmodi populo ait per Ezechielem prophetam: Zelus meus recessit a te, non irascar tibi amplius.
paras.en: These things are verified of the people of the Jews for the course of the Old Testament. But now the wrath of God has come upon them to the end. These things can now be said of the Christian people, which is [[1 Pet 2:9|a chosen generation|genus electum]], [[1 Pet 2:9|a holy nation, a purchased people|gens sancta, populus acquisitionis]], the portion and inheritance of God: not that all of them are elect, for even of those who believe [[Matt 22:14|many are called, but few are chosen|multi sunt vocati, pauci vero electi]]; but because more are elect in this people than in the other nations. And so the reprobate, wicked and vicious believers, foreknown [that is, foreknown as lost], God almighty, just, holy and to be feared, lets prosper and live in delights in this world, and his rod is not upon them. Of whom he says in the Psalm: [[Ps 80:13|So I let them go according to the desires of their heart: they shall walk in their own inventions|Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis eorum; ibunt in adinventionibus suis]]. Whence he says to such a people through the prophet Ezechiel: [[Ezech 16:42|my jealousy shall depart from thee|Zelus meus recessit a te]], [[Ezech 16:42|be angry no more|non irascar tibi amplius]].

paras.t: Sed hæc nobis ad commonitionem legentium, id est ad eorum exhortationem ne abhorrescant, etc., ut dictum est, dicta sunt paucis verbis, magnam sententiam includentibus. Jam autem veniendum est ad narrationem rerum gestarum, in quibus adversa gravissima contigerunt populo nostro.
paras.en: But these things, [[6:17|for a warning to the readers|ad commonitionem legentium]], that is, for their exhortation, that they be not shocked, etc., as was said, have been told [the margin gives the Vulgate's *dicta sint*, 'let this suffice', beside Denis's *dicta sunt*, 'have been told'] in few words that hold a great meaning. [[6:17|And now we must come to the narration|Jam autem veniendum est ad narrationem]] of the things done, in which the most grievous adversities befell our people.

paras.t: Igitur Eleazarus unus de primoribus, id est dignioribus majoribusque, Scribarum, qui erant legis periti, vir ætate provectus, et vultu decorus, aperto ore hians ex violentia persecutorum, volentium eum ad esum carnium porcinarum compellere, compellebatur carnem porcinam manducare. At ille gloriosissimam mortem, id est mortem virtuosam pro justitia et lege divina maxime gloriæ meritoriam, magis quam odibilem vitam, id est conversationem vitiosam, complectens, voluntarie præibat ad supplicium, ex caritate ad aliorum ædificationem. Intuens autem, id est mente perpendens, quemadmodum oporteret accedere, id est, quam constanter atque fideliter necesse sit ad martyrium progredi in casu hujusmodi, patienter sustinens destinavit, id est, decrevit et deliberavit, non admittere illicita, id est non agere contra legis præcepta, propter vitæ temporalis amorem, quum vita præsens ordinanda sit ad vitam spiritualem æternalem ac gloriosam.
paras.en: [[6:18|Eleazar one of the chief|Igitur Eleazarus unus de primoribus]], that is, of the worthier and greater, [[6:18|of the scribes|Scribarum]], who were skilled in the law, [[6:18|a man advanced in years, and of a comely countenance|vir ætate provectus, et vultu decorus]], [[6:18|was pressed to open his mouth|aperto ore hians]] under the violence of the persecutors, who wished to force him to the eating of pork, [[6:18|to eat swine's flesh|compellebatur carnem porcinam manducare]]. [[6:19|But he, choosing rather a most glorious death|At ille gloriosissimam mortem]], that is, a virtuous death for justice and the divine law, most meritorious of glory, [[6:19|than a hateful life|magis quam odibilem vitam]], that is, a vicious way of life, [[6:19|went forward voluntarily to the torment|voluntarie præibat ad supplicium]], out of charity, for the edification of others. [[6:20|And considering|Intuens autem]], that is, weighing in his mind, [[6:20|in what manner he was to come to it|quemadmodum oporteret accedere]], that is, how constantly and faithfully one must go forward to martyrdom in such a case, [[6:20|patiently bearing, he determined|patienter sustinens destinavit]], that is, decreed and resolved, [[6:20|not to do any unlawful things|non admittere illicita]], that is, not to act against the precepts of the law, [[6:20|for the love of life|propter vitæ temporalis amorem]] (of this temporal life), since the present life is to be ordered to the spiritual, eternal and glorious life.

paras.t: Hi autem qui adstabant, iniqua miseratione commoti, id est compassione fallaci trahente ad vitia, quæ venit non ex spirituali, sed sensuali amore, propter antiquam viri amicitiam, tollentes eum secreto, rogabant afferri carnes quibus vesci licitum erat secundum legem; et propter veterem amicitiam, etc. Unde hi videntur fuisse Judæi a lege ad gentilitatem prolapsi.
paras.en: [[6:21|But they that stood by, being moved with wicked pity|Hi autem qui adstabant, iniqua miseratione commoti]], that is, by a false compassion drawing to vice, which comes not from spiritual but from sensual love, [[6:21|for the old friendship they had with the man|propter antiquam viri amicitiam]], [[6:21|taking him aside, desired that flesh might be brought|tollentes eum secreto, rogabant afferri carnes]] which it was lawful to eat according to the law; [[6:22|and for the sake of their old friendship|et propter veterem amicitiam]], etc. Whence these seem to have been Jews fallen away from the law to heathenism.

paras.t: At ille, scilicet Eleazarus, cogitare cœpit ætatis suæ et senectutis eminentiam dignam: quia non solum longitudine temporum, sed et decore virtutum fuit ornata. Senectus enim venerabilis est non diuturna, etc., ut dicit Sapiens. Et ingenitæ nobilitatis canitiem, id est senium suum decoratum virtutibus, prout ingenita sua nobilitas ex Abraham et Patriarchis contracta requirebat: quoniam filius Abrahæ fuit non solum carne, sed et sanctitatis imitatione, secundum quod Christus in Joanne ait Judæis: Si filii Abrahæ estis, opera Abrahæ facite. Respondit cito; quia in re tam justa non fuit habenda longa consultatio; præmitti se velle in infernum, id est, per mortem temporalem transire ad limbum patrum.
paras.en: [[6:23|But he began to consider|At ille, scilicet Eleazarus, cogitare cœpit]], namely Eleazar, [[6:23|the dignity of his age, and his ancient years|ætatis suæ et senectutis eminentiam dignam]], for it was adorned not only by length of time but also by the beauty of the virtues. For [[Wis 4:8|venerable old age is not that of long time|Senectus enim venerabilis est non diuturna]], etc., as the Wise Man says. He considered also [[6:23|the inbred honour of his grey head|ingenitæ nobilitatis canitiem]], that is, his old age adorned with virtues, as his inborn nobility, drawn from Abraham and the Patriarchs, required: for he was a son of Abraham not only in the flesh, but also by imitation of his holiness, according to what Christ says to the Jews in John: [[John 8:39|If you be the children of Abraham, do the works of Abraham|Si filii Abrahæ estis, opera Abrahæ facite]]. So [[6:23|he answered without delay|Respondit cito]], since in so just a matter there was no need of long deliberation, [[6:23|that he would rather be sent into the other world|præmitti se velle in infernum]] [literally 'into hell', that is, the underworld], that is, to pass by temporal death to the limbo of the fathers.

paras.t: Non enim ætati nostræ, inquit, dignum est fingere, id est decens uti simulatione: quæ in tali casu fuisset scandalizativa et mortale peccatum, quum pro fidei ac legis divinæ defensione dandum sit testimonium evidens ac sincerum absque confictione. Quamobrem vita fortiter excedendo, id est virtuose ac fideliter finiendo, senectute dignus apparebo, id est, ita me habebo sicut meam condecet senectutem, ita ut merito senex appeller. Maledictus enim puer centum annorum. Si prompto animo pro gravissimis et sanctissimis legibus honesta morte perfungar, id est, transitorie utar. Dicuntur autem leges Dei gravissimæ, id est honestissimæ ac summe maturæ, quemadmodum homo facetus et honeste se habens, dicitur moribus gravis.
paras.en: [[6:24|For it doth not become our age, said he, to dissemble|Non enim ætati nostræ, inquit, dignum est fingere]], that is, it is not seemly to use pretence: which in such a case would have been a cause of scandal and a mortal sin, since for the defence of the faith and of the divine law a clear and sincere witness must be given without feigning. [[6:27|Wherefore, by departing manfully out of this life|Quamobrem vita fortiter excedendo]], that is, by ending it virtuously and faithfully, [[6:27|I shall shew myself worthy of my old age|senectute dignus apparebo]], that is, I shall bear myself as becomes my old age, so that I may deservedly be called an old man. For accursed is the child of a hundred years[[Is 65:20||]] [the margin's reference is misread; the words recall Is 65:20]. So also: [[6:28|if with a ready mind|Si prompto animo]], [[6:28|for the most venerable and most holy laws|pro gravissimis et sanctissimis legibus]], [[6:28|I suffer an honourable death|honesta morte perfungar]], that is, undergo it as a thing that passes. The laws of God are called *gravissimæ* [literally 'most grave'; the Douay-Rheims has 'most venerable'], that is, most honourable and supremely mature, as a man of good manners who bears himself honourably is said to be grave in his ways.

paras.t: His dictis, confestim ad supplicium trahebatur.
