Sed quum plagis perimeretur, dixit: Domine, qui habes scientiam, etc., duros corporis sustineo dolores, præsertim quia tam senex sum, videlicet nonagenarius; secundum animam vero, id est superiorem animæ portionem, videlicet secundum mentis dictamen et rationis censuram, et potissime secundum caritatis impulsum, propter timorem tuum filialem, qui caritatem includit, libenter hæc patior, ne te offendam, aut a te separer. Et iste hoc modo decessit, omnibus nobis ædificationem salubrem et grande exemplum relinquens, ut pro Deo, pro fide, pro justitia ad mortem quantumlibet duram simus parati, nec fictione aut duplicitate detestanda utamur.
paras.en: [[6:28|And having spoken thus, he was forthwith carried to execution|His dictis, confestim ad supplicium trahebatur]]. [[6:30|But when be was now ready to die with the stripes|Sed quum plagis perimeretur]], he [[6:30|said|dixit]]: [[6:30|O Lord, who hast the holy knowledge|Domine, qui habes scientiam]], etc., [[6:30|I suffer grievous pains in body|duros corporis sustineo dolores]], above all since I am so old, namely ninety years; [[6:30|but in soul|secundum animam vero]], that is, in the higher part of the soul, namely according to the dictate of the mind and the judgment of reason, and most of all according to the impulse of charity, [[6:30|because I fear thee|propter timorem tuum]] with a filial fear, which includes charity, [[6:30|am well content to suffer these things|libenter hæc patior]], lest I offend thee or be separated from thee. [[6:31|Thus did this man die|Et iste hoc modo decessit]], leaving to us all a wholesome edification and a great example, that for God, for the faith, for justice, we be ready for death however hard, and use no feigning or detestable double-dealing.

paras.t: Postremo, quoniam juxta doctrinam Apostoli, Corpora nostra templum sunt Spiritus Sancti, atque in sacris Ordinibus constituti, præsertim consecrati sunt Deo in templum, videamus ne et corpora nostra comessatione et luxuria polluantur, sed omni virtutum exercitio occupentur.
paras.en: Lastly, since according to the teaching of the Apostle our bodies are [[1 Cor 6:19|the temple of the Holy Ghost|templum sunt Spiritus Sancti]], and those set in holy Orders above all are consecrated to God as a temple, let us see that our bodies too be not defiled by revelling and riot, but be busied in every exercise of the virtues.

7.title: Expositio capituli septimi: Contigit autem septem fratres una cum matre sua apprehensos compelli a rege
7.title_en: Exposition of the seventh chapter: It came to pass also, that seven brethren, together with their mother, were apprehended, and compelled by the king

paras.t: Celeberrimum martyrium septem fratrum et venerandæ matris eorum, hic recitatur. Contigit autem septem fratres una cum matre sua apprehensos, compelli a rege Antiocho contingere contra fas, id est contra præceptum legis comedere, carnes porcinas, flagris et taureis cruciatos, id est flagellatos extremitatibus virgularum colligatarum, atque flagellis factis de corio taurorum. Unus autem ex illis qui erat primus, sic ait : Quid quæris, et quid vis discere a nobis ? Parati sumus mori, etc. Iratus itaque rex, jussit sartagines, id est caldarias magnas, et ollas æneas succendi ; et ei qui prior fuerat locutus, qui et primogenitus fuit, linguam amputari : quasi peccasset, tam constanter respondendo, per linguam ; et cute capitis abstracta, summas quoque manus et pedes, id est manus et pedes quæ sunt extrema membra in corpore hominis, præscindi. Aliqui tamen dicunt, extremitatem manuum ac pedum, id est digitos seu pollices, secundum quod in libro Judicum Adonibezec ait : Septuaginta reges, amputatis manuum ac pedum summitatibus, colligebant sub mensa mea ciborum reliquias. Et quum per omnia inutilis factus esset, id est ineptus ad opera vitæ præsentis, utpote membris privatus, nec diu vivere potens vita naturæ, jussit ei ignem admoveri, id est applicari, et adhuc spirante, id est anhelitum trahentem, torreri in sartagine, id est cremari et uri in caldaria seu patella.
paras.en: The most celebrated martyrdom of the seven brothers and of their venerable mother is related here. [[7:1|It came to pass also, that seven brethren, together with their mother, were apprehended|Contigit autem septem fratres una cum matre sua apprehensos]], [[7:1|and compelled by the king|compelli a rege]] Antiochus to touch [the print reads *contingere*, 'to touch', with a footnote giving the variant *edere*, 'to eat', the word of the Vulgate] [[7:1|against the law|contra fas]], that is, to eat, against the precept of the law, [[7:1|swine's flesh|carnes porcinas]], [[7:1|tormented with whips and scourges|flagris et taureis cruciatos]], that is, scourged with the ends of rods tied together, and with whips made of bulls' hide [*taureæ*, from *taurus*, 'bull']. [[7:2|But one of them, who was the eldest, said thus|Unus autem ex illis qui erat primus, sic ait]]: [[7:2|What wouldst thou ask, or learn of us?|Quid quæris, et quid vis discere a nobis]] [[7:2|we are ready to die|Parati sumus mori]], etc. [[7:3|Then the king being angry, commanded fryingpans|Iratus itaque rex, jussit sartagines]], that is, great cauldrons, [[7:3|and brazen caldrons to be made hot|et ollas æneas succendi]]; and [[7:4|to cut out the tongue|linguam amputari]] [[7:4|of him that had spoken first|ei qui prior fuerat locutus]], who was also the firstborn: as though he had sinned with his tongue by answering so steadfastly; [[7:4|and the skin of his head being drawn off|et cute capitis abstracta]], [[7:4|to chop off also|præscindi]] [[7:4|the extremities of his hands and feet|summas quoque manus et pedes]], that is, the hands and feet, which are the extreme members in the human body. Some, however, say the extremities of the hands and feet, that is, the fingers or thumbs, as Adonibezec says in the book of Judges: [[Judg 1:7|Seventy kings, having their fingers and toes cut off, gathered up the leavings of the meat under my table|Septuaginta reges, amputatis manuum ac pedum summitatibus, colligebant sub mensa mea ciborum reliquias]]. [[7:5|And when he was now maimed in all parts|Et quum per omnia inutilis factus esset]], that is, unfit for the works of the present life, being deprived of his members, and not able to live long by the life of nature, [[7:5|he commanded him|jussit ei]] [[7:5|to be brought to the fire|ignem admoveri]], that is, to be put to it, [[7:5|being yet alive|adhuc spirante]], that is, while he still drew breath, [[7:5|and to be fried in the fryingpan|torreri in sartagine]], that is, to be burned and roasted in a cauldron or pan.

paras.t: Quod quum fieret, mater et fratres ejus non terrebantur ; sed desuper confortati, se mutuo hortabantur fortiter mori pro lege divina, dicentes : Dominus Deus aspiciet veritatem vitæ atque justitiæ, et veram fidei sanctæ confessionem approbando, et remunerando hæc omnia, et eos qui veritati et æquitati repugnant, damnando ; et consolabitur in nobis, id est, nos consolabitur, atque pro temporali isto tormento gaudia conferet sempiterna. Sancti quoque martyres in ipsis suis martyriis mirabiliter consolantur et exhilarantur desuper in cordibus suis, ita quod consolatio talis frequenter copiose redundat in partem sensitivam, ac tormenta alleviat. Quemadmodum in protestatione cantici, id est in cantico suo cum invocatione testificationis cœli ac terræ edito ac prolato, declaravit Moyses, in Deuteronomio dicens : Et in servis suis consolabitur, id est, consolationem infundet cordibus servorum suorum. Nostra autem translatio habet, Et in servis suis miserebitur : et redit in idem, quoniam consolatio ista est miseratio Dei, et misericordiæ ejus effectus. Unde et Paulus fatetur : Benedictus Deus, qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra. Et Psalmista : Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam.
paras.en: While this was being done, his mother and brothers were not terrified; but, strengthened from above, they [[7:5|exhorted one another to die manfully|se mutuo hortabantur fortiter mori]] for the divine law, [[7:6|Saying: The Lord God will look upon the truth|dicentes : Dominus Deus aspiciet veritatem]] of life and of justice, and the true confession of the holy faith, approving and rewarding all these, and condemning those who resist truth and equity; [[7:6|and will take pleasure in us|et consolabitur in nobis]] [*consolabitur*: 'will comfort'; the Douay-Rheims has 'will take pleasure'], that is, he will comfort us, and for this temporal torment will bestow everlasting joys. The holy martyrs too, in their very martyrdoms, are wonderfully comforted and gladdened from above in their hearts, so that such consolation often overflows abundantly into the sensitive part and lightens the torments. It is [[7:6|as Moses declared|declaravit Moyses]] [[7:6|in the profession of the canticle|in protestatione cantici]], that is, in his canticle, uttered and set forth with the invocation of heaven and earth as witnesses, saying in Deuteronomy: [[7:6|And in his servants he will take pleasure|Et in servis suis consolabitur]], that is, he will pour consolation into the hearts of his servants. Our translation [that is, the Vulgate text of Deuteronomy] has: He [[Deut 32:36|will have mercy on his servants|in servis suis miserebitur]]; and it comes to the same thing, since this consolation is the mercy of God and the effect of his mercy. Hence Paul too declares: [[2 Cor 1:3|Blessed be the God|Benedictus Deus]], [[2 Cor 1:4|Who comforteth us in all our tribulation|qui consolatur nos in omni tribulatione nostra]]. And the Psalmist: [[Ps 93:19|According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, thy comforts have given joy to my soul.|Secundum multitudinem dolorum meorum in corde meo, consolationes tuæ lætificaverunt animam meam]]

paras.t: Mortuo itaque illo primo hoc modo, sequentem ducebant ad illudendum, et interrogabant, etc. At ille respondit patria voce : Non faciam, etc. Et in ultimo spiritu constitutus, id est, secundus frater, videlicet primus in ordine post primogenitum, quum passus esset supplicia similia suppliciis fratris sui defuncti, positus in agone et prope ultimam respirationem ac exspirationem, ait : Tu quidem, scelestissime, id est vitiosissime, utpote publicus persecutor justorum, et adversarius legis divinæ, crudelissimusque tyrannus, in præsenti vita nos perdis, id est interficis ; sed Rex mundi, in æterna vitæ resurrectione nos suscitabit, id est resurrectione electorum, quæ erit via ad vitam beatam ac sempiternam in corpore et anima. Quæ resurrectio vocatur immutatio, id est ad melius mutatio, juxta illud Apostoli : Omnes quidem resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur. Christus quoque in Joanne : Procedent qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ (haud dubium quin gloriæ) ; qui vero mala egerunt, in resurrectionem judicii.
paras.en: [[7:7|So when the first was dead after this manner|Mortuo itaque illo primo hoc modo]], [[7:7|they brought the next to make him a mocking stock|sequentem ducebant ad illudendum]], and [[7:7|they asked him|interrogabant]], etc. [[7:8|But he answered in his own language|At ille respondit patria voce]]: [[7:8|I will not do it|Non faciam]], etc. [[7:9|And when he was at the last gasp|Et in ultimo spiritu constitutus]], that is, the second brother, namely the first in order after the firstborn, when he had suffered torments like the torments of his dead brother, being in his agony and near his last breath and expiring, [[7:9|he said thus|ait]]: [[7:9|Thou indeed, O most wicked man|Tu quidem, scelestissime]], that is, most vicious, as being the public persecutor of the just, the adversary of the divine law, and a most cruel tyrant, [[7:9|destroyest us out of this present life|in præsenti vita nos perdis]], that is, killest us; [[7:9|but the King of the world|sed Rex mundi]] [[7:9|will raise us up|nos suscitabit]] [[7:9|in the resurrection of eternal life|in æterna vitæ resurrectione]], that is, in the resurrection of the elect, which will be the way to the blessed and everlasting life in body and soul. This resurrection is called a changing, that is, a changing for the better, according to that saying of the Apostle: [[1 Cor 15:51|We shall all indeed rise again: but we shall not all be changed|Omnes quidem resurgemus, sed non omnes immutabimur]]. And Christ too in John: [[John 5:29|And they that have done good things shall come forth unto the resurrection of life|Procedent qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ]] (no doubt, of glory); [[John 5:29|but they that have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment|qui vero mala egerunt, in resurrectionem judicii]].

paras.t: Post hunc tertius frater illuditur, id est, cum impiorum illorum derisione puniebatur ac illusorie tractabatur. Verumtamen ipse a spe sua non illudebatur, nec stulte, sed sapientissime habuit se. Et linguam postulatus, id est, exactus et jussus a tyranno linguam extendere, ut abscinderetur, cito protulit eam, tanquam ex corde paratus ad omnium membrorum suorum dilacerationem propter justitiæ defensionem, et manus constanter extendit ad amputationem ; et cum fiducia æternæ remunerationis, ait : E cœlo ista possideo, id est, membra corporis mei a Deo creatore cœlorum accepi et habeo. Ad corporis quoque formationem et organizationem, corpora cœlestia et eorum motores, motu, lumine et influentia cooperantur, tanquam instrumenta omnipotentiæ ac sapientiæ Creatoris. Videtur autem in hac narratione non servari ordo historiæ, quoniam sanctus martyr iste protulit verba hic, antequam lingua sua amputabatur. Vel, si lingua abscissa protulit ista, magnum fuit miraculum : quod certum est fieri potuisse Omnipotentis virtute, sicut in novo Testamento multi beatissimi martyres Christi linguis abscissis noscuntur locuti. Sed propter Dei leges implendas et defendendas, nunc hæc ipsa despicio, id est, viliter tractari permitto, et æquitati ac veritati postpono, quoniam ab ipso Deo me ea recepturum spero, melioranda ac glorificanda quatuor dotibus corporum beatorum : quæ sunt, impassibilitas, claritas, agilitas atque subtilitas. Unde et sanctus Job fassus est : Credo quod Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum ; et rursum circumdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea videbo Deum salvatorem meum.
paras.en: [[7:10|After him the third was made a mocking-stock|Post hunc tertius frater illuditur]], that is, he was punished with the derision of those wicked men and treated with mockery. Yet he himself was not mocked in his hope [*illudi*: 'to be mocked', and also 'to be deceived'], nor did he bear himself foolishly, but most wisely. And [[7:10|when he was required|linguam postulatus]] his tongue, that is, when he was called upon and ordered by the tyrant to put out his tongue so that it might be cut off, [[7:10|he quickly put forth|cito protulit]] it, as one ready from the heart to have all his limbs torn apart in defence of justice, [[7:10|and courageously stretched out his hands|et manus constanter extendit]] to be cut off; and [[7:11|with confidence|cum fiducia]] of eternal reward he [[7:11|said|ait]]: [[7:11|These I have from heaven|E cœlo ista possideo]], that is, I have received and hold the members of my body from God, the creator of the heavens. For in the forming and organizing of the body, too, the heavenly bodies and their movers cooperate by their motion, light and influence, as instruments of the omnipotence and wisdom of the Creator. It seems, however, that in this narrative the order of the history is not kept, since this holy martyr spoke these words before his tongue was cut off. Or, if he spoke them with his tongue cut off, it was a great miracle: which it is certain could have been done by the power of the Almighty, as in the New Testament many most blessed martyrs of Christ are known to have spoken after their tongues were cut out. [[7:11|but for the laws of God|Sed propter Dei leges]], for fulfilling and defending them, [[7:11|I now despise them|nunc hæc ipsa despicio]], that is, I allow them to be treated vilely, and set them after equity and truth, [[7:11|because I hope to receive them again from him|quoniam ab ipso Deo me ea recepturum spero]], to be bettered and glorified with the four dowries of the bodies of the blessed [that is, the four endowments of the glorified body], which are impassibility, clarity, agility and subtlety. Hence holy Job too confessed: I believe that [[Job 19:25|my Redeemer liveth, and in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|Redemptor meus vivit, et in novissimo die de terra surrecturus sum]]; [[Job 19:26|And I shall be clothed again with my skin, and in my flesh I shall see|et rursum circumdabor pelle mea, et in carne mea videbo]] God my Saviour [Denis reads *Deum salvatorem meum*, 'God my Saviour', where the Vulgate has *Deum meum*, 'my God'].

paras.t: Et hoc ita defuncto, quartum vexabant similiter torquentes. Et quum esset ad mortem, id est quartus frater morti jam proximus, ait : Potius est, ab hominibus morti datos, spem exspectare a Deo, iterum ab ipso resuscitandos : id est, eos qui ab hominibus adjudicati sunt morti propter justitiam, melius est exspectare a Deo promissam salutem, qui et resuscitandi sunt a Deo in die novissimo ; quam aliquid aliud huic contrarium facere. Tibi enim resurrectio ad vitam non erit, id est, non resurges in fine sæculi resurrectione beatæ immutationis seu gloriæ immortalis, sed resurrectione judicii condemnationis : quæ est mors secunda et infernalis. Omnes tamen resurgent ad vitam naturæ perpetuam. Istud autem intelligendum fuit sub conditione, videlicet nisi Antiochus pœniteret : vel per modum comminationis aut propheticæ denuntiationis.
paras.en: [[7:13|And after he was thus dead, they tormented the fourth in the like manner.|Et hoc ita defuncto, quartum vexabant similiter torquentes]] [[7:14|And when he was now ready to die|Et quum esset ad mortem]], that is, the fourth brother, now close to death, [[7:14|he spoke thus|ait]]: [[7:14|It is better, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God, to be raised up again by him|Potius est, ab hominibus morti datos, spem exspectare a Deo, iterum ab ipso resuscitandos]]: that is, for those who have been condemned to death by men for justice's sake, who are also to be raised up by God on the last day, it is better to look for the salvation promised by God than to do anything else contrary to this. [[7:14|for, as to thee, thou shalt have no resurrection unto life|Tibi enim resurrectio ad vitam non erit]], that is, thou shalt not rise at the end of the world by the resurrection of the blessed changing, or of immortal glory, but by the resurrection of the judgment of condemnation: which is [[Apoc 20:14|the second death|mors secunda]], the death of hell. All, however, will rise to the everlasting life of nature. But this was to be understood under a condition, namely unless Antiochus repented; or else by way of a threat, or of a prophetic announcement.

paras.t: Et quum admovissent quintum fratrem ad pœnam, vexabant eum. At ille respiciens in eum, dicit : Potestatem inter homines habes, et quum sis corruptibilis, facis quod vis. Noli putare genus nostrum, scilicet populum Judæorum, a Deo esse derelictum finaliter aut omnino ; vel quantum ad animarum salutem, quia hæc ipsa castigatio et persecutio nostra, est nobis causa coronationis æternæ, et signum dilectionis divinæ ad nos. Tu autem patienter sustine, id est, ad tempus et instar patientium præstolare, et videbis magnam potestatem ipsius, id est, omnipotentiam Dei per effectum diræ ultionis experieris, qualiter te et semen tuum torquebit. Hoc quasi prophetice dictum videtur, quia in brevi post hæc Antiochus durissime fuit plagatus, et infelicissime in gravissimis exspiravit tormentis, atque deinceps deputatus fuit æternis suppliciis. Filius quoque ejus Antiochus cum suo cognato Lysia fuit occisus. Similiter Alexander filius filii ejus ; deinde Antiochus filius Alexandri et multi de cognatis eorum. Possunt etiam per semen, omnes ejus imitatores intelligi.
paras.en: [[7:15|And when they had brought the fifth|Et quum admovissent quintum]] brother to punishment, [[7:15|they tormented him|vexabant eum]]. [[7:15|But he, looking upon the king|At ille respiciens in eum]], says: [[7:16|Whereas thou hast power among men though thou art corruptible, thou dost what thou wilt|Potestatem inter homines habes, et quum sis corruptibilis, facis quod vis]]. [[7:16|think not that our nation|Noli putare genus nostrum]], namely the people of the Jews, [[7:16|is forsaken by God|a Deo esse derelictum]] finally or altogether; or as regards the salvation of souls, because this very chastisement and persecution of ours is for us the cause of an eternal crown and a sign of God's love toward us. [[7:17|But stay patiently a while|Tu autem patienter sustine]], that is, wait for a time and in the manner of those who suffer patiently, [[7:17|and thou shalt see his great power|et videbis magnam potestatem ipsius]], that is, thou shalt experience the omnipotence of God by the effect of dire vengeance, [[7:17|in what manner he will torment thee and thy seed|qualiter te et semen tuum torquebit]]. This seems to have been said as a prophecy, for shortly after this Antiochus was most severely struck, and died most miserably in the gravest torments[[2 Mach 9:5||]], and thereafter was consigned to eternal punishments. His son Antiochus, too, was slain together with his kinsman Lysias[[1 Mach 7:4||]] [the margin's reference here is only partly legible (I Mach.); their death is told at 1 Mach 7:2–4]. Likewise Alexander, the son of his son[[1 Mach 11:17||]] [so the print; 1 Mach 10:1 calls Alexander the son of Antiochus]; then Antiochus the son of Alexander[[1 Mach 13:31||]], and many of their kinsmen. By his *seed*, too, all his imitators may be understood.

paras.t: Post hunc ducebant sextum, et is, scilicet sextus frater, mori incipiens, sic ait : Noli frustra errare, putando quod absque fructu hæc patiamur et sine dispositione providentiæ Dei. Nos enim propter nosmetipsos hoc patimur, pro nostra purgatione et coronatione, peccantes in Deum nostrum : per quod meruimus ista pati. Verumtamen frater iste hoc dixit in persona populi sui prævaricantis potius quam in sua persona, quemadmodum Esdras ait in sua peroratione : Deus meus, erubesco faciem meam levare ad te, quia peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum. Et digna admiratione facta sunt in nobis, id est adversa miranda. Tu autem ne existimes tibi impune futurum, id est sine ultione dissimulandum aut pertranseundum, quod contra Deum pugnare tentaveris, destruendo cultum ipsius, et ejus occidendo cultores : quibus ait per Zachariam, Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei. Unde et in Deuteronomio asseritur : Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetur. Hinc primo Regum libro inducitur : Si peccaverit vir in virum, placari ei poterit Dominus ; si autem in Dominum peccaverit, quis orabit pro eo ?
paras.en: [[7:18|After him they brought the sixth|Post hunc ducebant sextum]], [[7:18|and he|et is]], namely the sixth brother, [[7:18|being ready to die, spoke thus|mori incipiens, sic ait]]: [[7:18|Be not deceived without cause|Noli frustra errare]], thinking that we suffer these things without fruit and without the disposition of God's providence. [[7:18|for we suffer these things for ourselves|Nos enim propter nosmetipsos hoc patimur]], for our purification and crowning, [[7:18|having sinned against our God|peccantes in Deum nostrum]]: by which we have deserved to suffer these things. Yet this brother said this in the person of his prevaricating people rather than in his own person, as Esdras says in his prayer: [[1 Esd 9:6|My God|Deus meus]], I am [[1 Esd 9:6|ashamed to lift up my face to thee|erubesco faciem meam levare ad te]], for [[1 Esd 9:6|our sins are grown up even unto heaven|peccata nostra creverunt usque ad cœlum]]. [[7:18|and things worthy of admiration are done to us|Et digna admiratione facta sunt in nobis]], that is, adversities to be wondered at. [[7:19|But do not think that thou shalt escape unpunished|Tu autem ne existimes tibi impune futurum]], that is, to be overlooked or passed by without vengeance, [[7:19|for that thou hast attempted to fight against God|quod contra Deum pugnare tentaveris]], by destroying his worship and slaying his worshippers: to whom he says by Zacharias: [[Zach 2:8|he that toucheth you, toucheth the apple of my eye|Qui tetigerit vos, tanget pupillam oculi mei]]. Hence it is also declared in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 32:43|he will revenge the blood of his servants|Quia sanguinem servorum suorum ulciscetur]]. Hence it is said in the first book of Kings: [[1 Kings 2:25|If one man shall sin against another, God may be appeased in his behalf: but if a man shall sin against the Lord, who shall pray for him?|Si peccaverit vir in virum, placari ei poterit Dominus ; si autem in Dominum peccaverit, quis orabit pro eo]]

paras.t: Supra modum autem communem, mater fratrum istorum mirabilis, propter excellentiam suæ virtuositatis : cui nec in lege naturæ, neque in lege Mosaica legitur aliqua par fuisse, quantum ad fortitudinem hujus constantiæ in filiorum martyrizatione ; et bonorum memoria, id est sanctorum hominum commemoratione digna, ut eam sibi in exemplum proponant patientiæ ac virtutum ; quæ pereuntes, id est mortem patientes, septem filios conspiciens, bono animo ferebat, id est, æquanimiter tolerabat, propter spem quam in Deum habebat, id est propter speratam beatitudinem, quam exspectavit a Deo dandam sibi ac filiis suis, quam ex caritate ipsis optavit. Singulos illorum hortabatur patria voce, id est lingua materna, vel patrum sanctorum exhortatione, fortiter, repleta sapientia, id est dono sapientiæ et illuminatione superna, qua contemplabatur divina, cœlestia et æterna : quorum intuitu et amore vilipendit carnalia et caduca : et femineæ cogitationi, quæ interdum ex primis motibus cœpit præsentibus filiorum suorum doloribus molliter ac muliebriter condolere, masculinum animum inserens, id est viriles considerationes adjiciens, atque virtutum motus et effectus admiscens, per quas refrenavit ac vicit cogitationes et compassiones femineas, dixit ad eos :
paras.en: [[7:20|Now the mother|mater]] of these brothers [[7:20|was to be admired|mirabilis]] [[7:20|above measure|Supra modum]], above the common measure, for the excellence of her virtue: for we read of no woman, either under the law of nature or under the law of Moses, who was her equal in the strength of this constancy at the martyrdom of her sons; and [[7:20|worthy|digna]] [[7:20|to be remembered by good men|et bonorum memoria]], that is, worthy to be commemorated by holy men, so that they may set her before themselves as an example of patience and of the virtues; she who, beholding [[7:20|her seven sons|septem filios conspiciens]] [[7:20|slain|pereuntes]], that is, suffering death, [[7:20|bore it with a good courage|bono animo ferebat]], that is, endured it with an even mind, [[7:20|for the hope that she had in God|propter spem quam in Deum habebat]], that is, for the hoped-for beatitude, which she expected God to give to herself and to her sons, and which out of charity she desired for them. She [[7:21|exhorted every one of them in her own language|Singulos illorum hortabatur patria voce]], that is, in her mother tongue, or with the exhortation of the holy fathers [*patria vox*: 'native speech', but literally 'the fathers' voice', whence Denis's second reading], [[7:21|bravely|fortiter]], [[7:21|being filled with wisdom|repleta sapientia]], that is, with the gift of wisdom and with enlightenment from above, by which she contemplated divine, heavenly and eternal things, at the sight and for love of which she held carnal and perishable things cheap; and to [[7:21|a woman's thought|femineæ cogitationi]], which at times, by its first motions, began to grieve softly and as a woman with the present pains of her sons, [[7:21|joining a man's heart|masculinum animum inserens]], that is, adding manly considerations and mingling in the motions and effects of the virtues, by which she curbed and overcame her womanly thoughts and feelings of compassion, [[7:22|She said to them|dixit ad eos]]:

paras.t: Nescio qualiter in utero meo apparuistis, id est, qualiter sitis concepti, aucti et animati in ventre meo, ita quod per uteri mei tumorem, et corpusculorum vestrorum motionem, cœpit innotescere vos in alvo meo consistere. Nempe qualiter anima creetur ac infundatur, intellectus non capit humanus. Neque enim ego spiritum et animam donavi vobis et vitam, et singulorum membra non ego compegi, id est, membra vestra non formavi, sed Deus per causas secundas. Unde et sanctus Job loquitur Deo : Manus tuæ formaverunt me, et plasmaverunt me totum in circuitu. Hinc scriptum est in Ecclesiaste : Quomodo ignoras quæ sit via spiritus, et qua ratione compingantur ossa in ventre prægnantis ; sic nescis opera Dei qui fabricator est omnium. Neque enim ego spiritum, id est mentem, et animam rationalem, id est animam ipsam formam substantialem, corpus vivificantem, animantem, regentem, in qua est mens et inferiores sensitivæque vires, et vitam naturæ aut gratiæ, vobis donavi. Anima etenim rationalis non est ab intra, neque ex traduce, sed per creationem et infusionem a Deo. Itaque per hæc verba non est intelligendum, quod in homine sint duæ aut plures formæ substantiales ; sed anima una, plurium virium contentiva. Juxta quem modum ait Apostolus : Deus pacis sanctificet vos per omnia, ut integer spiritus vester et anima et corpus servetur.
paras.en: [[7:22|I know not how you were formed in my womb|Nescio qualiter in utero meo apparuistis]] [*apparuistis*: literally 'you appeared'], that is, how you were conceived, grew and were quickened in my womb, so that by the swelling of my womb and the movement of your little bodies it began to be known that you were in my belly. For how the soul is created and infused, human understanding does not grasp. [[7:22|for I neither gave you breath, nor soul, nor life|Neque enim ego spiritum et animam donavi vobis et vitam]], [[7:22|neither did I frame the limbs of every one of you|et singulorum membra non ego compegi]], that is, I did not form your members, but God did, through secondary causes. Hence holy Job too says to God: [[Job 10:8|Thy hands have made me, and fashioned me wholly round about|Manus tuæ formaverunt me, et plasmaverunt me totum in circuitu]] [Denis reads *formaverunt*, 'have formed', where the Vulgate has *fecerunt*, 'have made']. Hence it is written in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 11:5|As thou knowest not what is the way of the spirit, nor how the bones are joined together in the womb of her that is with child: so thou knowest not the works of God, who is the maker of all.|Quomodo ignoras quæ sit via spiritus, et qua ratione compingantur ossa in ventre prægnantis ; sic nescis opera Dei qui fabricator est omnium]] [[7:22|for I neither gave you breath|Neque enim ego spiritum]], that is, the mind, [[7:22|nor soul|et animam]], that is, the rational soul, the soul itself, the substantial form, which quickens, animates and rules the body, in which are the mind and the lower and sensitive powers, [[7:22|nor life|et vitam]] of nature or of grace. For the rational soul is not from within, nor by traduction [that is, handed on from the souls of the parents], but comes by creation and infusion from God. So these words are not to be understood as if there were two or more substantial forms in man, but one soul, containing many powers. In which manner the Apostle says: [[1 Thess 5:23|may the God of peace himself sanctify you in all things: that your whole spirit and soul and body may be preserved|Deus pacis sanctificet vos per omnia, ut integer spiritus vester et anima et corpus servetur]].

paras.t: Sed est mundi Creator, qui formavit hominis nativitatem, id est, fontaliter ex sapientia et omnipotentia sua instituit modum et processum generationis humanæ. Propter quod sanctus Job ait ad Dominum : Nonne sicut lac mulsisti me, et sicut caseum me coagulasti ? etc. Quique omnium invenit, id est, aliunde non accepit nec didicit, sed ex fonte sapientiæ suæ immensæ instituit, originem, hoc est exordium et processum cunctorum, inceptionem, cursum et ordinem universorum. Juxta hunc sensum in Baruch scriptum est : Qui fecit stellas, hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ. Apostolus quoque : Ex ipso, inquit, et per ipsum, et in ipso sunt omnia. Atque Isaias : Cum quo iniit consilium, et instruxit eum ? Et spiritum vobis iterum cum misericordia reddet et vitam, id est, in resurrectione futura misericorditer rursus conjunget animas vestras intellectuales corporibus vestris : sicque vitam restituet vobis, et glorificabit corpus et animam ; sicut nunc vos ipsos despicitis, id est, morti huic despicabili exponitis, propter leges ejus, id est, ut ejus impleatis præcepta.
paras.en: But it is [[7:23|the Creator of the world, that formed the nativity of man|mundi Creator, qui formavit hominis nativitatem]], that is, who from the fountain of his wisdom and omnipotence established the manner and process of human generation. Wherefore holy Job says to the Lord: [[Job 10:10|Hast thou not milked me as milk, and curdled me like cheese?|Nonne sicut lac mulsisti me, et sicut caseum me coagulasti]] etc. And he it is [[7:23|that found out|Quique omnium invenit]] the origin of all: that is, he did not receive it or learn it from elsewhere, but established it from the fountain of his own immense wisdom; [[7:23|the origin|originem]], that is, the beginning and process of all things, the inception, course and order of the universe. In this sense it is written in Baruch: He that made the stars[[Bar 3:35||]], [[Bar 3:37|He found out all the way of knowledge|hic adinvenit omnem viam disciplinæ]] [the margin's numbers are misread (Baruch, 35, 3); Denis joins Bar 3:35, where the stars shine 'to him that made them', to Bar 3:37]. The Apostle too: [[Rom 11:36|of him|Ex ipso]], he says, [[Rom 11:36|and by him, and in him, are all things|et per ipsum, et in ipso sunt omnia]]. And Isaias: [[Is 40:14|With whom hath he consulted, and who hath instructed him|Cum quo iniit consilium, et instruxit eum]]? [[7:23|he will restore to you again, in his mercy, both breath and life|Et spiritum vobis iterum cum misericordia reddet et vitam]], that is, in the resurrection to come he will mercifully join your intellectual souls to your bodies again: and so he will restore life to you, and will glorify body and soul; [[7:23|as now you despise yourselves|sicut nunc vos ipsos despicitis]], that is, expose yourselves to this despicable death, [[7:23|for the sake of his laws|propter leges ejus]], that is, so as to fulfil his precepts.

paras.t: Antiochus autem contemni se arbitratus a fratribus interfectis, a quibus fuit acriter increpatus, imo et aspernatus secundum quod vitiosus : juxta illud in Psalmo, Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus ; simul et exprobrantis voce despecta, id est, despiciens ipse Antiochus verba fratrum exprobrantium sibi, sicut despexit eorum personas. Sicque reputavit se despectum, primo, quia sic fuit reprehensus ab illis ; secundo, quia a tam vilibus secundum suam æstimationem fuit contemptus. Quum adhuc adolescentior superesset, ut saltem vinceret illum sua persuasione, non solum verbis hortabatur, sed et cum juramento affirmabat se divitem et beatum facturum illum, id est prosperum in præsentibus bonis, et felicem secundum suam superstitionem.
paras.en: [[7:24|Now Antiochus, thinking himself despised|Antiochus autem contemni se arbitratus]] by the brothers who had been slain, by whom he had been sharply rebuked, and indeed spurned, as being wicked, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 14:4|In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing|Ad nihilum deductus est in conspectu ejus malignus]]; [[7:24|and withal despising the voice of the upbraider|simul et exprobrantis voce despecta]], that is, Antiochus himself despising the words of the brothers who upbraided him, as he despised their persons. And so he thought himself despised: first, because he had been so reproved by them; secondly, because he had been scorned by men so mean in his own estimation. [[7:24|when the youngest was yet alive|Quum adhuc adolescentior superesset]], so as at least to overcome him by his persuasion, he [[7:24|did not only exhort him by words, but also assured him with an oath, that he would make him a rich and a happy man|non solum verbis hortabatur, sed et cum juramento affirmabat se divitem et beatum facturum illum]], that is, prosperous in present goods, and happy according to his superstition.

paras.t: Sed quum ad hæc adolescens nequaquam inclinaretur, vocavit rex matrem, ut adolescenti fieret in salutem, id est, persuaderet filio suo evadere mortem, et sanitatem ac prosperitatem hujus vitæ eligere. Quum autem multis verbis eam esset hortatus, promisit se mater suasuram filio suo, non tamen secundum regis intentionem, sed secundum veram dilectionem. Suasit etenim filio suo, ut veram amplecteretur salutem, et propter eam subiret mortem. Et ait filio : Miserere mei, id est, non permittas me in maximum labi mœrorem, obediendo huic tyranno, quæ te novem mensibus in utero portavi, etc. Peto, nate, ut adspicias ad cœlum et terram, et ad omnia quæ in eis sunt, et intelligas quia ex nihilo fecit illa Deus omnia. Ita fiet, id est, ex hoc concipies tantum timorem, dilectionem, et venerationem ad proprium Creatorem, ut non timeas carnificem istum, qui sic dilaniat homines, sicut carnifices bruta ; sed dignus fratribus tuis effectus particeps, id est, per constantiam promerens eorum frater vocari, non solum carne, sed et religione atque martyrio, suscipe mortem patienter et libenter propter Deum, ut in illa miseratione, id est in futura pia remuneratione ac coronatione, cum fratribus tuis te recipiam, id est, tibi rursus conjungar, et nunquam amplius a te separer, atque ex tua associatione plenius glorier ac jucunder, consors et particeps gloriæ tuæ : et tanto plus, quanto magis te diligo, et quo plus tibi cooperata sum ut pervenires ad tam beatificum finem.
paras.en: [[7:25|But when the young man was not moved with these things|Sed quum ad hæc adolescens nequaquam inclinaretur]], [[7:25|the king called the mother|vocavit rex matrem]], [[7:25|to deal with the young man to save his life|ut adolescenti fieret in salutem]], that is, to persuade her son to escape death and to choose the health and prosperity of this life. [[7:26|And when he had exhorted her with many words|Quum autem multis verbis eam esset hortatus]], [[7:26|she promised that she would counsel her son|promisit se mater suasuram filio suo]]: not, however, according to the king's intention, but according to true love. For she persuaded her son to embrace the true salvation, and for its sake to undergo death. And she [[7:27|said|ait]] to her son: [[7:27|have pity upon me|Miserere mei]], that is, do not let me fall into the greatest grief by obeying this tyrant, [[7:27|that bore thee nine months in my womb|quæ te novem mensibus in utero portavi]], etc. [[7:28|I beseech thee, my son, look upon heaven and earth, and all that is in them, and consider that God made them out of nothing|Peto, nate, ut adspicias ad cœlum et terram, et ad omnia quæ in eis sunt, et intelligas quia ex nihilo fecit illa Deus omnia]]. [[7:29|So|Ita fiet]], that is, from this thou wilt conceive such fear, love and reverence toward thy own Creator, that [[7:29|thou shalt not fear this tormentor|ut non timeas carnificem istum]], who tears men to pieces as butchers do brute beasts [*carnifex*: 'executioner', and also 'butcher']; [[7:29|but being made a worthy partner with thy brethren|sed dignus fratribus tuis effectus particeps]], that is, deserving by thy constancy to be called their brother, not only in the flesh, but also in religion and in martyrdom, [[7:29|receive death|suscipe mortem]] patiently and willingly for God's sake, [[7:29|that in that mercy|ut in illa miseratione]], that is, in the loving reward and crowning to come, [[7:29|I may receive thee again with thy brethren|cum fratribus tuis te recipiam]], that is, that I may be joined to thee again and never more be parted from thee, and may glory and rejoice the more fully in thy company, a sharer and partner in thy glory: and the more so, the more I love thee, and the more I have worked with thee that thou mightest come to so blessed an end.

paras.t: Quum hæc illa tam optima ac strenuissima mater Spiritu Sancto repleta, adhuc diceret, ait adolescens, inflammatus eloquio dilectissimæ ac fidelissimæ matris : Quid sustinetis ? quasi dicat : Inaniter exspectatis quod acquiescam persuasionibus regis. Non obedio præcepto regis in re tam illicita, sed præcepto legis. Tu vero, Antioche, qui inventor omnis malitiæ factus es in Hebræos, id est excogitator et inflictor tantæ persecutionis ac seductionis et subversionis in populum Judæorum, quorum multos crudelissime occidisti, multos a lege Dei ad idololatriam pertraxisti, non effugies manum Dei, id est potestatem ejus vitia ulciscentem. Nos enim pro peccatis nostris hæc patimur : juxta sensum præhabitum ; et si nobis propter increpationem et correptionem Dominus noster modicum iratus est, id est, quia ex sua justitia castigavit nos propter peccata nostra citra condignum in sæculo isto, ne æternaliter pereamus, sed iterum reconciliabitur servis suis, id est, castigatis ignoscet, et post tot adversa tribuet prospera.
paras.en: [[7:30|While she|Quum hæc illa]], this most excellent and most valiant mother, filled with the Holy Ghost, [[7:30|was yet speaking these words|adhuc diceret]], [[7:30|the young man said|ait adolescens]], inflamed by the eloquence of his most loving and most faithful mother: [[7:30|For whom do you stay?|Quid sustinetis]] [the print reads *Quid*, 'what', with a footnote giving the variant *Quem*, 'whom', the word of the Vulgate] As if to say: You wait in vain for me to yield to the king's persuasions. [[7:30|I will not obey the commandment of the king|Non obedio præcepto regis]] in so unlawful a matter, [[7:30|but the commandment of the law|sed præcepto legis]]. [[7:31|But thou|Tu vero]], Antiochus, [[7:31|that hast been the author of all mischief against the Hebrews|qui inventor omnis malitiæ factus es in Hebræos]], that is, the deviser and inflicter of so great a persecution, seduction and subversion against the people of the Jews, many of whom thou hast most cruelly slain, and many drawn away from the law of God to idolatry, [[7:31|shalt not escape the hand of God|non effugies manum Dei]], that is, his power that punishes vices. [[7:32|For we suffer thus for our sins|Nos enim pro peccatis nostris hæc patimur]]: in the sense given above; [[7:33|And though the Lord, our God, is angry with us a little while, for our chastisement and correction|et si nobis propter increpationem et correptionem Dominus noster modicum iratus est]], that is, because in his justice he has chastised us for our sins less than we deserve in this world, so that we may not perish eternally, [[7:33|yet he will be reconciled again to his servants|sed iterum reconciliabitur servis suis]], that is, he will pardon them once chastised, and after so many adversities will grant prosperity.

paras.t: Tu autem, sceleste, id est scelerate, et omnium hominum flagitiosissime, vel absolute, vel quantum ad aliquid, præsertim quantum ad homines tunc viventes, noli frustra extolli vanis spebus, id est confidentiis falsis, quibus præsumis te magna et felicia atque victorias jugiter adepturum, in servos ejus inflammatus, id est, ira, odio, persecutione accensus contra Dei cultores. Non enim omnipotentis Dei judicium effugisti. Nam fratres mei modico dolore nunc sustentato, id est tolerato isto temporali mortis supplicio parvo, tam respectu præmii gloriosi ac sempiterni, quam infernalis tormenti, sub testamento æternæ vitæ effecti sunt, id est, sub firma promissione et certa exspectatione beatificæ fruitionis sunt constituti, quam in sinu Abrahæ infallibiliter præstolantur. Tu vero judicio Dei justas superbiæ tuæ pœnas exsolves. Ego autem trado me, invocans Deum maturius, id est cum gravitate internæ affectionis ; vel quod ait, Maturius, refertur ad verba sequentia, genti nostræ propitium fieri, id est, rogans Deum, ut celerius fiat clemens, et misericorditer agens populo Judæorum, et te cum tormentis et verberibus, id est plagis divinæ ultionis, confiteri, quod ipse est Deus solus. Hoc post paucos annos fuit impletum, et sic fuit exaudita oratio hujus sancti et magnanimi adolescentis, zelo justitiæ istud rogantis. In me autem et in fratribus meis desinet Omnipotentis ira, præsertim quum ad beatificam Dei pervenerimus visionem. Nam et in patribus exsistentibus in limbo, aliquo modo videtur mansisse ira Dei, in quantum propter originalis peccati reatum retardabantur a gloria : quæ retardatio fuit quædam peccati illius vindicta, et hæc ira Dei vocatur.
paras.en: [[7:34|But thou, O wicked|Tu autem, sceleste]], that is, criminal, [[7:34|and of all men most flagitious|et omnium hominum flagitiosissime]], either absolutely or in some respect, above all with regard to the men then living, [[7:34|be not lifted up without cause with vain hopes|noli frustra extolli vanis spebus]], that is, with false confidences, by which thou presumest that thou wilt always win great and happy things and victories, [[7:34|whilst thou art raging against his servants|in servos ejus inflammatus]], that is, kindled with anger, hatred and persecution against the worshippers of God. [[7:35|For thou hast not yet escaped the judgment of the Almighty God|Non enim omnipotentis Dei judicium effugisti]]. [[7:36|For my brethren having now undergone a short pain|Nam fratres mei modico dolore nunc sustentato]], that is, having borne this temporal punishment of death, which is small both in respect of the glorious and everlasting reward and in respect of the torment of hell, [[7:36|are under the covenant of eternal life|sub testamento æternæ vitæ effecti sunt]], that is, they are set under a firm promise and a sure expectation of the beatific enjoyment, which they await without fail in the bosom of Abraham. [[7:36|but thou, by the judgment of God, shalt receive just punishment for thy pride|Tu vero judicio Dei justas superbiæ tuæ pœnas exsolves]]. [[7:37|But I|Ego autem]] give myself up, [[7:37|calling upon God|invocans Deum]] *maturius*, that is, with the gravity of inward affection [*maturius* means 'more speedily', and also 'more maturely, more gravely', whence Denis's first reading]; or else what he says, *maturius*, belongs to the words that follow, [[7:37|to be speedily merciful to our nation|genti nostræ propitium fieri]], that is, asking God that he may the sooner become clement and deal mercifully with the people of the Jews, [[7:37|and that thou by torments and stripes|et te cum tormentis et verberibus]], that is, by the blows of divine vengeance, [[7:37|mayst confess that he alone is God|confiteri, quod ipse est Deus solus]]. This was fulfilled a few years later[[2 Mach 9:5||]], and so the prayer of this holy and great-souled youth was heard, who asked it out of zeal for justice. [[7:38|But in me, and in my brethren|In me autem et in fratribus meis]] [[7:38|shall cease|desinet]] [[7:38|the wrath of the Almighty|Omnipotentis ira]], above all when we have come to the beatific vision of God. For in the fathers too who were in limbo the wrath of God seems in some way to have remained, inasmuch as they were held back from glory because of the guilt of original sin: and this delay was a certain punishment of that sin, and it is called the wrath of God.

paras.t: Tunc rex accensus ira, in hunc crudelius desævit, etc. Novissime autem et mater post filios consumpta est, id est feliciter mortua, et (ut creditur) martyrizata.
paras.en: [[7:39|Then the king being incensed with anger, raged against him more cruelly|Tunc rex accensus ira, in hunc crudelius desævit]], etc. [[7:41|And last of all, after the sons, the mother also was consumed|Novissime autem et mater post filios consumpta est]], that is, she died happily, and (as is believed) by martyrdom.

paras.t: His verbis Magister in historiis addit : Pro hac tanti prærogativa martyrii, asserunt plurimi, de his septem fratribus Ecclesiam solennizare.
paras.en: To these words the Master in the Histories [Peter Comestor, in the *Historia scholastica*] adds: Because of the privilege of so great a martyrdom, many assert, the Church keeps a solemn feast of these seven brothers.

paras.t: Præterea, si in veteri Testamento, janua regni cœlestis nondum aperta, tam fervidi erant electissimi fratres isti ad sustinendum tam acerbum martyrium : quanto magis sub evangelica lege, aditu regni superni patefacto, debemus esse fervidi ac parati ad tolerandum quæcumque adversa, imo et amarissimas mortes pro Deo ?
paras.en: Moreover, if in the Old Testament, when the gate of the heavenly kingdom was not yet open, these most chosen brothers were so fervent to endure so bitter a martyrdom: how much more, under the law of the Gospel, now that the way into the kingdom above has been thrown open, ought we to be fervent and ready to bear any adversities whatever, nay, even the bitterest deaths, for God?

paras.t: Amplius, hujus venerandæ matris exemplo discant parentes sobolem suam vero, sancto et spirituali, non carnali aut sensuali amore diligere, eamque salubriter informare, nec a religionis ingressu (quæ est mors civilis atque martyrium quoddam) retrahere.
paras.en: Further, by the example of this venerable mother let parents learn to love their offspring with a true, holy and spiritual love, not with a carnal or sensual one, and to form them wholesomely, and not to hold them back from entering religion (which is a civil death [that is, a death in law: the religious leaves the world and its civil affairs] and a kind of martyrdom).

paras.t: Postremo, quoniam septenario universitas designatur, possunt per septem hos martyres, universi evangelicæ legis martyres figurari. Et sicut post martyres illos consummata est mater eorum, ita post eorum martyria qui in fine mundi sunt ab Antichristo et suis ministris martyrizandi, sancta mater Ecclesia consummabitur tota in gloria plena. Demum in novo Testamento invenitur simile præfato martyrio in beatissima femina Felicitate, et septem filiis ejus martyribus gloriosissime coronatis.
paras.en: Lastly, since the number seven signifies the whole, all the martyrs of the law of the Gospel can be figured by these seven martyrs. And as their mother was consummated after those martyrs [*consummata*, 'brought to completion', echoing *consumpta*, 'consumed', of v. 41], so, after the martyrdoms of those who at the end of the world are to be martyred by Antichrist and his ministers, holy Mother Church will be wholly consummated in full glory. Finally, in the New Testament a martyrdom like the one described is found in the most blessed woman Felicity and her seven sons, martyrs most gloriously crowned.

8.title: Elucidatio capituli octavi: Judas vero Machabæus, et qui cum illo erant, introibant latenter in castella
8.title_en: Explanation of the eighth chapter: But Judas Machabeus, and they that were with him, went privately into the towns

paras.t: Quoniam Deus gloriosus post tempestatem tranquillitatem largitur, describitur hic qualiter populum suum lamentabiliter conculcatum cœpit mirabiliter exaltare, fecitque triumphare. Et quæ hic scribuntur, in primo libro præhabita sunt.
paras.en: Since the glorious God gives calm after the storm, it is described here how he began wonderfully to exalt his people, who had been pitiably trodden down, and made them triumph. And what is written here has been told already in the first book[[1 Mach 3:1||]] [the margin's chapter number is unclear, perhaps iii].

paras.t: Judas vero Machabæus, et qui cum illo erant, videlicet fratres et consanguinei ejus, et qui in Judaismo permanserunt, introibant latenter in castella Judææ, quæ gentiles ministri Antiochi obtinuerunt et inhabitaverunt ad tempus injuste. Idcirco latenter et nocturnis temporibus ac per insidias poterant expugnari. Et invocabant Dominum, ut vocem sanguinis ad se clamantis audiret. Oppressio enim et interfectio innocentium, est unum de quatuor peccatis clamantibus ante Deum, quæ specialiter exigunt desuper fieri ultionem.
paras.en: [[8:1|But Judas Machabeus, and they that were with him|Judas vero Machabæus, et qui cum illo erant]], namely his brothers and kinsmen, and [[8:1|such as continued in the Jews' religion|et qui in Judaismo permanserunt]], [[8:1|went privately into the towns|introibant latenter in castella]] of Judea, which the gentile ministers of Antiochus had taken and for a time unjustly inhabited. For this reason they could be taken by storm secretly, at night and by ambush. [[8:2|And they called upon the Lord|Et invocabant Dominum]], that he [[8:3|would hear the voice of the blood that cried to him|vocem sanguinis ad se clamantis audiret]]. For the oppression and slaying of the innocent is one of the four sins crying out before God, which in a special way demand that vengeance be done from on high.

paras.t: Videns autem Philippus, quem Antiochus in Jerusalem posuit principem ad affligendum Judæos, ut dictum est ante, paulatim virum ad provectum venire, id est Judam successive magis ac magis prævalere, ad Ptolemæum ducem Cœlesyriæ et Phœnicis scripsit. Quæritur, an iste Philippus, fuerit cui in primo libro legitur Antiochus suum filium commisisse. Et dicunt quidam, quod imo. Contra quos objicit quidam: Primo, quoniam iste Philippus fuit in Jerusalem; alius autem, cum rege in Perside, quando factum est bellum istud. Secundo, quoniam iste fuit Phryx natione, ut patuit ante; alter autem erat collactaneus Antiochi, ut capitulo fertur sequenti. Sed istæ objectiones videntur inanes. Si enim bene pensentur quæ hic et tertio primi libri capitulo scripta sunt, missio ista ad Ptolemæum facta per Philippum, præcessit iter Antiochi ad Persidem. Ad aliam posset quis dicere, quod Philippus iste ex uno latere exstitit Phryx, ex alio collactaneus regis. Verumtamen parva est vis, an fuerit idem an alter.
paras.en: [[8:8|Then Philip seeing|Videns autem Philippus]], whom Antiochus had set as governor in Jerusalem to afflict the Jews, as was said before[[2 Mach 5:22||]], [[8:8|that the man gained ground by little and little|paulatim virum ad provectum venire]] [the margin gives the Vulgate's *profectum* beside Denis's *provectum*; both mean 'advance'], that is, that Judas was prevailing more and more, [[8:8|wrote to Ptolemee, the governor of Celesyria and Phenicia|ad Ptolemæum ducem Cœlesyriæ et Phœnicis scripsit]]. It is asked whether this Philip was the one to whom, as we read in the first book, Antiochus committed his son[[1 Mach 6:14||]]. And some say that he was. Against them someone objects: first, that this Philip was in Jerusalem, but the other with the king in Persia, when this war was waged. Secondly, that this one was a Phrygian by nation, as appeared before[[2 Mach 5:22||]], but the other was the foster-brother of Antiochus, as is told in the next chapter[[2 Mach 9:29||]]. But these objections seem empty. For if what is written here and in the third chapter of the first book[[1 Mach 3:31||]] is well weighed, this sending to Ptolemee by Philip came before the journey of Antiochus into Persia. To the other someone could say that this Philip was a Phrygian on one side, and on the other the king's foster-brother. Yet it matters little whether he was the same or another.

paras.t: At ille, scilicet Ptolemæus, velociter misit Nicanorem, datis ei viginti millibus, etc., adjuncto Gorgia. Videtur ista historia dissonare a dictis in primo libro, quum scriptum sit ibi: Elegit Lysias Ptolemæum et Nicanorem et Gorgiam, et misit cum eis quadraginta millia virorum et septem millia equitum. Porro, quod hic et ibi de eodem bello fit sermo, constat ex eo quod additur ibi et hic de conventione mercatorum ad emendum Judæos, quos præsupponebant vincendos. Nam subditur hic: Constituit autem Nicanor regi, id est, ad commodum regis Antiochi ordinavit, vel regi ante suum recessum asseruit, ut tributum, quod erat dandum Romanis, quibus tributarius fuit Antiochus, de captivitate Judæorum suppleret, id est, de pecunia quam accepturum se præsumpsit pro Judæis vendendis, promittens se nonaginta mancipia, id est servos seu supposita, Judæorum, talento distracturum, id est pro uno talento daturum ac undique dispersurum. Ad istud respondendum videtur, quod Philippus primo scripserit Ptolemæo, a quo missa fuerunt viginti millia: quibus paulo post, ante congressum contra Judam, Lysias addidit alia viginti millia, et equitum millia septem.
paras.en: [[8:9|And he with all speed sent Nicanor|At ille, scilicet Ptolemæus, velociter misit Nicanorem]], namely Ptolemee, [[8:9|giving him no fewer than twenty thousand|datis ei viginti millibus]], etc., [[8:9|joining also with him Gorgias|adjuncto Gorgia]]. This history seems to disagree with what is said in the first book, since it is written there: [[1 Mach 3:38|Then Lysias chose Ptolemee|Elegit Lysias Ptolemæum]], [[1 Mach 3:38|and Nicanor, and Gorgias|et Nicanorem et Gorgiam]], [[1 Mach 3:39|And he sent with them forty thousand men, and seven thousand horsemen|et misit cum eis quadraginta millia virorum et septem millia equitum]]. Now that the same war is spoken of here and there is clear from what is added there and here about the gathering of merchants to buy the Jews[[1 Mach 3:41||]], whom they took for granted would be conquered. For it follows here: [[8:10|And Nicanor purposed|Constituit autem Nicanor]] [[8:10|for the king|regi]], that is, arranged for the profit of King Antiochus, or assured the king before his departure, that he would make up [[8:10|the tribute|ut tributum]] [[8:10|that was to be given to the Romans|quod erat dandum Romanis]], to whom Antiochus was tributary, [[8:10|by making so much money of the captive Jews|de captivitate Judæorum suppleret]], that is, from the money he presumed he would receive for selling the Jews, [[8:11|promising that they should have ninety slaves|promittens se nonaginta mancipia]], that is, servants or underlings, of the Jews, [[8:11|for one talent|talento distracturum]], that is, that he would give them for one talent and scatter them everywhere. To this it seems the answer should be that Philip first wrote to Ptolemee, by whom twenty thousand were sent; and to these, a little later, before the engagement with Judas, Lysias added another twenty thousand, and seven thousand horsemen.

paras.t: Ex quibus, scilicet Judæis cum Juda exsistentibus, quidam formidantes, propter multitudinem adversariorum, et non credentes divinæ justitiæ, id est non satis sperantes quod justitia Dei eis auxiliaretur, eorumque inimicis adversaretur, in fugam vertebantur. Alii vero Dominum deprecabantur, ut eriperet eos de impio Nicanore, qui eos priusquam cominus, id est prope, veniret, vendiderat dicendo quod daret nonaginta mancipia Judæorum pro talento; et si non propter eos, id est si non propter ipsorum merita, sed tamen propter testamentum quod erat ad patres eorum, id est propter conservationem veteris Testamenti in suo vigore, vel propter adimpletionem promissionis factæ Patriarchis de conservanda eorum posteritate.
paras.en: [[8:13|And some of them|Ex quibus quidam]], namely of the Jews who were with Judas, [[8:13|being afraid|formidantes]] because of the multitude of their adversaries, [[8:13|and distrusting the justice of God|et non credentes divinæ justitiæ]], that is, not hoping enough that the justice of God would help them and oppose their enemies, [[8:13|fled away|in fugam vertebantur]]. [[8:14|Others sold all that they had left, and withal besought the Lord|Alii vero Dominum deprecabantur]], [[8:14|that he would deliver them from the wicked Nicanor|ut eriperet eos de impio Nicanore]], who, [[8:14|before he came near them|priusquam cominus]] (*near*, that is, close at hand), [[8:14|had sold them|vendiderat]] by saying that he would give ninety slaves of the Jews for a talent; [[8:15|And if not for their sakes|et si non propter eos]], that is, if not for their own merits, [[8:15|yet for the covenant that he had made with their fathers|sed tamen propter testamentum quod erat ad patres eorum]], that is, for the preserving of the Old Testament in its force, or for the fulfilling of the promise made to the Patriarchs that their posterity should be preserved [*testamentum* is both 'covenant' and 'testament'].

paras.t: Convocatis autem Machabæus septem millibus, qui cum ipso erant. Contra hoc objici potest, quoniam primo libro habetur, quod erant tria millia tantum. Respondetur, quod ibi numerantur qui ceteris magis erant armati. Rogabat ut fortiter contenderent, id est, pugnarent, ante oculos habentes, id est recordantes, contumeliam quæ in loco sancto esset illata, id est, quam perfidi illi intulerant templo; itemque injuriam civitatis Jerusalem habitæ ludibrio et contemptui; adhuc etiam veterum instituta convulsa, id est, præcepta patribus data, esse violata. Vel, per veterum instituta, intelligendæ sunt ordinationes aliquæ a Judæorum senioribus factæ. Itaque, propter tanta adversariorum facinora, eos crederent expugnandos.
paras.en: [[8:16|But Machabeus calling together seven thousand that were with him|Convocatis autem Machabæus septem millibus, qui cum ipso erant]]. Against this it can be objected that in the first book it is said there were only three thousand[[1 Mach 4:6||]]. The answer is that there those are counted who were better armed than the rest. He [[8:16|exhorted them|Rogabat]] [[8:16|to fight manfully|ut fortiter contenderent]], that is, to do battle: [[8:17|Setting before their eyes|ante oculos habentes]], that is, remembering, [[8:17|the injury they had unjustly done the holy place|contumeliam quæ in loco sancto esset illata]], that is, which those faithless men had done to the temple; [[8:17|and also the injury they had done to the city, which had been shamefully abused|itemque injuriam civitatis Jerusalem habitæ ludibrio]] and contempt; [[8:17|besides their destroying the ordinances of the fathers|adhuc etiam veterum instituta convulsa]], that is, that the precepts given to the fathers had been violated. Or by *the ordinances of the fathers* [literally 'of the ancients'] are to be understood certain ordinances made by the elders of the Jews. And so, because of such great crimes of their adversaries, they should believe that these must be overcome.

paras.t: Admonuit autem eos de auxiliis Dei, id est, qualiter Deus adjuvit frequenter patres eorum, sicut in Exodo, Judicum, Regum, et Paralipomenon libris narratur; et de prælio quod eis adversus Galatas fuit in Babylonia, ubi ut ad rem, id est ad pugnam, ventum est, Macedonibus sociis hæsitantibus, id est metuentibus Macedonibus exsistentibus cum Judæis, ipsi Judæi soli exsistentes sex millia, peremerunt centum viginti millia. De isto bello non legitur alibi in Scripturis, neque in Josepho: et tamen mirabilius fuisse videtur, quod in primo libro leguntur tria millia Judæorum missa a Jonatha regi Demetrio, occidisse in Antiochia centum millia hominum.
paras.en: [[8:19|Moreover, he put them in mind also of the helps their fathers had received from God|Admonuit autem eos de auxiliis Dei]], that is, how God often helped their fathers, as is told in the books of Exodus, Judges, Kings and Paralipomenon; [[8:20|And of the battle that they had fought against the Galatians, in Babylonia|et de prælio quod eis adversus Galatas fuit in Babylonia]], where, [[8:20|when it came to the point|ut ad rem]], that is, to the fight, [[8:20|and the Macedonians, their companions, were at a stand|Macedonibus sociis hæsitantibus]], that is, when the Macedonians who were with the Jews were afraid, [[8:20|they, being in all but six thousand|ipsi Judæi soli exsistentes sex millia]], the Jews being alone, [[8:20|slew a hundred and twenty thousand|peremerunt centum viginti millia]]. This war is not read of elsewhere in the Scriptures, nor in Josephus: and yet it seems to have been more wonderful that, as we read in the first book, three thousand Jews sent by Jonathan to King Demetrius slew a hundred thousand men at Antioch[[1 Mach 11:44||]][[1 Mach 11:48||]].

paras.t: Constituit itaque fratres suos duces utrique ordini, unicuique eorum commisso. Et dicunt aliqui, quod in quolibet ordine seu acie erant aliqui equites, et quidam pedestres, quum tamen nec in isto, neque in libro primo legatur Judas equis usus in præliis. Simonem et Josephum et Jonathan. Josephus iste dicitur fuisse is, qui primo libro Eleazarus appellatur: quem duodecimo libro Antiquitatum Josephus nominat Saphum.
paras.en: [[8:22|So he appointed his brethren captains over each division of his army|Constituit itaque fratres suos duces utrique ordini]], each of them being given his charge. And some say that in each division or line there were some horsemen and some foot soldiers, though neither in this book nor in the first is Judas read to have used horses in his battles. [[8:22|Simon, and Joseph, and Jonathan|Simonem et Josephum et Jonathan]]. This Joseph is said to have been the one who in the first book is called Eleazar[[1 Mach 2:5||]] [the margin's numbers are unclear], whom Josephus, in the twelfth book of the Antiquities, names *Saphus* [the name is unclear in the scan].

paras.t: Ad hoc etiam ab Esdra lecto sancto libro. Iste fuit alter ab Esdra de Babylone reverso. Itaque Esdras iste legit ex libro Moysis aliqua verba pro pugnatorum confortatione, juxta illud Deuteronomii: Appropinquante prælio, stabit sacerdos ante aciem, et loquetur: Audi, Israel, nolite timere, quia Dominus in medio vestri est. Et dato signo de adjutorio Dei eis mox adfuturo. Quod signum potuit esse clangor tubarum in ipso congressu, juxta illud Numerorum: Si exieritis ad bellum, clangetis ululantibus tubis, et erit recordatio vestri coram Domino, ut eruamini de manibus inimicorum vestrorum. In prima acie ipse dux, scilicet Judas, commisit cum Nicanore, id est contra Nicanorem et aciem ejus.
paras.en: [[8:23|And after the holy book had been read to them by Esdras|Ad hoc etiam ab Esdra lecto sancto libro]]. This was another Esdras than the one who returned from Babylon. So this Esdras read some words from the book of Moses to strengthen the fighters, according to that of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 20:2|And when the battle is now at hand, the priest shall stand before the army|Appropinquante prælio, stabit sacerdos ante aciem]], [[Deut 20:2|and shall speak|et loquetur]]: [[Deut 20:3|Hear, O Israel|Audi, Israel]], [[Deut 20:3|be not afraid|nolite timere]], [[Deut 20:4|Because the Lord your God is in the midst of you|quia Dominus in medio vestri est]] [Denis quotes loosely, drawing the words together from Deut 20:2–4]. And [[8:23|he had given them for a watchword, The help of God|dato signo de adjutorio Dei]] that would soon be with them. That signal may have been the blast of the trumpets at the very engagement, according to that of Numbers: [[Num 10:9|If you go forth to war|Si exieritis ad bellum]], [[Num 10:9|you shall sound aloud with the trumpets, and there shall be a remembrance of you before the Lord|clangetis ululantibus tubis, et erit recordatio vestri coram Domino]], [[Num 10:9|that you may be delivered out of the hands of your enemies|ut eruamini de manibus inimicorum vestrorum]]. Then, [[8:23|himself leading the first band, he joined battle with Nicanor|In prima acie ipse dux, scilicet Judas, commisit cum Nicanore]], namely Judas, that is, against Nicanor and his line.

paras.t: Et facto sibi adjutore Omnipotente, interfecerunt Judas et sui super novem millia hominum. Verumtamen primo libro habetur, Tria millia. Ad quod respondetur, quod in acie Nicanoris tria millia corruerunt; in toto autem adversariorum exercitu, novem millia. Sed reversi sunt Judas et sui hora conclusi, id est detenti, quoniam imminebat hora in qua cœpit celebratio sabbati: in quo quamvis potuerunt pugnare se defendendo, non tamen sponte et sine necessitate alios invadendo aut insequendo.
paras.en: [[8:24|And the Almighty being their helper|Et facto sibi adjutore Omnipotente]], Judas and his men [[8:24|slew above nine thousand men|interfecerunt super novem millia hominum]]. Yet in the first book it says, three thousand[[1 Mach 4:15||]]. To which the answer is that in Nicanor's line three thousand fell, but in the whole army of the adversaries nine thousand. [[8:26|But they came back|Sed reversi sunt]], Judas and his men, [[8:26|for want of time|hora conclusi]], that is, held back, since the hour was at hand in which the keeping of the sabbath began: on which, although they could fight in defending themselves, they could not of their own will and without need attack or pursue others.

paras.t: Et ex his qui cum Timotheo et Bacchide erant contra se contendentes, id est contra ipsos Judæos pugnantes, super viginti millia interfecerunt Judæi cum principe suo Juda. De isto bello habetur primo libro. Ibi tamen habetur, Octo millia; sed additur ibi de alio bello, et poterant simul esse plus quam viginti millia. Ibi tamen non fit sermo de Bacchide; putantque aliqui quod Bacchides iste sit alter ab illo, quem in primo libro legitur cum Alcimo misisse Demetrius. Et quum arma eorum collegissent, diligenter omnia composuerunt in locis opportunis, ut suo tempore uterentur eisdem.
paras.en: And [[8:30|of them that were with Timotheus and Bacchides, who fought against them|Et ex his qui cum Timotheo et Bacchide erant contra se contendentes]], that is, fighting against the Jews themselves, the Jews with their leader Judas [[8:30|slew above twenty thousand|super viginti millia interfecerunt]]. This war is told of in the first book. Yet there it says, eight thousand[[1 Mach 5:34||]] [the margin gives 1 Mach. v]; but another battle is added there, and together they could come to more than twenty thousand. There, however, nothing is said of Bacchides; and some think that this Bacchides is another than the one whom, as we read in the first book, Demetrius sent with Alcimus[[1 Mach 7:8||]]. [[8:31|And when they had carefully gathered together their arms, they laid them all up in convenient places|Et quum arma eorum collegissent, diligenter omnia composuerunt in locis opportunis]], to use them in their time.

paras.t: Et quum epinicia, id est festa de victoriis contra hostes obtentis, ad regratiandum Deo, agerentur in Jerusalem, eos qui sacras januas templi incenderant, id est, Callisthenem, qui fuit in hoc principalis, incenderunt, etc. Facinorosissimus autem Nicanor, qui mille negotiantes, id est mercatores, ad Judæorum venditionem a se faciendam adduxerat. Porro an mercatores illi fuerunt mille dumtaxat, an plures, ita quod ponatur hic numerus determinatus pro indeterminato, videtur ambiguum. Humiliatus auxilio Domini ab his, quos nullos existimaverat, deposita veste gloriæ, id est veste sua pretiosa, ne agnosceretur, per mediterranea fugiens secretius quo valebat, solus venit Antiochiam, etc., vel quia omnino solus, vel quia cum paucis venit illuc; et prædicabat protectorem Deum habere Judæos. Hoc dixit, suam dejectionem excusando magis quam Deum laudando.
paras.en: [[8:33|And when they kept the feast of the victory|Et quum epinicia]], that is, the feasts for victories won over the enemy, held to give thanks to God, [[8:33|at Jerusalem|agerentur in Jerusalem]], [[8:33|they burnt Callisthenes, that had set fire to the holy gates|eos qui sacras januas templi incenderant, id est, Callisthenem]] [Denis's text reads 'those who had set fire to the holy gates of the temple, that is, Callisthenes'], who was the chief in this, etc. [[8:34|But as for that most wicked man, Nicanor, who had brought a thousand merchants|Facinorosissimus autem Nicanor, qui mille negotiantes]], that is, traders, [[8:34|to the sale of the Jews|ad Judæorum venditionem]] which he was to make. Whether those merchants were a thousand only, or more, so that a definite number is put here for an indefinite one, seems doubtful. [[8:35|Being, through the help of the Lord, brought down by them, of whom he had made no account|Humiliatus auxilio Domini ab his, quos nullos existimaverat]], [[8:35|laying aside his garment of glory|deposita veste gloriæ]], that is, his costly garment, so as not to be recognized, [[8:35|fleeing through the midland country|per mediterranea fugiens]] as secretly as he could, [[8:35|he came alone to Antioch|solus venit Antiochiam]], etc., either because he came there quite alone, or with few; [[8:36|now professed that the Jews had God for their protector|prædicabat protectorem Deum habere Judæos]]. This he said rather to excuse his own downfall than to praise God.

9.title: Explanatio capituli noni: Eodem tempore Antiochus inhoneste revertebatur de Perside.
9.title_en: Explanation of the ninth chapter: At that time Antiochus returned with dishonour out of Persia.

paras.t: Mors sceleratissimi Antiochi hoc loco describitur. Eodem tempore Antiochus inhoneste revertebatur de Perside. Intraverat enim eam urbem quæ dicitur Persepolis, quæ primo libro Elymaides nuncupatur: quam cur introierit, dictum est ibi. Et quum venisset circa Ecbatanam civitatem, etc.: de qua fit mentio in Judith et Esdræ libris. Jussit agitari currum sine intermissione: ut molestiam sibi factam in Judæis ulcisceretur; cælesti eo judicio perurgente, id est, Deo cæli justo judicio permittente impium illum sic furere contra Judæos, et ex consequenti præcipere currum sic agitari, ad quod consecuta est ruina et conquassatio corporis sui: quod fuit effective a Deo, qui permisit illum sic insanire, quatenus hanc plagam incurreret, eo quod ita superbe locutus est venturum se Jerosolymam, et congeriem, id est collectionem et cumulum, sepulcri Judæorum eam facturum, hoc est, quod occideret universos in Jerusalem commorantes Judæos, ita quod ipsa fieret occisorum sepulcrum.
paras.en: The death of the most wicked Antiochus is described in this place. [[9:1|At that time Antiochus returned with dishonour out of Persia|Eodem tempore Antiochus inhoneste revertebatur de Perside]]. [[9:2|For he had entered into the city called Persepolis|Intraverat enim eam urbem quæ dicitur Persepolis]], which in the first book is called Elymais[[1 Mach 6:1||]] [the margin note here could not be read; Elymais is named at 1 Mach 6:1]: why he entered it was said there. [[9:3|Now when he was come about Ecbatana|Et quum venisset circa Ecbatanam]] the city, etc.: which is mentioned in the books of Judith[[Jdt 1:1||]] and Esdras[[1 Esd 6:2||]] [the margin notes here are partly unreadable; Ecbatana is named at Judith 1:1 and 1 Esdras 6:2]. [[9:4|he commanded his chariot to be driven, without stopping|Jussit agitari currum sine intermissione]], to avenge upon the Jews the trouble done to him; [[9:4|the judgment of heaven urging him forward|cælesti eo judicio perurgente]], that is, God by the just judgment of heaven permitting that wicked man so to rage against the Jews, and in consequence to order the chariot to be driven so, which was followed by the ruin and shattering of his body: and this was the work of God [Latin *effective*: God was its efficient cause], who permitted him so to rage that he might incur this plague, [[9:4|because he had spoken so proudly|eo quod ita superbe locutus est]] [[9:4|that he would come to Jerusalem|venturum se Jerosolymam]], [[9:4|and make it a common|et congeriem]] heap (that is, a collection and pile), a [[9:4|burying place of the Jews|sepulcri Judæorum eam facturum]]: that is, that he would slay all the Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, so that the city itself would become the sepulchre of the slain.

paras.t: Sed qui universa conspicit Dominus Deus, percussit eum insanabili et invisibili plaga, quæ intra viscera fuit latens. Non tamen fuit correctus. Ut enim finivit hunc sermonem, apprehendit eum dolor dirus viscerum. Et quidem satis juste, etc.
paras.en: [[9:5|But the Lord, the God of Israel, that seeth all things, struck him with an incurable and an invisible plague|Sed qui universa conspicit Dominus Deus, percussit eum insanabili et invisibili plaga]], which lay hidden within his bowels. Yet he was not corrected. [[9:5|For as soon as he had ended these words, a dreadful pain in his bowels|Ut enim finivit hunc sermonem, apprehendit eum dolor dirus viscerum]]. [[9:6|And indeed very justly|Et quidem satis juste]], etc.

paras.t: Super hæc autem et superbia repletus, ignem iracundiæ, indignationis, impatientiæ, animo spirans, id est evaporans animo, id est corde et etiam corpore per verba comminatoria turbulentosque gestus, in Judæos: sicut de nequissimo Daciano sanctus recitat Augustinus; contigit illum impetu euntem, id est celerrime procedentem in sua quadriga, de curru cadere: et forsan currus reversabatur. Isque qui sibi videbatur fluctibus maris imperare, supra humanum modum superbia repletus, et montium altitudines in statera appendere, etc., id est, tam superbe se habuit, ac si hoc putasset. Estque iste sermo hyperbolicus, ad innuendum inhumanum fastum et arrogantiam ejus. In gestatorio, id est instrumento facto ad portandum, portabatur.
paras.en: [[9:7|Moreover, being filled with pride|Super hæc autem et superbia repletus]], [[9:7|breathing out fire|ignem]] of wrath, indignation and impatience [[9:7|in his rage|animo spirans]], that is, breathing it out in mind (that is, in heart) and also in body, by threatening words and turbulent gestures, [[9:7|against the Jews|in Judæos]], as holy Augustine relates of the most wicked Dacian [the Roman governor in Spain who martyred St Vincent the deacon, of whom Augustine speaks in his sermons on that saint]; [[9:7|it happened as he was going with violence|contigit illum impetu euntem]], that is, driving on at full speed in his four-horse chariot, [[9:7|that he fell from the chariot|de curru cadere]]: and perhaps the chariot was overturned. [[9:8|Thus he that seemed to himself to command even the waves of the sea|Isque qui sibi videbatur fluctibus maris imperare]], [[9:8|being proud above the condition of man|supra humanum modum superbia repletus]], [[9:8|and to weigh the heights of the mountains in a balance|et montium altitudines in statera appendere]], etc.: that is, he bore himself as proudly as if he had thought this. And this saying is hyperbolical, to hint at his inhuman haughtiness and arrogance. [[9:8|in a litter|In gestatorio]], that is, in a contrivance made for carrying, he [[9:8|was carried|portabatur]].

paras.t: Hinc ergo cœpit ex gravi deductus superbia, id est ex detestabili et importabili elatione ad extremam calamitatem dejectus, ad agnitionem sui venire; juxta illud Isaiæ, Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui. Unde per Jeremiam Dominus: Castigo te, inquit, ne tibi innoxius videaris. Et ait: Justum est subditum esse Deo, cujus justam vindictam in me ipso experior, et mortalem non paria Deo sentire: ex quo apparet, quod divinum quid impie sensit de se. Orabat autem scelestus hic Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam, id est veniam peccatorum et gratiam, consecuturus: quoniam ejus oratio et pœnitentia non provenit ex zelo justitiæ, neque ex caritate, neque ex odio culpæ, sed ex timore pure servili, et desiderio evadendi afflictiones corporales quas incidit. Sic et de Esau scribit Apostolus, quod non invenit pœnitentiæ locum, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam.
paras.en: [[9:11|And by this means, being brought from his great pride|Hinc ergo cœpit ex gravi deductus superbia]], that is, cast down from detestable and unbearable haughtiness into the uttermost calamity, [[9:11|he began to come to the knowledge of himself|ad agnitionem sui venire]]; according to that of Isaias: [[Is 28:19|vexation alone shall make you understand what you hear|Tantummodo sola vexatio dabit intellectum auditui]].
