Whence the Lord says by Jeremias: [[Jer 30:11|I will chastise thee|Castigo te]], he says, [[Jer 30:11|that thou mayst not seem to thyself innocent|ne tibi innoxius videaris]] [the margin reads as Jer. x, 11; the words are at Jer 30:11]. And he said: [[9:12|It is just to be subject to God|Justum est subditum esse Deo]], whose just vengeance I experience in myself, [[9:12|and that a mortal man should not equal himself to God|et mortalem non paria Deo sentire]]: from which it appears that he had impiously thought himself something divine. [[9:13|Then this wicked man prayed to the Lord, of whom he was not like to obtain mercy|Orabat autem scelestus hic Dominum, a quo non esset misericordiam]], that is, pardon of sins and grace: because his prayer and penance did not come from zeal for justice, nor from charity, nor from hatred of the fault, but from purely servile fear [that is, fear of punishment only, not the filial fear that dreads offending God], and from the desire to escape the bodily afflictions into which he had fallen. So too the Apostle writes of Esau that [[Heb 12:17|he found no place of repentance, although with tears he had sought it|non invenit pœnitentiæ locum, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam]].

paras.t: Deinde multa et magna promisit, ut misericordiam consequeretur, id est curationem et evasionem suppliciorum divini judicii. Et civitatem Jerusalem, quam paulo ante volebat facere sepulcrum congestorum, id est Judæorum occisorum simul accumulatorum, optat reddere liberam a tributo, ac Judæos æquales in privilegiis Atheniensibus facere pollicetur. Erant quippe Athenienses privilegiati et liberati in multis, quoniam philosophiæ studium viguit ibi.
paras.en: Then he promised many great things, that he might obtain mercy, that is, healing and escape from the punishments of the divine judgment. [[9:14|And the city|Et civitatem]] of Jerusalem, which a little before he meant to make [[9:14|a common burying place|sepulcrum congestorum]] (that is, of the Jews slain and heaped up together), [[9:14|he now desireth to make free|optat reddere liberam]] from tribute; [[9:15|And the Jews|ac Judæos]] [[9:15|he now promiseth to make equal|æquales]] in privileges [[9:15|with the Athenians|Atheniensibus facere pollicetur]]. For the Athenians were privileged and made free in many things, because the study of philosophy flourished there.

paras.t: Et desperans de sua curatione: nam sensit dolores suos augeri assidue; scripsit Judæis, in quos scivit se gravius excessisse: Optimis civibus Judæis plurimam salutem, etc. Si ex sententia cuncta vobis sunt, id est, omnia prospere ad libitum vestrum vobis eveniunt, maximas agimus gratias. Et ego infirmitate gravi apprehensus, non desperans memetipsum. Jam dictum est, quod scripsit desperans de sua curatione. Ideo videtur ista mendaciter loqui, præsertim quum subdat, sed spem multam habens effugiendi infirmitatem. Ex quibus etiam verbis elicitur, quod timore mortis et desiderio corporalis sanitatis, dixit et scripsit atque pœnituit, non amore virtutum.
paras.en: And [[9:18|despairing|Et desperans]] of his cure (for he felt his pains increase continually), [[9:18|he wrote to the Jews|scripsit Judæis]], against whom he knew he had most grievously transgressed: [[9:19|To his very good subjects the Jews|Optimis civibus Judæis]] [[9:19|much health|plurimam salutem]], etc. [[9:20|if all matters go with you to your mind|Si ex sententia cuncta vobis sunt]], that is, if everything turns out prosperously for you at your pleasure, [[9:20|we give very great thanks|maximas agimus gratias]]. And I, [[9:21|being taken with a grievous disease|infirmitate gravi apprehensus]], not [[9:22|distrusting my life|desperans memetipsum]]. It has already been said that he wrote despairing of his cure. So he seems to be speaking falsely here, especially since he adds: [[9:22|but having great hope to escape the sickness|sed spem multam habens effugiendi infirmitatem]]. From these words too it is drawn that he spoke and wrote and repented out of fear of death and desire for bodily health, not out of love of virtue.

paras.t: Respiciens autem, id est ego perpendens, quod pater meus Antiochus Magnus ostendit qui post se susciperet principatum, scilicet quod Seleucus filius ejus senior succederet sibi in regno, ut si quid contrarium accideret aut difficile nuntiaretur, id est, si aliqua ardua et adversa negotia evenirent, scientes hi qui in regionibus erant, id est habitatores regionum ipsius, cui esset rerum summa derelicta, id est gubernatio regni commissa, non turbarentur immoderate, videlicet certi ad quem deberent recurrere in talibus causis. Ad hæc considerans de proximo potentes quosque et vicinos, id est reges aut principes in gyro regni mei habitantes, insidiari temporibus, id est observare quibus temporibus possent regnum meum commodius impugnare, et eventum exspectantes, id est opportunitatem seu effectum, in quo hoc possent implere: quod maxime esset, quando non sciretur quis esse deberet successor meus in regno: ideo designavi Antiochum filium meum regem, id est, institui quod ipse mihi succedat in regno, quem sæpe, recurrens in superiora regna, scilicet Persarum atque Medorum aut aliorum, multis vestrum commendavi. Istud videtur blandum magis quam verum. Et scripsi ad eum quæ subjecta sunt in epistola ei missa.
paras.en: [[9:23|But considering|Respiciens autem]], that is, I weighing, [[9:23|that my father|quod pater meus]] Antiochus the Great [[9:23|appointed who should reign after him|ostendit qui post se susciperet principatum]], namely that Seleucus his elder son should succeed him in the kingdom, so that [[9:24|if any thing contrary to expectation should fall out, or any bad tidings should be brought|ut si quid contrarium accideret aut difficile nuntiaretur]], that is, if any hard and adverse business should arise, [[9:24|they that were in the countries|scientes hi qui in regionibus erant]], that is, the inhabitants of his regions, [[9:24|knowing to whom the whole government was left|cui esset rerum summa derelicta]], that is, to whom the governance of the kingdom was committed, [[9:24|might not be troubled|non turbarentur]] beyond measure, being sure, that is, to whom they should have recourse in such matters. [[9:25|Moreover, considering that neighbouring princes, and borderers|Ad hæc considerans de proximo potentes quosque et vicinos]], that is, the kings or princes dwelling round about my kingdom, [[9:25|wait for opportunities|insidiari temporibus]], that is, watch for the times at which they might attack my kingdom more conveniently, [[9:25|and expect what shall be the event|et eventum exspectantes]], that is, the opportunity or the outcome in which they might accomplish this, which would be above all when it was not known who was to be my successor in the kingdom: therefore [[9:25|I have appointed my son, Antiochus, king|designavi Antiochum filium meum regem]], that is, I have ordained that he shall succeed me in the kingdom, [[9:25|whom I often|quem sæpe]], [[9:25|when I went into the higher provinces|recurrens in superiora regna]], namely those of the Persians and Medes or others, [[9:25|recommended to many of you|multis vestrum commendavi]]. This seems more flattering than true. And [[9:25|I have written to him what I have joined here below|scripsi ad eum quæ subjecta sunt]] in the letter sent to him.

paras.t: Oro itaque vos memores beneficiorum publice et privatim, id est, rogo ut vos ipsi, recordantes beneficiorum quæ vobis exhibui manifeste et in privato (quæ tamen beneficia pauca aut nulla fuisse videntur: nisi forsan ante confirmationem suam in regimine, quando suam occultans malitiam, cunctis se præbuit gratiosum), ut unusquisque vestrum conservet fidem, id est fidelitatem, ad me et ad filium meum. Confido enim eum modeste et humane acturum: quod utique spectat ad regem, ne abutatur magnitudine potestatis, et clementia decoretur. Unde et rex apum caret aculeo. Et sequentem propositum meum, communem vobis fore, id est pium et justum, sicut et ceteris, ne personarum acceptor exsistat.
paras.en: [[9:26|I pray you, therefore|Oro itaque vos]], [[9:26|remembering favours both public and private|memores beneficiorum publice et privatim]]: that is, I ask that you yourselves, remembering the favours which I have shown you openly and in private (though these favours seem to have been few or none, unless perhaps before he was established in his rule, when, hiding his malice, he showed himself gracious to all), [[9:26|you will every man of you continue to be faithful|ut unusquisque vestrum conservet fidem]], that is, keep fidelity, [[9:26|to me and to my son|ad me et ad filium meum]]. [[9:27|For I trust that he will behave with moderation and humanity|Confido enim eum modeste et humane acturum]]: which indeed befits a king, that he should not abuse the greatness of his power, and should be adorned with clemency. Hence the king of the bees, too, has no sting. And [[9:27|following my intentions|sequentem propositum meum]], [[9:27|will be gracious unto you|communem vobis fore]] [Latin *communem*, "common": even-handed towards all], that is, kind and just, as also to the rest, so as not to be a respecter of persons.

paras.t: Igitur homicida et blasphemus, pessime, id est atrocissime, nec ad salutem, percussus a Deo, miserabili obitu vita defunctus est, id est vita privatus. Unde elicitur, quod non vere pœnituit. Transferebat autem corpus ejus de loco illo ad sepulcrum patrum suorum, Philippus collactaneus ejus, id est eodem lacte nutritus: de quo primo libro plenius continetur. Dicitur autem hic, quod Antiochus obiit in montibus. Nihilominus præallegato capitulo legitur decidisse in lectum, videlicet post lapsum de curru, de quo ibi nil legitur. Qui metuens Antiochi filium, ad Ptolemæum Philometorem, regem Ægypti, qui fuit filius Ptolemæi Epiphanis, abiit. Primo tamen venit et occupavit Antiochiam, et præfuit ibi. Filius autem Antiochi adhæsit Lysiæ, et opposuit se Philippo, et eum in Antiochia oppugnavit: quam contra regem tenere non valens, fugit, ut dictum est, in Ægyptum.
paras.en: [[9:28|Thus the murderer and blasphemer|Igitur homicida et blasphemus]], [[9:28|being grievously|pessime]], that is, most cruelly and not unto salvation, [[9:28|struck|percussus]] by God, [[9:28|died a miserable death|miserabili obitu vita defunctus est]], that is, was deprived of life. From this it is drawn that he did not truly repent. [[9:29|But Philip, that was brought up with him|Philippus collactaneus ejus]], that is, nursed with the same milk, [[9:29|carried away his body|Transferebat autem corpus ejus]] from that place to the sepulchre of his fathers: of him more is contained in the first book[[1 Mach 6:14||]][[1 Mach 6:55||]][[1 Mach 6:56||]] [the margin, partly unreadable, seems to give 1 Mach. vi, 14, 55, 56]. Now it is said here that Antiochus died [[9:28|among the mountains|in montibus]]. Nevertheless in the chapter alleged above it is read that he [[1 Mach 6:8|laid himself down upon his bed|decidisse in lectum]], namely after the fall from the chariot, of which nothing is read there. He, [[9:29|out of fear of the son of Antiochus|metuens Antiochi filium]], went [[9:29|to Ptolemee Philometor|ad Ptolemæum Philometorem]], king of Egypt, who was the son of Ptolemee Epiphanes. But first he came and seized Antioch, and ruled there[[1 Mach 6:63||]]. The son of Antiochus, however, held to Lysias, and set himself against Philip, and besieged him in Antioch[[1 Mach 6:63||]]: and not being able to hold it against the king, Philip fled, as has been said, into Egypt.

paras.t: Ex isto docemur capitulo, quam metuenda sint Dei judicia, et quam multa ad veram requirantur contritionem. Quod item plurimi videntur pœnitere in angustiis et extremis, non tamen salubriter: quoniam ex servili timore, non ex dilectione nec zelo justitiæ; nec sincere, quoniam Deum offenderunt, sed propter mala pœnalia et æterna supplicia, quæ sibi imminere verentur. Tempore ergo sanitatis et juventutis est pœnitendum.
paras.en: From this chapter we are taught how much the judgments of God are to be feared, and how many things are required for true contrition. Likewise, that very many seem to repent in straits and at the last, yet not unto salvation: since they do so out of servile fear, not out of love nor zeal for justice; nor sincerely, because they have offended God, but on account of the penal evils and eternal punishments which they fear are hanging over them. Therefore one must repent in the time of health and youth.

10.title: Declaratio capituli decimi: Machabæus autem, et qui cum illo erant
10.title_en: Explanation of the tenth chapter: But Machabeus, and they that were with him

paras.t: Purgatio templi, et varia bella Machabæi, hic describuntur.
paras.en: The cleansing of the temple and the various wars of Machabeus are described here.

paras.t: Machabæus autem, et qui cum illo erant, Domino se protegente, templum et civitatem Jerusalem recepit, id est recuperavit. Aras autem, etc. Ista plenius sunt descripta atque exposita primo libro: idcirco pertranseundum. Et de ignitis lapidibus igne concepto, id est excusso. Dicuntur autem igniti lapides, qui duri et apti sunt, ut ignis excutiatur ex eis.
paras.en: [[10:1|But Machabeus, and they that were with him, by the protection of the Lord|Machabæus autem, et qui cum illo erant, Domino se protegente]], [[10:1|recovered the temple and the city|templum et civitatem Jerusalem recepit]] of Jerusalem, that is, won them back. [[10:2|But he threw down the altars|Aras autem]], etc. These things were more fully described and explained in the first book[[1 Mach 4:36||]]: so we must pass over them. [[10:3|and taking fire out of the fiery stones|Et de ignitis lapidibus igne concepto]], that is, struck out. Those stones are called fiery which are hard and fit for fire to be struck from them.

paras.t: Rogabant Dominum, ne amplius malis talibus inciderent, id est, tam feroces persecutiones et clades a perfidis sustinerent; sed ab ipso mitius corriperentur, et non barbaris et blasphemis hominibus traderentur. Ita et David ait: Melius est mihi incidere in manus Domini (multæ enim miserationes ejus), quam in manus hominum. In libro Judicum filii Israel etiam leguntur Deo offenso dixisse: Redde tu nobis quidquid tibi placet.
paras.en: And [[10:4|they besought the Lord|Rogabant Dominum]], [[10:4|that they might no more fall into such evils|ne amplius malis talibus inciderent]], that is, should suffer such fierce persecutions and slaughters from faithless men; [[10:4|that they might be chastised by him more gently, and not be delivered up to barbarians and blasphemous men|sed ab ipso mitius corriperentur, et non barbaris et blasphemis hominibus traderentur]]. So David too says: [[2 Kings 24:14|it is better that I should fall into the hands of the Lord (for his mercies are many) than into the hands of men|Melius est mihi incidere in manus Domini (multæ enim miserationes ejus), quam in manus hominum]]. In the book of Judges, too, the children of Israel, when God had been offended, are read to have said: [[Judg 10:15|do thou unto us whatsoever pleaseth thee|Redde tu nobis quidquid tibi placet]].

paras.t: Thyrsos, id est baculos seu medios frutices, ex quibus rami hinc inde procedunt ac oriuntur, et ramos præferebant ei, id est, adducebant ad reverentiam Dei, qui prosperavit mundare locum suum, id est, prosperum dedit successum purgandi templum per Judam et suos.
paras.en: *They carried* [[10:7|boughs|Thyrsos]] [*thyrsi*], that is, staves or the middle stems of shrubs, from which branches spring out and grow on either side, [[10:7|and green branches|et ramos]] [[10:7|for him|præferebant ei]], that is, brought them for the honour of God, [[10:7|that had given them good success in cleansing his place|qui prosperavit mundare locum suum]], that is, gave good success in cleansing the temple through Judas and his men.

paras.t: Hic, scilicet filius Antiochi, suscepto regno, constituit super negotia regni Lysiam quemdam. Et Antiochus pater hujus Antiochi constituit super negotia regni in magna parte Philippum, ut libro primo dictum est. Antiochus vero filius præfati Antiochi, a Lysia nutritus, præfecit eum totius regni negotiis.
paras.en: [[10:11|For when he was come to the crown|suscepto regno]] (he, that is, the son of Antiochus), [[10:11|he appointed over the affairs of his realm one Lysias|constituit super negotia regni Lysiam quemdam]]. And Antiochus, the father of this Antiochus, had set Philip over the affairs of the kingdom in great part, as was said in the first book[[1 Mach 6:14||]]. But Antiochus, the son of the aforesaid Antiochus, who had been brought up by Lysias[[1 Mach 6:17||]], put him over the affairs of the whole kingdom.

paras.t: Nam Ptolemæus qui dicebatur, id est cognominatus est, Macer: nam supra facta est mentio de alio Ptolemæo; justi tenax erga Judæos esse constituit, id est, decrevit se juste habere, non tyrannice neque inique, circa Judæos. Condoluit enim eorum miseriis et pressuris, quas ab Antiocho et ejus ministris sustinuerunt. Idcirco non voluit eos injuste gravare. Hinc subditur: et præcipue propter iniquitatem, id est iniquam oppressionem, quæ facta erat in eos; et pacifice cum eis agere voluit. Sed ob hoc accusatus ab amicis, vel suis, vel Antiochi regis: de quo subditur, apud Eupatorem, id est Antiochum Antiochi Nobilis filium; quum frequenter proditor audiret, id est, quum sæpe audiret se proditorem vocari; vel, quum Antiochus Eupator audiret multoties, quod Ptolemæus iste proditor esset, eo quod Cyprum sibi creditam, id est suæ commissam custodiæ a Philometore rege Ægypti, deseruisset, et ad Antiochum Nobilem translatus, id est sponte profectus, et de ejus familia factus, etiam ab eo recessisset, non satisfaciendo ejus crudelitati circa Judæos, veneno vitam finivit: et sic injuste interfectus est, saltem quoad causam Judæos respicientem.
paras.en: [[10:12|For Ptolemee, that was called|Nam Ptolemæus qui dicebatur]], that is, was surnamed, [[10:12|Macer|Macer]] (for mention was made above of another Ptolemee[[2 Mach 8:8||]] [the margin's reference is unclear]), [[10:12|was determined to be strictly just to the Jews|justi tenax erga Judæos esse constituit]], that is, resolved to behave justly, not tyrannically or unjustly, towards the Jews. For he grieved with them in their miseries and oppressions, which they had suffered from Antiochus and his ministers. Therefore he would not burden them unjustly. Hence it follows: [[10:12|and especially by reason of the wrong|et præcipue propter iniquitatem]], that is, the unjust oppression, [[10:12|that had been done them|quæ facta erat in eos]]; and he wished to deal peaceably with them. [[10:13|But being accused for this|Sed ob hoc accusatus]] [[10:13|by his friends|ab amicis]], either his own or King Antiochus's, of whom it follows, [[10:13|to Eupator|apud Eupatorem]], that is, Antiochus the son of Antiochus the Illustrious; [[10:13|and being oftentimes called traitor|quum frequenter proditor audiret]], that is, since he often heard himself called a traitor; or, since Antiochus Eupator often heard that this Ptolemee was a traitor, [[10:13|because he had left Cyprus|eo quod Cyprum]], [[10:13|which Philometor had committed to him|sibi creditam]], that is, committed to his keeping by Philometor king of Egypt, had deserted it, [[10:13|and coming over to Antiochus the Illustrious|et ad Antiochum Nobilem translatus]], that is, having gone of his own accord and become one of his household, [[10:13|had revolted also from him|etiam ab eo recessisset]], by not satisfying his cruelty towards the Jews, [[10:13|he put an end to his life by poison|veneno vitam finivit]]: and so he was unjustly put to death, at least as to the cause that concerned the Jews.

paras.t: Gorgias autem, quum esset dux locorum, id est princeps aliquarum terrarum vel urbium circa Judæam, assumptis advenis, id est extraneis ad ejus auxilium confluentibus, frequenter Judæos debellabat quosdam, videlicet quos hinc inde improvise invasit. Judæi vero qui tenebant opportunas munitiones, id est congrua fortalitia in Judæa, fugatos ab Jerosolymis gentiles, id est a Juda aut suis inde expulsos, suscipiebant ad pugnandum adversus eos. Hi vero qui erant cum Machabæo, multa vi insistentes, id est valde fortiter obsistentes, loca obtinuerunt, id est, fortalitia Idumæorum, quibus præerat Gorgias, expugnaverunt. Machabæus ad eas, quæ amplius perurgebant, pugnas conversus est, id est contra fortiores adversarios, et contra impugnationes acriores personaliter dimicavit: in quo patet strenuitas et audacia ejus.
paras.en: [[10:14|But Gorgias, who was governor of the holds|Gorgias autem, quum esset dux locorum]], that is, the prince of certain lands or cities around Judea, [[10:14|taking with him the strangers|assumptis advenis]], that is, the foreigners who flocked to help him, [[10:14|often fought against the Jews|frequenter Judæos debellabat]], some of them, namely those whom he attacked unawares here and there. [[10:15|And the Jews that occupied the most commodious holds|Judæi vero qui tenebant opportunas munitiones]], that is, fitting strongholds in Judea, [[10:15|received|suscipiebant]] [[10:15|those that were driven out of Jerusalem|fugatos ab Jerosolymis gentiles]], the gentiles [Denis takes these of the gentiles driven out by Judas], that is, those driven out from there by Judas or his men, to fight against them. [[10:16|Then they that were with Machabeus|Hi vero qui erant cum Machabæo]], [[10:17|assaulting them with great force|multa vi insistentes]], that is, resisting very bravely, [[10:17|won the holds|loca obtinuerunt]], that is, they stormed the strongholds of the Idumeans, of which Gorgias was in command. [[10:19|Machabeus|Machabæus]] [[10:19|departed to those expeditions which urged more|ad eas, quæ amplius perurgebant, pugnas conversus est]], that is, he fought in person against the stronger adversaries and the fiercer assaults: in which his vigour and daring are plain.

paras.t: Hi vero qui cum Simone erant, id est Judæi exsistentes cum Simone fratre Machabæi, cupiditate ducti, a quibusdam qui in turribus erant, suasi sunt pecunia; et septuaginta millibus didrachmis acceptis, dimiserunt quosdam, id est, pecuniam acceperunt a quibusdam gentilibus obsessis in turribus, quos permiserunt effugere. Quum autem Machabæo nuntiatum hoc esset, congregatis principibus, id est ducibus sui exercitus, quos sibi substituit, accusavit quod pecunia fratres vendidissent, id est, quod pro pecunia permiserunt fugere multos gentiles, qui postea occiderunt Judæos, sicque illorum evasio fuit occisorum ab eis Judæorum perditio. Hos ergo Judæos proditores factos per acceptionem pecuniæ pro adversariorum evasione, interfecit Judas.
paras.en: [[10:20|Now they that were with Simon|Hi vero qui cum Simone erant]], that is, the Jews who were with Simon, the brother of Machabeus, [[10:20|being led with covetousness, were persuaded for the sake of money by some that were in the towers|cupiditate ducti, a quibusdam qui in turribus erant, suasi sunt pecunia]]; [[10:20|and taking seventy thousand didrachmas, let some of them|et septuaginta millibus didrachmis acceptis, dimiserunt quosdam]], that is, they took money from certain gentiles besieged in the towers, whom they [[10:20|escape|effugere]] [the margin and the Vulgate read *dimiserunt quosdam effugere*; Denis's gloss supplies the verb]. [[10:21|But when it was told Machabeus|Quum autem Machabæo nuntiatum hoc esset]], [[10:21|he assembled the rulers|congregatis principibus]], that is, the captains of his army, whom he had put in his place, [[10:21|and accused those men that they had sold their brethren for money|accusavit quod pecunia fratres vendidissent]], that is, that for money they had let many gentiles escape, who afterwards slew Jews; and so their escape was the ruin of the Jews slain by them. So [[10:22|he put these traitors to death|Hos ergo Judæos proditores factos per acceptionem pecuniæ pro adversariorum evasione, interfecit Judas]], that is, these Jews who had turned traitors by taking money for the escape of their adversaries.

paras.t: Consequenter describitur mira, magna, ac cœlestis victoria Judæis contra Timotheum et suos concessa. At Timotheus, etc., convocato exercitu peregrinæ, id est extraneæ, multitudinis, et congregato equitatu Asiano, id est bellatorum ex Asia, advenit quasi armis Judæam capturus. Machabæus autem et qui cum ipso erant, deprecabantur Dominum, ad altaris crepidinem, id est extremitatem in circuitu, provoluti, ut inimicis eorum esset inimicus, secundum quod impii erant (odit enim omnes qui operantur iniquitatem, et odio sunt Deo impius et impietas), sic ut illos temporaliter refrenaret atque prosterneret, ne diutius populum Dei vexarent, et cultum impedirent divinum. Et post orationem longius de civitate Jerusalem procedentes, ne adversarii intrando Judæam, damna ei inferrent, proximi hostibus effecti, resederunt.
paras.en: Next is described the wonderful, great and heavenly victory granted to the Jews against Timotheus and his men. [[10:24|But Timotheus|At Timotheus]], etc., [[10:24|having called together a multitude of foreign troops|convocato exercitu peregrinæ]] (*foreign*, that is, strange), [[10:24|and assembled horsemen out of Asia|et congregato equitatu Asiano]], that is, of warriors from Asia, [[10:24|came as though he would take Judea by force of arms|advenit quasi armis Judæam capturus]]. [[10:25|But Machabeus, and they that were with him|Machabæus autem et qui cum ipso erant]], [[10:25|prayed to the Lord|deprecabantur Dominum]], [[10:26|lying prostrate|provoluti]] [[10:26|at the foot of the altar|ad altaris crepidinem]], that is, at its edge round about, [[10:26|to be an enemy to their enemies|ut inimicis eorum esset inimicus]], inasmuch as they were wicked (for he hateth [[Ps 5:7|all the workers of iniquity|omnes qui operantur iniquitatem]], and [[Wis 14:9|to God the wicked and his wickedness are hateful|odio sunt Deo impius et impietas]]), so that he would curb them and lay them low in time, lest they should harass the people of God any longer and hinder the divine worship. [[10:27|And so after prayer|Et post orationem]] [[10:27|they went forth further from the city|longius de civitate Jerusalem procedentes]], lest the adversaries should enter Judea and do it harm, [[10:27|and when they were come very near the enemies they rested|proximi hostibus effecti, resederunt]].

paras.t: Primo autem solis ortu, videlicet valde mane, utrique commiserunt pugnam, scilicet Judas cum suo exercitu contra Timotheum ac suos. Isti, scilicet Judas et sui, victoriæ et prosperitatis sponsorem cum virtute Dominum habentes: Dominus enim in Deuteronomio et alibi sæpe, spopondit fidelibus bellatoribus suis triumphum. Itaque cum virtute, id est cum efficacia, vel cum fide et spe habebant Deum triumphi sponsorem, in quo solo sperabant. Illi autem, puta Timotheus ac sui, ducem belli animum habebant, id est, in propria animositate ac robore confidebant. Sed quum vehemens pugna esset, apparuerunt adversariis, scilicet Timotheo et suis, de cœlo missi: nam sancti angeli erant in Judæorum missi subsidium; viri quinque in equis, id est angeli in specie virorum equestrium, Judæis ducatum præstantes. Denique, quæ sequuntur difficultatem non habent. De hoc autem prælio videtur textus loqui primo libro.
paras.en: [[10:28|But as soon as the sun was risen|Primo autem solis ortu]], that is, very early, [[10:28|both sides joined battle|utrique commiserunt pugnam]], namely Judas with his army against Timotheus and his men; [[10:28|the one part|Isti]], namely Judas and his men, [[10:28|having, with their valour, the Lord for a surety of victory, and success|victoriæ et prosperitatis sponsorem cum virtute Dominum habentes]]: for the Lord in Deuteronomy and often elsewhere promised triumph to his faithful warriors[[Deut 28:7||]][[Lev 26:7||]] [the margin gives Deut. xxviii, 1–14, and Lev. xxvi, 7–8]. So *with their valour*, that is, with power, or with faith and hope, they had God as the surety of triumph, in whom alone they hoped. But [[10:28|the other side|Illi autem]], namely Timotheus and his men, [[10:28|making their rage their leader in battle|ducem belli animum habebant]], that is, trusted in their own fierce spirit and strength. [[10:29|But when they were in the heat of the engagement, there appeared to the enemies|Sed quum vehemens pugna esset, apparuerunt adversariis]], namely to Timotheus and his men, sent [[10:29|from heaven|de cœlo]] (for holy angels had been sent to help the Jews), [[10:29|five men upon horses|viri quinque in equis]], that is, angels in the likeness of horsemen, [[10:29|conducting the Jews|Judæis ducatum præstantes]]. What follows has no difficulty. The text seems to speak of this battle in the first book[[1 Mach 5:6||]].

11.title: Declaratio capituli undecimi: Sed parvo post tempore, Lysias procurator regis
11.title_en: Explanation of the eleventh chapter: A short time after this Lysias, the king's lieutenant

paras.t: Mirabilis victoria contra Lysiam data Judæis, hic recitatur.
paras.en: The wonderful victory given to the Jews against Lysias is related here.

paras.t: Sed parvo post gesta in præcedenti capitulo scripta tempore, Lysias, etc., congregatis octoginta millibus, veniebat adversus Judæos, existimans se civitatem Jerusalem captam gentibus habitaculum facturum. Præsumpsit enim se occisurum aut evecturum omnes Judæos in Jerusalem commorantes, et positurum in ea habitatores gentiles, templum vero in pecuniæ quæstum habiturum, ita quod oblationes, decimas, primitias, et sacrificia quæ offerri solebant in templo, converteret in lucra ac commoda regis ac sua; et per singulos annos venale sacerdotium, id est venditurum omni anno pontificatum, etc.
paras.en: [[11:1|A short time after|Sed parvo post tempore]] the things written in the preceding chapter, [[11:1|Lysias|Lysias]], etc., [[11:2|Gathered together fourscore thousand men|congregatis octoginta millibus]], [[11:2|and came against the Jews, thinking to take the city, and make it a habitation of the Gentiles|veniebat adversus Judæos, existimans se civitatem Jerusalem captam gentibus habitaculum facturum]]. For he presumed that he would slay or carry off all the Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, and put gentile inhabitants in it, [[11:3|And to make a gain of the temple|templum vero in pecuniæ quæstum habiturum]], so that he would turn the offerings, tithes, first-fruits and sacrifices that used to be offered in the temple into gains and profits for the king and himself; [[11:3|and to set the high priesthood to sale every year|et per singulos annos venale sacerdotium]], that is, that he would sell the high priesthood every year, etc.

paras.t: Ut autem Machabæus et sui cognoverunt expugnari præsidia, id est fortalitia sua a Lysia, hortatus est Machabæus ferre auxilium fratribus, id est Judæis, qui in præsidiis erant obsessi, et a Lysia impugnabantur. In tempore enim angustiæ comprobatur amicus. Quumque pariter prompto animo procederent versus Lysiam, qui munitionem Bethsuræ obsidebat, apparuit præcedens eos eques armis aureis hastam vibrans, ad ostendendum quod audacter aggrederentur adversarios suos. Fuitque eques ille angelus sanctus, in specie equestris viri apparens. Tunc omnes simul benedixerunt misericordem Dominum, ferocissimas bestias et muros ferreos parati penetrare, id est quæcumque ardua aggredi: estque hyperbole. De isto bello videtur mentio fieri quarto primi libri capitulo. Ibi tamen legitur Lysias congregasse sexaginta millia et equitum quinque millia. Ibi quoque leguntur de ejus exercitu quinque millia corruisse; hic vero undecim millia peditum, equitum vero mille sexcenti. Hæc autem videntur posse concordari, per hoc quod additur ibi: Videns autem Lysias suorum fugam et Judæorum audaciam, abiit Antiochiam, et elegit milites, ut multiplicati, rursus venirent in Judæam. Sicque videtur post redisse cum pluribus, et majorem passus ruinam in suis.
paras.en: [[11:6|But when Machabeus, and they that were with him, understood that the strong holds were besieged|Ut autem Machabæus et sui cognoverunt expugnari præsidia]], that is, their strongholds, by Lysias, Machabeus [[11:7|exhorted|hortatus est]] them [[11:7|to succour their brethren|ferre auxilium fratribus]], that is, the Jews who were besieged in the strongholds and attacked by Lysias. For in the time of distress a friend is proved[[Prov 17:17||]] [the margin's reference is partly unreadable; the saying recalls Prov 17:17]. [[11:8|And when they were going forth together with a willing mind|Quumque pariter prompto animo procederent]] towards Lysias, who was besieging the fortress of Bethsura, [[11:8|there appeared at Jerusalem a horseman going before them|apparuit præcedens eos eques]], [[11:8|with golden armour, shaking a spear|armis aureis hastam vibrans]], to show that they should boldly attack their adversaries. And that horseman was a holy angel, appearing in the likeness of a horseman. [[11:9|Then they all together blessed the merciful Lord|Tunc omnes simul benedixerunt misericordem Dominum]], [[11:9|being ready to break through not only men, but also the fiercest beasts, and walls of iron|ferocissimas bestias et muros ferreos parati penetrare]], that is, to attempt anything however hard: and this is hyperbole. This war seems to be mentioned in the fourth chapter of the first book[[1 Mach 4:28||]]. Yet there we read that Lysias gathered sixty thousand, and five thousand horsemen. There, too, five thousand of his army are read to have fallen; but here eleven thousand footmen, and one thousand six hundred horsemen. But these things seem able to be reconciled by what is added there: [[1 Mach 4:35|And when Lysias saw that his men were put to flight, and how bold the Jews were|Videns autem Lysias suorum fugam et Judæorum audaciam]], [[1 Mach 4:35|he went to Antioch, and chose soldiers, that they might come again into Judea with greater numbers|abiit Antiochiam, et elegit milites, ut multiplicati, rursus venirent in Judæam]]. And so it seems that he came back afterwards with more men, and suffered a greater ruin among his own.

paras.t: Et quia non insensatus, id est usu rationis carens, erat Lysias. Erat tamen insensatus, id est vera et spirituali sapientia destitutus, secundum quod quidam fatentur: Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam. Unde quibusdam deceptis scribit Apostolus: O insensati Galatæ. Secum ipse reputans factam diminutionem, id est, minorationem sui exercitus pensans, et intelligens invictos esse Hebræos, Dei omnipotentis auxilio innitentes, id est eo quod divino subsidio inhærerent ac juvarentur, misit ad eos, etc., pro pace facienda inter se et eos; et regem compulsurum amicum fieri, id est, quod induceret regem prece et suggestione, ad hoc quod reconciliaretur Judæis. Annuit autem Machabæus precibus Lysiæ, et quæcumque Machabæus scripsit Lysiæ, ut ea impetraret a rege in Judæorum favorem, ea rex concessit.
paras.en: [[11:13|And as he was a man of understanding|Et quia non insensatus, id est usu rationis carens, erat Lysias]] [literally 'since Lysias was not senseless'], that is, lacking the use of reason. Yet he was senseless, that is, devoid of true and spiritual wisdom, according to what certain men confess: [[Wis 5:4|We fools esteemed their life madness|Nos insensati, vitam illorum æstimabamus insaniam]]. Whence the Apostle writes to some who had been deceived: [[Gal 3:1|O senseless Galatians|O insensati Galatæ]]. [[11:13|considering with himself the loss he had suffered|Secum ipse reputans factam diminutionem]], that is, weighing the lessening of his army, [[11:13|and perceiving that the Hebrews could not be overcome, because they relied upon the help of the Almighty God|et intelligens invictos esse Hebræos, Dei omnipotentis auxilio innitentes]], that is, because they clung to the divine aid and were helped by it, [[11:13|he sent to them|misit ad eos]], etc., to make peace between himself and them; [[11:14|and that he would persuade the king to be their friend|et regem compulsurum amicum fieri]], that is, that he would bring the king by prayer and suggestion to be reconciled with the Jews. [[11:15|Then Machabeus consented to the request of Lysias|Annuit autem Machabæus precibus Lysiæ]], [[11:15|and whatsoever Machabeus wrote to Lysias|et quæcumque Machabæus scripsit Lysiæ]], that he might obtain it from the king in the Jews' favour, [[11:15|the king allowed of|ea rex concessit]].

paras.t: Deinde in textu ponitur epistola Lysiæ ad Judæos, in qua inter cetera dicitur: Quæcumque regi potuerunt perferri, id est ea quæ poterant Antiocho regi convenienter insinuari ac præsentari ex parte vestra, exposui, id est, declaravi ei per scripta vel nuntium; et quæ res permittebat, concessit, id est, id quod dispositio rerum rationabiliter admisit vobis impendi, rex indulsit. Subditur data litteræ hujus: Anno centesimo quadragesimo octavo: quod intelligitur de annis regni Græcorum; Dioscori mensis, scilicet Junii, in quo sol intrat signum Geminorum, qui Græce vocantur Dioscori. Sed oritur quæstio. Hæc enim epistola scripta est mortuo Antiocho Nobili, qui (ut in primo libro habetur) obiit anno centesimo quadragesimo nono: quomodo ergo scripta est ista epistola anno centesimo quadragesimo octavo? Respondetur, quod iste annus centesimus quadragesimus octavus fuit idem cum illo centesimo quadragesimo nono: sic tamen, quod exordia hujus anni diversimode accipiuntur.
paras.en: Next the text sets down the letter of Lysias to the Jews, in which among other things it says: [[11:18|whatsoever things could be reported to the king|Quæcumque regi potuerunt perferri]], that is, the things on your part that could fittingly be suggested and put before King Antiochus, [[11:18|I have represented to him|exposui]], that is, I have declared to him by writing or by messenger; [[11:18|and he hath granted as much as the matter permitted|et quæ res permittebat, concessit]], that is, what the ordering of things reasonably allowed to be bestowed on you, the king has granted. The date of this letter follows: [[11:21|In the year one hundred and forty-eight|Anno centesimo quadragesimo octavo]], which is understood of the years of the kingdom of the Greeks; [[11:21|of the month of Dioscorus|Dioscori mensis]], namely June, in which the sun enters the sign of the Twins, who in Greek are called the Dioscuri. But a question arises. For this letter was written after the death of Antiochus the Illustrious, who (as is said in the first book) died in the year one hundred and forty-nine[[1 Mach 6:16||]]: how then was this letter written in the year one hundred and forty-eight? The answer is that this hundred and forty-eighth year was the same as that hundred and forty-ninth, but in such a way that the beginnings of this year are reckoned differently.

paras.t: Regis autem epistola, ista continebat: Rex Antiochus Lysiæ fratri salutem. Illustres autem et nobiles, cognatos suos nominant fratres. Unde secundo Regum libro Joab ad Amasam: Salve, inquit, mi frater. Patre nostro inter deos translato, id est ad deorum societatem assumpto et deificato, quia fervens erat in cultu deorum suorum. Sic etenim reges paganorum putabant parentes suos post vitam istam deificari, sicut et nos ponimus viros sanctos in obitu mox angelis sociari. Nos volentes eos, qui sunt in regno nostro, sine tumultu agere, id est pacifice vivere, […] Judæos […] velle tenere suum institutum, id est legem eis a Deo suo […]; ac propterea postulare a nobis concedi sibi legitima sua, id est, dari eis a nobis licentiam observandi legum suarum statuta. Volentes igitur hanc quoque gentem quietam esse, statuentes judicavimus templum restitui illis, etc., id est, dari eis libertatem servandi ritus et observantias legis suæ in templo: quod utique jam recuperaverant et habebant, quando ista epistola edita fuit.
paras.en: [[11:22|But the king's letter contained these words|Regis autem epistola, ista continebat]]: [[11:22|King Antiochus to Lysias, his brother, greeting|Rex Antiochus Lysiæ fratri salutem]]. Illustrious and noble men call their kinsmen brothers. Whence, in the second book of Kings, Joab says to Amasa: [[2 Kings 20:9|God save thee, my brother|Salve, inquit, mi frater]]. [[11:23|Our father being translated amongst the gods|Patre nostro inter deos translato]], that is, taken up into the company of the gods and deified, because he was fervent in the worship of his gods. For so the kings of the pagans thought that their parents were deified after this life, as we too hold that holy men are joined to the angels as soon as they die. [[11:23|we are desirous that they that are in our realm should live quietly|nos volentes eos, qui sunt in regno nostro, sine tumultu agere]], that is, live in peace, […] the Jews […] [[11:24|would keep to their own manner of living|velle tenere suum institutum]], that is, the law [given] them by their God […] [the scan is damaged here; a few words are lost]; [[11:24|and therefore that they request us to allow them to live after their own laws|ac propterea postulare a nobis concedi sibi legitima sua]], that is, that we give them leave to observe the statutes of their laws. [[11:25|Wherefore being desirous that this nation also should be at rest, we have ordained and decreed, that the temple should be restored to them|Volentes igitur hanc quoque gentem quietam esse, statuentes judicavimus templum restitui illis]], etc., that is, that they be given freedom to keep the rites and observances of their law in the temple: which indeed they had already recovered and held when this letter was issued.

paras.t: Ad Judæos autem epistola regis talis erat: Rex Antiochus senatui Judæorum, id est congregationi majorum seu collegio seniorum gubernantium Judaicum populum. Dicitur enim senatus, a senex et natus, quasi natio seniorum: quoniam seniores prudentia et ætate, ad officium præsidentiæ hujus eligebantur. Si valetis, id est, si prospere vobis succedit, sic estis ut volumus: quasi dicat, Diligimus vos, quia bona volumus vobis. Diligere enim, secundum Philosophum, est alicui bonum velle. Adiit, id est accessit, nos Menelaus, dicens, vos velle descendere ad vestros qui sunt apud nos, id est ad Judæos qui in urbibus regni nostri hinc inde morantur. His ergo qui commeant, id est, ad nostra transeunt loca ex loco et populo vestro, usque ad diem tricesimum mensis Xanthici, id est Aprilis, dexteras damus securitatis, id est salvum conductum, ut Judæi inter nos habitantes, utantur cibis et legibus suis, id est cibis eis licitis juxta legem suam, aliisque præceptis propriæ legis; et nemo eorum molestiam patiatur de his quæ per ignorantiam gesta sunt, id est propter præteritas pugnas habitas inter nostros et populum Judæorum, in quibus Judæi putabant se juste moveri; vel propter alia in quibus ex ignorantia contra nostra fecerunt præcepta. Misimus autem et Menelaum, id est, virum istum quem misistis ad nos, remisimus ad vos, qui vos alloquatur, informando vos ore tenus plenius de nostra voluntate. Valete. Hinc dicitur, quod iste Menelaus fuit alter a pessimo Menelao, de quo dictum est supra, et de quo infra continetur. Siquidem iste Menelaus missus videtur a Juda et suis, pro impetranda licentia quod aliqui boni in lege periti, possent invisere Judæos inter gentiles mansionem habentes, ad informandum eos de observantia legis.
paras.en: [[11:27|But the king's letter to the Jews was in this manner|Ad Judæos autem epistola regis talis erat]]: [[11:27|King Antiochus to the senate of the Jews|Rex Antiochus senatui Judæorum]], that is, to the assembly of the elders, or the college of seniors governing the Jewish people. For *senatus* is so called from *senex* [old man] and *natus*, as it were 'a nation of elders' [the second word is unclear in the scan], since the elders, for their prudence and age, were chosen for the office of this presidency. [[11:28|If you are well|Si valetis]], that is, if things go well with you, [[11:28|you are as we desire|sic estis ut volumus]]: as if to say, We love you, because we wish you good things. For to love, according to the Philosopher, is to wish someone good. [[11:29|Menelaus came to us|Adiit nos Menelaus]], that is, approached us, [[11:29|saying that you desired to come down to your countrymen, that are with us|dicens, vos velle descendere ad vestros qui sunt apud nos]], that is, to the Jews who dwell here and there in the cities of our kingdom. So: [[11:30|to all that come and go|His ergo qui commeant]], that is, who pass from your place and people to our places, [[11:30|until the thirtieth day of the month of Xanthicus|usque ad diem tricesimum mensis Xanthici]], that is, of April, [[11:30|We grant, therefore, a safe conduct|dexteras damus securitatis]] [literally 'the right hands of security'], that is, a safe-conduct, [[11:31|That the Jews may use their own kind of meats, and their own laws|ut Judæi utantur cibis et legibus suis]], the Jews living among us, that is, meats lawful to them according to their law, and the other precepts of their own law; [[11:31|and that none of them|et nemo eorum]] [[11:31|be molested for things which have been done by ignorance|molestiam patiatur de his quæ per ignorantiam gesta sunt]], that is, for the past battles fought between our men and the people of the Jews, in which the Jews thought they were justly moved; or for other things in which they acted against our precepts out of ignorance. [[11:32|And we have sent also Menelaus|Misimus autem et Menelaum]], that is, this man whom you sent to us we have sent back to you, [[11:32|to speak to you|qui vos alloquatur]], informing you more fully by word of mouth of our will. [[11:33|Fare ye well|Valete]]. Hence it is said that this Menelaus was another than the most wicked Menelaus of whom it was said above[[2 Mach 4:23||]], and of whom more is told below[[2 Mach 13:3||]]. For this Menelaus seems to have been sent by Judas and his men to obtain leave for some good men learned in the law to visit the Jews dwelling among the gentiles, to instruct them in the observance of the law.

paras.t: Miserunt etiam Romani, id est legati Romanorum constituti in via versus Antiochiam, epistolam ad Judæos, ita se habentem: Quintus Memmius et Titus Manilius legati Romanorum. Magni autem Romani communiter habuerunt nomina duo ac plura. Populo Judæorum salutem. De his, id est, quæ Lysias cognatus regis concessit vobis, et nos concessimus, ut sint rata. Jam enim Romani dominabantur regibus Syriæ et Ægypti ac aliis multis. Ideo auctoritatem habebant confirmandi aut revocandi concessa a regibus illis et eorum principibus. De quibus autem ad regem judicavit referendum, id est de majoribus causis, confestim aliquem nuntium mittite ad nos, insinuando nobis quid postuletis, diligentius inter vos conferentes, quid et qualiter deceat vos postulare, ut decernamus, id est determinemus, sicut expedit vobis. Videtur autem epistola ista Romanorum missa Judæis, antequam Judas misit Romam ad ineundam societatem cum ipsis. Hoc enim fuit, Antiocho et Lysia occisis regnante Demetrio, ut patet primo libro.
paras.en: [[11:34|The Romans also sent them a letter|Miserunt etiam Romani]], that is, the envoys of the Romans, who were on their way towards Antioch, [[11:34|a letter, to this effect|epistolam ad Judæos, ita se habentem]]: [[11:34|Quintus Memmius, and Titus Manilius, ambassadors of the Romans|Quintus Memmius et Titus Manilius legati Romanorum]]. The great Romans commonly had two or more names. [[11:34|to the people of the Jews, greeting|Populo Judæorum salutem]]. [[11:35|Whatsoever Lysias, the king's cousin, hath granted to you, we also have granted|De his, id est, quæ Lysias cognatus regis concessit vobis, et nos concessimus]], that they may stand. For the Romans already ruled over the kings of Syria and Egypt and many others; therefore they had authority to confirm or revoke what was granted by those kings and their princes. [[11:36|But touching such things as he thought should be referred to the king|De quibus autem ad regem judicavit referendum]], that is, the greater matters, [[11:36|send some one forthwith|confestim aliquem nuntium mittite]] to us, putting before us what you ask, [[11:36|after you have diligently conferred among yourselves|diligentius inter vos conferentes]] what and how it befits you to ask, [[11:36|that we may decree|ut decernamus]], that is, determine, [[11:36|as it is convenient for you|sicut expedit vobis]] [the margin gives the Vulgate's *congruit* beside Denis's *expedit*]. This letter of the Romans seems to have been sent to the Jews before Judas sent to Rome to make an alliance with them. For that was after Antiochus and Lysias had been slain, in the reign of Demetrius, as appears in the first book[[1 Mach 8:17||]].

12.title: Expositio capituli duodecimi: His factis pactionibus
12.title_en: Exposition of the twelfth chapter: When these covenants were made

paras.t: Describuntur hic varia bella ac gesta Machabæi.
paras.en: Various wars and deeds of Machabeus are described here.

paras.t: His factis pactionibus, id est confœderationibus pacis inter regem Antiochum ac Judæos, Lysias pergebat ad regem. Judæi autem agriculturæ operam dabant: quod ante propter assidua bella facere non valebant, saltem tam plene. Sed hi qui resederant, id est aliqui ex principibus regis, qui juxta Judæam post Lysiæ recessum manebant, videlicet Timotheus, non ille qui in fine capituli decimi narratur a Judæis occisus, et Apollonius, sed et Hieronymus, et Demophon Superbus: qui ita cognominatus est, forsan ob suæ elationis excessum, quemadmodum rex Romanorum Tarquinius, vocatus est Tarquinius Superbus; et Nicanor Cypriarches, id est princeps Cypri constitutus a rege, non sinebant eos in silentio agere et quiete, id est pacifice, et sine renisione.
paras.en: [[12:1|When these covenants were made|His factis pactionibus]], that is, these alliances of peace between King Antiochus and the Jews, [[12:1|Lysias went to the king|Lysias pergebat ad regem]], [[12:1|and the Jews gave themselves to husbandry|Judæi autem agriculturæ operam dabant]]: which before, because of the constant wars, they had not been able to do, at least so fully. [[12:2|But they that were behind|Sed hi qui resederant]], that is, some of the king's princes, who stayed near Judea after Lysias had gone away, namely [[12:2|Timotheus|Timotheus]], not the one who at the end of the tenth chapter is told to have been slain by the Jews[[2 Mach 10:37||]], [[12:2|and Apollonius|et Apollonius]], [[12:2|also Hieronymus, and Demophon|sed et Hieronymus, et Demophon]] *the Proud* [Denis reads *Superbus*; the margin gives the Vulgate's *super hos*, 'besides these'], who was so surnamed perhaps for the excess of his pride, as the king of the Romans Tarquin was called Tarquin the Proud; [[12:2|and besides them Nicanor, the governor of Cyprus|et Nicanor Cypriarches]], that is, the prince of Cyprus appointed by the king, [[12:2|would not suffer them to live in peace, and to be quiet|non sinebant eos in silentio agere et quiete]], that is, peaceably and without resistance.

paras.t: Joppitæ vero, id est gentiles commorantes in urbe maritima nomine Joppe, tale flagitium perpetraverunt: rogabant deceptorie Judæos, cum quibus habitabant, id est secum morantes in Joppe, ascendere scaphas, id est naviculas, quas paraverant Joppitæ ad recipiendum in eis Judæos, cum uxoribus et filiis Judæorum ipsorum, etc. Secundum commune itaque decretum civitatis Joppensis, et ipsis acquiescentibus, id est, Judæis facientibus sicut communitas illa Joppensis decrevit fallaciter ipsos Judæos rogare, quum in altum processissent, id est longe a littore; ubi et aqua paulatim fit altior, tendens ad quamdam rotunditatem sicut et quælibet gutta, sicut in sphæra mundi probatur; submerserunt Joppitæ non minus ducentos Judæos. Quam fraudulentissimam impiissimamque crudelitatem Judas, etc., tanquam communis patronus populi sui, zelo justitiæ viriliter vindicavit. Et sicut fecit Joppitis pro scelere facti, sic fecit Jamnitis gentilibus pro impia eorum voluntate, qua voluerunt tractare Judæos sibi cohabitantes sicut Joppitæ fecerunt. Innotuit namque Jamnitarum voluntas facinorosa per certa indicia.
paras.en: [[12:3|The men of Joppe|Joppitæ vero]], that is, the gentiles living in the seaside city named Joppe, [[12:3|also were guilty of this kind of wickedness|tale flagitium perpetraverunt]]: [[12:3|they desired the Jews|rogabant deceptorie Judæos]], deceitfully, [[12:3|who dwelt among them|cum quibus habitabant]], that is, who lived with them in Joppe, to go [[12:3|into the boats|ascendere scaphas]], that is, small ships, which the people of Joppe [[12:3|had prepared|paraverant]] to take the Jews in them, [[12:3|with their wives and children|cum uxoribus et filiis]] of those Jews, etc. Then, [[12:4|according to the common decree of the city|Secundum commune itaque decretum civitatis]] of Joppe, [[12:4|when they had consented to|et ipsis acquiescentibus]], that is, the Jews doing as that community of Joppe had deceitfully decreed to ask them, [[12:4|when they were gone forth into the deep|quum in altum processissent]], that is, far from the shore (where the water little by little grows deeper, curving to a certain roundness, as does any drop, as is proved in the sphere of the world), the people of Joppe [[12:4|drowned no fewer than two hundred of them|submerserunt Joppitæ non minus ducentos]] Jews. This most deceitful and impious [[12:5|cruelty|crudelitatem]] [[12:5|Judas|Judas]], etc., as the common patron of his people, manfully avenged with the zeal of justice. And as he did to the people of Joppe for the crime they had done, so he did to the gentiles of Jamnia for their wicked will, with which they wished to treat the Jews living among them as the people of Joppe had done. For the criminal will of the men of Jamnia had become known by sure signs.

paras.t: Inde, scilicet a Jamnia civitate, quum abiissent Judas et sui, commiserunt cum eo, id est, contra eum in via pugnaverunt Arabes, etc., qui victi, a Juda petebant dextras sibi dari, id est pacem concedi, promittentes se pascua daturos, id est prata et pascualia loca Judæis circa se morantibus, et pecora multa habentibus.
paras.en: And [[12:10|when they were now gone from thence|Inde, scilicet a Jamnia civitate, quum abiissent]], namely from the city of Jamnia, Judas and his men, the Arabians [[12:10|set upon them|commiserunt cum eo]], that is, fought against him on the way, etc., who [[12:11|being overcome|victi]], [[12:11|besought Judas for peace|a Juda petebant dextras sibi dari]] [literally 'asked that right hands be given them'], that is, that peace be granted them, [[12:11|promising to give him pastures|promittentes se pascua daturos]], that is, meadows and grazing places, to the Jews who lived round about them and had many flocks.

paras.t: Aggressus est autem Judas cum suis civitatem quamdam firmam, quæ habitabatur a turbis promiscuarum, id est diversarum commixtarumque, gentium. Hi autem qui erant in ea, remissius agebant, non resistendo viriliter, quia in fortitudine sui oppidi confidebant, maledictis lacessentes, id est provocantes, Judam, et loquentes quæ fas non est, Deum Israel blasphemando aut maledicendo: quod scilicet ipsum Judam et suos juvare non posset, quemadmodum Sennacherib fecisse legitur. Quæ verba tam impia atque nefaria sunt, ut Scriptura denotet ea per eorum contraria, ut quum tertio Regum inducitur: Benedixit Naboth Deo et regi. Job quoque primo: Nisi in faciem benedixerit tibi, id est maledixerit. Et item: Benedic Deo, et morere. Machabæus autem invocato magno mundi Principe, Deo majestatis immensæ: de quo et Aristoteles undecimo primæ Philosophiæ: Entia, inquit, nolunt male disponi. Pluralitas principum mala: unus ergo princeps. De quo ait Scriptura: Quem constituit alium super terram? aut quem posuit super orbem quem fabricatus est? Qui sine arietibus, id est bellicis instrumentis sic appellatis, et machinis aliis, temporibus Jesu, id est Josue, præcipitavit Jericho, dejiciendo muros ejus, ut habetur Josue libro. Irruit ferociter muris, et innumerabiles cædes fecit, etc.
paras.en: [[12:13|He also laid siege to a certain strong city|Aggressus est autem Judas cum suis civitatem quamdam firmam]], Judas with his men, [[12:13|and inhabited by multitudes|quæ habitabatur a turbis promiscuarum]], *different*, that is, diverse and mingled, [[12:13|of different nations|gentium]]. [[12:14|But they that were within it|Hi autem qui erant in ea]] [[12:14|behaved in a more negligent manner|remissius agebant]], not resisting manfully, because [[12:14|trusting in the strength|in fortitudine]] of their town, [[12:14|and provoked Judas with railing|maledictis lacessentes]], that is, provoking Judas, [[12:14|and uttering such words as were not to be spoken|et loquentes quæ fas non est]], by blaspheming or cursing the God of Israel, namely saying that he could not help Judas and his men, as Sennacherib is read to have done[[4 Kings 18:35||]][[Is 36:20||]]. These words are so impious and wicked that the Scripture marks them by their contraries, as when in the third book of Kings it is brought in: [[3 Kings 21:13|Naboth hath blasphemed God and the king|Benedixit Naboth Deo et regi]] [literally 'Naboth blessed God and the king']. And Job too, in the first chapter: [[Job 1:11|if he bless thee not to thy face|Nisi in faciem benedixerit tibi]], that is, curse thee. And again: [[Job 2:9|bless God and die|Benedic Deo, et morere]]. [[12:15|But Machabeus calling upon the great Lord of the world|Machabæus autem invocato magno mundi Principe]], the God of immense majesty, of whom even Aristotle says, in the eleventh book of the First Philosophy [that is, the *Metaphysics*]: Beings will not be badly ordered; a plurality of princes is bad: therefore one prince. Of whom the Scripture says: [[Job 34:13|What other hath he appointed over the earth? or whom hath he set over the world which he made?|Quem constituit alium super terram? aut quem posuit super orbem quem fabricatus est?]] [[12:15|who without any rams|Qui sine arietibus]], that is, the instruments of war so called, [[12:15|or engines of war|et machinis]] of other kinds, [[12:15|in the time of Josue|temporibus Jesu]], that is, of Josue, [[12:15|threw down the walls of Jericho|præcipitavit Jericho]], by casting down its walls, as is told in the book of Josue[[Jos 6:20||]], [[12:15|fiercely assaulted the walls|Irruit ferociter muris]], [[12:16|he made an unspeakable slaughter|et innumerabiles cædes fecit]], etc. [the words of this passage are damaged in the scan and are given as in the Vulgate where they quote it]

paras.t: Et venerunt Judas et sui ad eos, qui dicuntur Tubianæi, Judæos: qui secundum Glossam non erant Judæi natione, sed quidam Judæis confœderati, dicti Tubianæi, quasi aliena tuba vocati. Dositheus autem et Sosipater qui erant duces cum Machabæo, id est sub eo: quoniam Judas præfuit toti exercitui, seu parti quam sibi assumpsit; illi vero parti exercitus, ut millenarii aut tribuni. Peremit Judas decem millia viros, a Timotheo in fortalitio quodam relictos. Cognito autem Judæ adventu, Timotheus præmisit mulieres et pueros sibi subjectos, et gentiles, ne a Judæis caperentur, in præsidium, id est fortalitium, quod Carnion dicitur. Erat enim inexpugnabile, id est valde difficulter expugnabile. Verumtamen Judas divina virtute expugnavit, et combussit illud cum exsistentibus in eodem, ut in primo libro legitur, ubi præsidium istud vocatur Carnaim. Quumque cohors Judæ prima apparuisset, id est, prima pars sui exercitus, sive prima ipsius turba seu societas venisset obviam hostibus, timor hostibus incussus est ex præsentia Dei, id est occulta operatione Dei ubique præsentis, populo suo gratiose adstantis. Deus enim invisibiliter corda immutat, perterret, confortat. Vel forte per aliquod signum visibile Deus præsentiam suam ostendit. Et in fugam versi sunt alius ab alio, id est ab invicem fugientes, et unus præ alio evadere nitens; ita ut magis a suis dejicerentur, id est, a se invicem perimerentur: sicut de Madianitis legitur in libro Judicum, quod mutua cæde se truncabant. Timotheus incidit in partes, id est in manum bellatorum qui erant sub ducatu Dosithei et Sosipatris.
paras.en: And Judas and his men [[12:17|came|venerunt]] [the first word is damaged in the scan] [[12:17|to the Jews that are called Tubianites|ad eos, qui dicuntur Tubianæi, Judæos]]; who, according to the Gloss, were not Jews by nation, but certain men allied to the Jews, called Tubianites as though 'called by another's trumpet' [*tuba*, 'trumpet']. [[12:19|But Dositheus, and Sosipater, who were captains with Machabeus|Dositheus autem et Sosipater qui erant duces cum Machabæo]], that is, under him: for Judas commanded the whole army, or the part he took for himself, and they a part of the army, as captains of thousands or tribunes. Judas [[12:19|slew|Peremit]] [[12:19|ten thousand men|decem millia viros]], [[12:19|that were left by Timotheus|a Timotheo]] in a certain stronghold. [[12:21|Now when Timotheus had knowledge of the coming of Judas|Cognito autem Judæ adventu, Timotheus]], [[12:21|he sent the women|præmisit]] [[12:21|the women and children|mulieres et pueros]] subject to him, and the gentiles, lest they be taken by the Jews, [[12:21|into a fortress|in præsidium]], that is, a stronghold, [[12:21|called Carnion|quod Carnion dicitur]]. [[12:21|for it was impregnable|Erat enim inexpugnabile]], that is, very hard to storm. Yet Judas by divine power stormed it, and burned it with those who were in it, as we read in the first book[[1 Mach 5:43||]], where this stronghold is called Carnaim. [[12:22|But when the first band of Judas came in sight|Quumque cohors Judæ prima apparuisset]], that is, the first part of his army, or its first troop or band, had come to meet the enemy, [[12:22|the enemies were struck with fear|timor hostibus incussus est]] [[12:22|by the presence of God|ex præsentia Dei]], that is, by the hidden working of God, who is present everywhere and graciously stands by his people. For God invisibly changes, terrifies and strengthens hearts. Or perhaps God showed his presence by some visible sign. [[12:22|and they were put to flight one from another|Et in fugam versi sunt alius ab alio]], that is, fleeing from one another, each striving to escape before the other, [[12:22|so that they were often thrown down by their own companions|ita ut magis a suis dejicerentur]], that is, slew one another: as is read of the Madianites in the book of Judges, that they cut each other down in mutual slaughter[[Judg 7:22||]]. [[12:24|And Timotheus himself fell into the hands|Timotheus incidit in partes]], that is, into the hands of the warriors who were under the command [[12:24|of Dositheus and Sosipater|Dosithei et Sosipatris]].

paras.t: Post horum fugam et necem movit Judas exercitum ad Ephron civitatem munitam, etc. Est autem historia ista primo libro scripta atque exposita.
paras.en: [[12:27|And after he had put to flight and destroyed these|Post horum fugam et necem]], Judas [[12:27|removed his army to Ephron, a strong city|movit Judas exercitum ad Ephron civitatem munitam]], etc. This history is written and explained in the first book[[1 Mach 5:46||]].

paras.t: Inde ad civitatem Scytharum abierunt Judas ac suus exercitus. Contestantibus autem, etc., id est, Judæis qui inter Scythas illos gentiles manebant, dicentibus Judæ Machabæo quod Scythæ fuissent et essent eis benigni, etiam temporibus infelicitatis, id est adversitatis; Judas et sui admonuerunt Scythas, ut de cetero essent Judæis illis benevoli. Et sic venerunt Jerosolymam die solenni Septimanarum instante, id est festo Pentecostes imminente; quod celebrabatur evolutis septem hebdomadibus, a primo die festivitatis paschalis, prout in Levitico scribitur.
paras.en: [[12:29|From thence they departed to Scythopolis|Inde ad civitatem Scytharum abierunt]], Judas and his army. [[12:30|But the Jews that were among the Scythopolitans testifying|Contestantibus autem]], etc., that is, the Jews who lived among those gentile Scythians telling Judas Machabeus that the Scythians had been and were kind to them, [[12:30|even in the times of their adversity|etiam temporibus infelicitatis]], that is, of adversity, Judas and his men exhorted the Scythians to be well disposed to those Jews thenceforth. And so [[12:31|they came to Jerusalem, the feast of the weeks being at hand|venerunt Jerosolymam die solenni Septimanarum instante]], that is, when the feast of Pentecost was at hand, which was kept when seven weeks had passed from the first day of the paschal feast, as is written in Leviticus[[Lev 23:15||]].

paras.t: Et post Pentecosten abierunt Judas et sui contra Gorgiam. Exivit autem Gorgias contra Judam cum peditibus tribus millibus, et equitibus quadringentis. Quibus congressis, contigit paucos ruere Judæorum: et hoc propter eorum iniquitatem, quæ paulo post subditur. Dositheus vero quidam de Bachinoris, id est de populo gentili sic dicto, Judæis confœderato; vel de Judæis sic appellatis a loco in quo habitabant; et iste Dositheus fuit alius a prædicto; vir fortis, Gorgiam tenebat, etc. Atque ita Gorgias fugit in Maresa, id est in locum sic nuncupatum. At illis qui cum Esdrin erant, id est cum viro principali de parte Gorgiæ, diutius pugnantibus contra Judæos, et fatigatis ipsis, vel Judæis, ut aliqui dicunt: primum tamen magis consonat textui; invocavit Judas Dominum, etc.
paras.en: [[12:32|And after Pentecost they marched against Gorgias|Et post Pentecosten abierunt contra Gorgiam]], Judas and his men. [[12:33|And he came out|Exivit autem]] [[12:33|with three thousand footmen and four hundred horsemen|cum peditibus tribus millibus, et equitibus quadringentis]], Gorgias against Judas. [[12:34|And when they had joined battle, it happened that a few of the Jews were slain|Quibus congressis, contigit paucos ruere Judæorum]]: and this because of their iniquity, which is told a little later. [[12:35|But Dositheus|Dositheus vero]], [[12:35|one of Bacenor's band|quidam de Bachinoris]], that is, of a gentile people so called, allied to the Jews, or of Jews so called from the place in which they lived (and this Dositheus was another than the one spoken of before), [[12:35|a valiant man, took hold of Gorgias|vir fortis, Gorgiam tenebat]], etc. [[12:35|and so Gorgias escaped to Maresa|Atque ita Gorgias fugit in Maresa]], that is, into a place so named. [[12:36|But when they that were with Esdrin|At illis qui cum Esdrin erant]], that is, with a chief man of Gorgias's side, [[12:36|had fought long|diutius pugnantibus]] against the Jews, [[12:36|and were weary|et fatigatis]] themselves (or the Jews, as some say; but the first fits the text better), [[12:36|Judas called upon the Lord|invocavit Judas Dominum]], etc.

paras.t: Et quum septimus dies, scilicet sabbatum, superveniret, secundum consuetudinem legis purificati aqua lustrationis propter contactum mortuorum in præliis, prout in Numeris fuit præceptum, sabbatum egerunt, quiescendo devote in laudibus Dei. Invenerunt autem Judæi qui erant cum Juda, sub tunicis interfectorum Judæorum in bello prætacto, de donariis idolorum, id est aliqua pretiosa idolis dedicata, a quibus lex prohibet Judæos ne talia sibi assumerent, juxta illud Deuteronomii: Non assumes ex eis quidquam. Non inferes quidpiam ex idolo in domum tuam, ne fias anathema, sicut et illud est. Omnibus ergo Judæis ibi præsentibus, manifestum factum est ob hanc causam eos corruisse; et rogaverunt Dominum ut id quod factum fuerat delictum, oblivioni traderetur, id est, pie ignosceretur.
paras.en: And [[12:38|when the seventh day came|Et quum septimus dies, scilicet sabbatum, superveniret]] (namely the sabbath), [[12:38|they purified themselves according to the custom|secundum consuetudinem legis purificati]] of the law, with the water of purification, because of their touching the dead in the battles, as was commanded in Numbers[[Num 19:11||]], [[12:38|and kept the sabbath|sabbatum egerunt]], resting devoutly in the praises of God. [[12:40|And they found|Invenerunt autem]], the Jews who were with Judas, [[12:40|under the coats of the slain|sub tunicis interfectorum]] Jews in the battle just mentioned, [[12:40|some of the donaries of the idols|de donariis idolorum]], that is, some precious things dedicated to idols, [[12:40|which the law forbiddeth to the Jews|a quibus lex prohibet Judæos]], that they should not take such things to themselves, according to that of Deuteronomy: [[Deut 7:25|neither shalt thou take to thee any thing thereof|Non assumes ex eis quidquam]]. [[Deut 7:26|Neither shalt thou bring any thing of the idol into thy house, lest thou become an anathema, like it|Non inferes quidpiam ex idolo in domum tuam, ne fias anathema, sicut et illud est]]. So, all the Jews there being present, [[12:40|so that all plainly saw, that for this cause they were slain|manifestum factum est ob hanc causam eos corruisse]]; [[12:42|they besought|rogaverunt]] the Lord [[12:42|that the sin which had been committed might be forgotten|ut id quod factum fuerat delictum, oblivioni traderetur]], that is, be mercifully forgiven.

paras.t: At vero fortissimus Judas, qui mente et corpore fuit fortissimus, facta collatione, id est pia distributione facta, [vel] tractatu cum suis habito de agendis pro prædictis occisis, duodecim millia drachmas argenti, id est argenteos nummos, qui drachmæ vocantur. Drachma namque nummus est certæ quantitatis, habens imaginem regis. Talium ergo nummorum duodecim millia misit Jerosolymam, in qua erat locus sacrificiorum, videlicet templum in quo fieri debuit ista oblatio. Ideo sequitur: offerri pro peccatis mortuorum sacrificium, id est, ut pecunia ista offerretur ibi Deo in sacrificium, hoc est ad usus divinos pro remissione peccati illorum, qui donaria idolorum assumpserant sibi, ut dictum est, et pro aliis eorum remittendis peccatis. Speravit autem Judas eos antequam exspiraverunt, de illo suo pœnituisse peccato. Bene et religiose, id est pie atque fideliter, de resurrectione futura et generali cogitans. Nisi enim eos qui ceciderant per mortem corporalem ac temporalem, resurrecturos speraret in die novissimo (sicut sanctus Job, In novissimo, inquit, die de terra surrecturus sum), superfluum videretur et vanum orare pro mortuis, et eadem ratione sacrificium offerre pro ipsis esset inane.
paras.en: [[12:42|But the most valiant Judas|At vero fortissimus Judas]], who was most valiant in mind and body, [[12:43|And making a gathering|facta collatione]], that is, having made a godly collection, or having taken counsel with his men about what should be done for the aforesaid slain, [[12:43|twelve thousand drachms of silver|duodecim millia drachmas argenti]], that is, silver coins, which are called drachms. For the drachm is a coin of fixed weight bearing the king's image. Twelve thousand of such coins, then, he sent [[12:43|to Jerusalem|misit Jerosolymam]], in which was the place of sacrifices, namely the temple, in which this offering was to be made. Therefore it follows: [[12:43|for sacrifice to be offered for the sins of the dead|offerri pro peccatis mortuorum sacrificium]], that is, that this money should be offered there to God in sacrifice, that is, for divine uses, for the remission of the sin of those who had taken the donaries of the idols to themselves, as was said, and for the remitting of their other sins. And Judas hoped that before they died they had repented of that sin of theirs. [[12:43|thinking well and religiously concerning the resurrection|bene et religiose de resurrectione]], that is, piously and faithfully, the future and general resurrection. [[12:44|For if he had not hoped that they that were slain should rise again|nisi enim eos qui ceciderant resurrecturos speraret]], by bodily and temporal death, on the last day (as holy Job says: [[Job 19:25|in the last day I shall rise out of the earth|In novissimo, inquit, die de terra surrecturus sum]]), [[12:44|it would have seemed superfluous and vain to pray for the dead|superfluum videretur et vanum orare pro mortuis]], and for the same reason it would be idle to offer sacrifice for them.

paras.t: Contra hoc argui potest, quoniam istud videtur sonare, ac si animæ non punirentur post vitam hanc, nisi resumptis corporibus. Possetque aliquis dicere, quod quamvis corpora non essent resuscitanda, pium tamen esset pro animarum a corpore separatarum reconciliatione et ereptione a pœnis orare atque sacrificare. Imo multæ fidelium animæ, a pœnis purgatorii liberantur per orationes et hostias ante corporum suscitationem. Et respondendum, quod plena animarum remuneratio absque corporum resuscitatione et glorificatione fieri nequit: ad quod insinuandum, istud satis extense prolatum est.
paras.en: Against this it can be argued that this seems to sound as if souls were not punished after this life except when they have taken their bodies again. And someone could say that even if bodies were not to be raised, it would still be godly to pray and sacrifice for the reconciliation of souls separated from the body and for their deliverance from punishment. Indeed many souls of the faithful are freed from the pains of purgatory through prayers and sacrifices before the raising of their bodies. And the answer must be that the full reward of souls cannot be had without the raising and glorifying of the bodies: and to suggest this, the saying is put rather broadly.

paras.t: Et quia considerabat quod hi qui cum pietate, id est religione fidei cultuque Dei, dormitionem, id est mortem, acceperant, optimam haberent repositam gratiam, id est spem felicitatis æternæ, seu ipsum præmium beatificum eis paratum ac reservatum a Domino: sicut ait Apostolus ad Timotheum, Reposita est mihi corona justitiæ, quam reddet mihi Dominus in die illa justus Judex. Sancta ergo et salubris est cogitatio pro defunctis exorare, eleemosynas facere, sacrificiumque offerre, ut a peccatis solvantur, id est, a pœnis quæ debentur eorum peccatis, liberentur: quæ peccata in contritione, quantum ad culpam, remissa sunt; et nisi in hac vita satisfiat pro ipsis, oportet quod restat post hanc vitam suppleri.
paras.en: [[12:45|And because he considered that they who had fallen asleep with godliness|Et quia considerabat quod hi qui cum pietate … dormitionem … acceperant]], *with godliness*, that is, in the religion of faith and the worship of God, *had fallen asleep*, that is, had died, [[12:45|had great grace laid up for them|optimam haberent repositam gratiam]], that is, the hope of eternal happiness, or the blessed reward itself prepared and kept for them by the Lord: as the Apostle says to Timothy: [[2 Tim 4:8|there is laid up for me a crown of justice which the Lord the just judge will render to me in that day|Reposita est mihi corona justitiæ, quam reddet mihi Dominus in die illa justus Judex]]. [[12:46|It is therefore a holy and wholesome thought to pray for the dead|Sancta ergo et salubris est cogitatio pro defunctis exorare]], to give alms, and to offer sacrifice, [[12:46|that they may be loosed from sins|ut a peccatis solvantur]], that is, may be freed from the pains that are due to their sins: which sins, as to the guilt, were forgiven in contrition; and unless satisfaction is made for them in this life, what remains must be made up after this life.

14.title: Explanatio capituli quartidecimi: Sed post triennii tempus
14.title_en: Explanation of the fourteenth chapter: But after the space of three years

paras.t: Bella Judæ et suorum gesta contra Demetrium filium Seleuci, hic recitantur.
paras.en: The wars waged by Judas and his men against Demetrius, the son of Seleucus, are related here.

paras.t: Sed post triennii tempus a morte Antiochi Nobilis: quod tamen per synecdochen verificatur, quia Antiochus (ut in primo libro dictum est) obiit anno centesimo quadragesimo nono, et Demetrius venit anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo, ut in primo libro invenitur. Verumtamen annus qui ibi centesimus quadragesimus nonus vocatur, in isto libro centesimus quadragesimus octavus supra undecimo capitulo nuncupatur: quod qualiter concordetur, tactum est ibi. Cognovit Judas Demetrium Seleuci filium, etc., tenuisse regiones adversus Antiochum: quia exercitus reliquit Antiochum, et adhæsit Demetrio, qui fuit filius senioris filii Magni Antiochi.
paras.en: [[14:1|But after the space of three years|Sed post triennii tempus]] from the death of Antiochus the Illustrious: which, however, is true by synecdoche [the figure in which a part is put for the whole], since Antiochus (as was said in the first book) died in the year one hundred and forty-nine[[1 Mach 6:16||]], and Demetrius came in the year one hundred and fifty-one, as is found in the first book[[1 Mach 7:1||]]. Yet the year that is there called the hundred and forty-ninth is called in this book, above in the eleventh chapter, the hundred and forty-eighth[[2 Mach 11:21||]]: how this is reconciled was touched on there. [[14:1|Judas, and they that were with him, understood that Demetrius, the son of Seleucus|Cognovit Judas Demetrium Seleuci filium]], etc., [[14:2|had made himself master of the countries against Antiochus|tenuisse regiones adversus Antiochum]]: because the army left Antiochus and joined Demetrius, who was the son of the elder son of Antiochus the Great.

paras.t: Alcimus autem quidam, qui summus sacerdos fuerat ab Antiocho factus: de quo Alcimo multa sunt habita primo libro; sed voluntarie coinquinatus est vitiis gentilitatis, temporibus commixtionis, quando jussit Antiochus ut omnes de regno suo essent populus unus, ut scriptum est primo libro; considerans sibi nullo modo esse salutem, id est optatam prosperitatem, seu corporis sanitatem sub Juda, qui ipsum propter scelera sua fugavit, neque accessum ad altare, Juda præsidente, venit ad Demetrium anno centesimo quinquagesimo. Primo libro legitur, Anno centesimo quinquagesimo primo; sed concordatio est inducta. Offerens ei auream coronam, tanquam de jure regnanti, et palmam, forsitan auream in signum triumphi, et tanquam victori, et thallos qui templi esse videbantur, id est sublata de templo, aut similia thallis templi. Thalli autem dicuntur offertoria vasa, quibus in præcipuis festis utebantur sacerdotes, et instar turrium erant formata. Et ipsa die siluit de causa propter quam venit, ne videretur regi munera dedisse propter proprium commodum.
paras.en: [[14:3|Now one Alcimus, who had been chief priest|Alcimus autem quidam, qui summus sacerdos fuerat]], made so by Antiochus (of this Alcimus much was told in the first book[[1 Mach 7:5||]]), [[14:3|but had wilfully defiled himself|sed voluntarie coinquinatus est]] with the vices of heathendom [[14:3|in the time of mingling|temporibus commixtionis]], when Antiochus commanded that all in his kingdom should be one people, as is written in the first book[[1 Mach 1:43||]]; [[14:3|seeing that there was no safety for him|considerans sibi nullo modo esse salutem]], that is, the prosperity he wished for, or bodily safety, under Judas, who had driven him out for his crimes, [[14:3|nor access to the altar|neque accessum ad altare]] while Judas was in charge, [[14:4|Came to king Demetrius in the year one hundred and fifty|venit ad Demetrium anno centesimo quinquagesimo]]. In the first book we read, In the year one hundred and fifty-one[[1 Mach 7:1||]]; but the reconciling of this has been given. [[14:4|presenting unto him a crown of gold|Offerens ei auream coronam]], as to one reigning by right, [[14:4|and a palm|et palmam]], perhaps of gold, as a sign of triumph and as to a victor, [[14:4|some boughs that seemed to belong to the temple|et thallos qui templi esse videbantur]], that is, taken from the temple, or like the *thalli* of the temple.
